reviews.title: Tragus piercing appoved
reviews.text: Great value for the money.  The buds go right up behind your tragus really blocking any extra sound.  For those of us with a tragus piercing, it does work fine, but my earring starts to ache after maybe 45 minutes.  But it does not slip out even with the tragus stud.  The wire seemed like poorer quality than I was anticipating--thicker and flat rather than thin and roundish like the more current models--but that is more of a style critique than one of functionality.  The headphones have worked well for the few weeks that I have been using it.  If you're looking for something that will stay in your ear and block out all other sound, producing high sound quality, this is a great model to get, especially for the price.

reviews.title: Good sound but not great for using while on the move
reviews.text: I bought these headphones as a cheaper alternative to a more robust pair of wireless headphones, like the pixel buds or airpods. Really, I bought them in late 2019 as a hold out for the pixel buds 2 and the USB C cable on my pixel 3 keeps giving out and I just didn't want to deal with the hassle of wired headphones any longer.  The sound quality is good. As someone who is used to listening on a respectable set of AKG 702s or Sony MDR-7056s they obviously don't stack up, but it's better than I would have thought to achieve for the price point, especially in the width of the soundstage.  My main gripe is the in-ear feel. They encompass your whole ear canal with sweaty, grippy plastic. The bad kind. Like the kind that makes it really hard to talk while wearing them, or when you move you hear a muffled rumpling with every step. I personally can't stand that and would prefer a more open ear f…

Anker makes good, if not great, products and gives you tremendous value for the money. The only reason for the 4 in sound is lack of pulsing base, the battery life is absolutely amazing. Another solid Anker product.

reviews.title: Most AMAZING Customer Service
reviews.text: These came highly recommended through an online newsletter, yet I was sadly disappointed (initially). The earbuds, even after switching out to different sizes, didn't stay in very well. After expressing this concern in a review, Anker's customer service reached out to me inquiring how they could fix the problem. They offered to send me their upgraded headphones at no cost, and informed me (with much pride) that along with engineers they seek out customer voices and opinions to help shape their products. I was absolutely floored with how personable they were, and how adamant they were about ensuring customer satisfaction. This is SO RARE to find these days, but ANKER did a phenomenal job and has earned a lifelong customer for it. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

After trying the troubleshooting without success the seller sent me a new set which are working great. Awesome product, exceptional customer service. Definitely will be a return buyer.

reviews.title: Quality for the price

I typically go about two weeks between case recharges. They sound good, but not studio quality or anything. If you're in an office and want some music in the background they work excellent.  I find that as I move frequently, they often feel like they are going to fall out and I have to continuously reposition them in my ears.  The biggest issue though is that I find these to be incredibly uncomfortable in my ears after an hour or more. I've tried all the different ear pieces on both, and they just get annoying after a period of ti…

reviews.title: Nineteen Bucks - Whaddya Want From Them???
reviews.text: I am not going to lie to you and say these sound as good as my B&Os or even as good as AirPods. Both of those earbud sets are worth what you pay for them in sound and all around quality. That's not necessarily true of other brands in their price range. Read carefully when you start to shop, because a name doesn't mean that much anymore.  So, for sound alone? I wouldn't buy these. The top end is almost painfully bright. Midrange is accurate. Bass is on the weak side of accurate. They're serviceable. But about the same sound quality as those 10 pair for 12 dollar wired sets (which is to say - as good as many many sets that cost 2-5 times as much).  But comfort? These are lovely. My ears are small. These haven't fallen out once.  Set up was easy. They stay connected. Overall experience is positive, and I recommend them.

reviews.title: UPDATED update
reviews.text: March 2022- I contacted the seller to let them know of the issues. Since the product is still under warranty they shipped out a new pair within a week. The product might not be the best ,although I think you get what you pay for in this case. But the seller is amazing and I would definitely work with them again.  I kept them. It's January '22 and left side broken. It whispers sound. Right side normal. Couple months worth of kinda crappy use. Nah .....  I've had them for almost a month and will return them. They're my first try with wireless and I can see the appeal when they work.  Pros: Reasonable cost.  Fairly intuitive functions.  When works, works fine.  Cons: If they're in my purse they cut in and out. So maybe a foot away from me and don't work well.  Battery life isn't that good.  Can't really be heard by other person when on phone call.  So all in all, meh. I liked the experience…

reviews.title: Great ear buds!
reviews.text: I enjoy walking about 3 miles around out neighborhood and listening to books when I do. These ear buds are great for that. Since they do such a good job at cancelling outside noise I sometimes just use one when I'm walking since we have no sidewalks and I want to be able to hear the cars.  There are days I use these for several hours doing Spanish lessons online and listening to books. I have never run out of battery and the case recharges them when I put them away. The quality of the sound it great and not at all tinny or sounding like coming through cheap speakers. I'm so glad I found these and just hope I don't lose them. I've gone through several sets of ear buds (some lost and some just quit working) and these are the best I've found.

I love that I can pause my videos, turn the volume up and down, and skip songs just by pressing the ear buds. They have a long rang I can go from my phone before they dont work. They do a decent job blocking out sound, and the battery lasts a long, one charge will last me all day at work and sometimes out of work for almost the whole week. They don't fall out of my ears, although I do have to twist them in a weird way dor them to fit comfortably and snug. Basically, the ear bugs are facing backwards out of my ears, but that might just be my anatomy vs the bud. Overall, I am really happy with this purchase, and they were a great price!!!

The other, not so much. I really like the look of them, they look like they cost two or threes times as much. I have pretty large flappers, but the ear cups are generous and I can, with periodic adjustment, wear them comfortably for several hours. The only nit, and it is just that, is the tiny grooves cut on the sides are dust collectors as expected from the photos. Bought these for the office. May pick up another pair for the house as well. Overall, nice cans!

reviews.title: Good Quality but Great Customer Service
reviews.text: The headphones were pretty good given the price. I was looking for a standard, comfortable quality cheaper set for airplane rides or relaxing at home and saw this product. It doesn't feel flimsy or cheap quality, but for some reason, mine stopped working in less than a month. I do know I dropped it from my bed to the floor, but that shouldn't have caused the headphones to break entirely (no physical damage as it was maybe a 2 foot drop).  Going to look out for another pair of headphones, maybe a better known brand and hopefully will not have to re-order after that.  Edit: Rachel from oneodio reached out (without me having to even contact them myself) and worked with me to get a replacement sent over. Received it and it's working great like before!

reviews.title: Great value - Punches Above Its Weight
reviews.text: Got the TOZO A1 primarily to use with my Nintendo Switch.  Works great with the Switch…pairs with easily and stays connected, no problem.  Didn’t intend to use for music, but turns out these value-priced buds work fantastic listening to music on my iPhone.  Sure, they’re not as good as Sony WF1000XM4 or Apple AirPods Pro, but for less-than-$20 these easily outperform original Airpods.  Other positives:  USB C charging, a small/pocketable case, and decent battery life.  These are pretty small, but not teensy-tiny…about the same size as Beats Studio Buds (sound a lot like them, too; but doesn’t have nearly as much bass presence as the Beats).  The only negative I have is the “non-standard” size of the included eartip.  It’s about half the size of other buds. The buttons that you would think control that, only skip forward and backward in what you are listening to. But the headphone is soft and comfy. The sound is great (they aren't full ear headphones, so not all outside sounds are going to be blocked), and they are so much more comfortable than earbuds, which NEVER stay in my ears anyway. features: Noise cancelling earbuds – Engineered with the world-class noise cancelling. Bose controllable noise cancellation and full Transparency Mode allow you to eliminate distractions, let your surroundings in, or a little bit of each..Note : If the size of the earbud tips does not match the size of your ear canals or the headset is not worn properly in your ears, you may not obtain the correct sound qualities or call performance. Comfortable wireless earbuds – Three sizes of StayHear Max eartips are included for a secure fit. Crafted from soft silicone, they provide passive noise blocking with total comfort.

Simple touch controls – It’s as easy as tap, swipe, or press. Control your noise cancellation settings, pause, play, and volume right from the side of the earbud itself. Enable it all in the Bose Music app.
Noise-rejecting microphones – Tiny microphones work together to focus on your voice, filtering out surrounding noises for fewer distractions during phone calls.

Long battery life — Listen for up to 6 hours on a single charge. The charging case provides an additional 12 hours and charges via the included USB-C cable or wirelessly with any Qi-certified charging mat (not included).

description: Better sound begins with better silence. So Bose engineered QuietComfort Earbuds with the world-class noise cancelling and high-fidelity audio. Because when you eliminate distractions, music goes up, and so does passion. Baking. Coding. Rock climbing. And every other thing that makes you — you. Our controllable noise cancelling allows you to eliminate distractions as needed, or let in your surroundings with a full Transparency Mode. It sounds — and feels — as if you aren’t wearing earbuds at all. Better still? These truly wireless earbuds also include exclusive Volume-optimized Active EQ for high-fidelity audio that sounds full and balanced at any volume. These comfortable earbuds are easy to wear all day long because every surface that touches your ear is made of soft silicone. Instead of buttons, these true wireless earbuds feature a capacitive touch interface. Tap and press the surface to control your content — just like you would with your phone. And the instant you take a wireless earbud out of your ear, your music, podcast, or video automatically pauses so you don’t miss a second. They’re also IPX-4 rated so sweat, water, and the weather won’t get in the way of your music. Bose QuietComfort Earbuds are compatible with iOS and Android and optimized for Bluetooth 5.1 so you’ll enjoy a strong and reliable wireless signal as long as you’re within 30 feet of your paired device. On a single charge you can expect up to six hours of playback time, and the wireless charging case gives you up to 12 more hours of listening time. For your convenience, the charging case is compatible with any Qi-certified wireless charging mat (not included). Bose QuietComfort Earbuds are available in your choice of Triple Black or Soapstone. Powerful yet compact, you’ll never need to take them off.

So I took them off and put them back in my JUST fully charged case, went back a few hours later to try them again. Considering the 20 hours running time I expected my earbuds to be fine because I'd used them MAYBE 20 minutes. They were dead. What a waste of money. Super disappointed.

The sound quality and direction are great in both headsets.  Some differences which were important to me:  The Good: The Stealth uses USB-C. The Arctis uses micro USB. The Stealth uses a rigid mic boom and swings up out of the way to mute. The Arctis uses a flexible wire boom and has a button (and a red LED indicator when muted) to mute. There is an iOS app which lets you manipulate settings and such. Updating the firmware on my Mac was easy. I experienced only slight connection issues during gameplay compared with the Arctis.  The Bad: The band across the top is quite firm and after a ~2 hour session was uncomfortable. The ear cups press in on my head to a level which caused sharp pain towards the end of a ~2 hour sesson. I wear glasses and these squeeze a little too much. The earcups are removable, and you can make space for glasses by adjusting a notched band but it's still tight. That's why I put them at 4 stars, everything else is top notch. USB-c charging is fantastic and I'm glad companies are finally starting to do this. The battery last about 20 hours and I went for a few gaming sessions between charges. The sound quality is excellent with a rich range. Overall these are a pretty solid choice for PS5.

The feature I really like is that you can amplify and adjust your voice level. I am able to speak normally and still give loud clear instructions over Discord. Pairs easily, I didn't even need to go into my settings. The only flaw I see is that the mic is kinda short. I wish it was half an inch or an inch longer. You mute and unmute yourself by moving your mic up or down. I honestly wished it was a button instead, but it isn't a deal breaker. reviews.title: Great Customer Service
reviews.text: I have purchased two sets of these headphones for my daughter who is 5. The first set was 7 months ago. They fit well, were well made and my enjoyed using them. A few weeks ago I noticed the sound stopped working on one side and shortly thereafter both sides no longer produced sound. I was very disappointed as these were not even a year old. I contacted the company and the customer service I received was amazing. They responded to my email within hours, they tried to troubleshoot the problem and were quick to offer a replacement free of charge. This occurred over a few emails back and forth all within minutes of each other. The new set was mailed out the same day. Every product has the chance for a defect but the customer service was above and beyond my expectations. I will happily purchase from them again.

reviews.title: Useful in quieter environments
reviews.text: I gave this product 4 stars because of durability. Thus far, these have been the longest lasting headphones in my preschool class. I think that these would be a much better buy for personal use for a child at home or riding in a car in a quieter environment. I purchased these because of the volume control. I have to monitor the children when using headphones and have also tried to tape the volume control on the CD player but not all storybook CDs are at the same noise level. Some of the CDs were very hard to hear in a classroom of 22 four and five yr olds. The concept is great but can’t give a better review unless trying them in a more appropriate setting. I would definitely recommend these outside the classroom. They have a noise limit and safely protects little ears from loud noises.

reviews.title: Excellent value for a kid headphone - WORKS FOR THE PLANE
reviews.text: I had bought a pair of JLab kid headphones for my daughter a year or so ago from Wal Mart for about $15 and they were essentially garbage. The combo of a steep rolloff of high frequencies (I'm guessing around 13Khz) and the volume limiter made them impossible to use for any kind of noisy environment like an airplane or even a car.  ...These are a huge upgrade from that AND at a lower price. They have a full frequency response (which allows you to listen at lower volumes due to being able to hear detail) and the 93db volume limit allows for listening in noisy places without risk of hearing damage. They are durable for my 2 & 5 YO. The daisy chain feature is also a great bonus. Now, the overall sound quality isn't going to compare to any serious headphone (obviously) and the background noise isolation could be better but for the $$, it would be tough to find something better.

reviews.title: Excellent sound, frustrating bluetooth and terrible mic
reviews.text: Sound and noise canceling are best-of-breed, if that's all you need: this is a pretty good buy. So if you want to switch from your phone to your computer, you need to explicitly disconnect from the phone, then connect from the computer.  And do the reverse to go back (it'll happily reconnect to your now-sleeping laptop, and will refuse to switch to your phone). reviews.title: Good Noise Cancellation, Some Problems
reviews.text: I've had these for a month using a Pixel 5, transitioning from over-ear headphones, and I mostly like them overall. Their battery is lasting forever, and that case recharges them -- you just have to recharge the case occasionally. The buds fit in, rotate into my earbuds pretty well, they just don't always remember their settings. I wasn't a fan of the constant switch between Ambient Sound and Noise Cancellation, so I changed the left bud to volume control, and the right bud controls play/pause. Still, there are unexpected blips in my earbuds, with no changes otherwise. And the Ambient Sound still pops up occasionally. If you're walking around outside, you can typically hear your footsteps very clearly.

reviews.title: Can't make phone calls - horrible mic - collecting dust
reviews.text: From day 1, whenever I make a call, no one can hear what I'm saying. Instead, they hear a ton of static and a very quiet muffled incoherent voice. Totally useless for communicating. I wish I could return or replace these but now they collect dust in my drawer.

reviews.title: Above average offering, but don't care for the design of them or the gesture controls
reviews.text: This product feels different to me than other Sony stuff I've gotten. It's like they've gone out of their way to make everything feel like cardboard. The packaging was like egg carton, and the earbuds and their charging station are a rough lightweight material in a drab color. The earbuds themselves are customizable, but bulky compared to the competition. I find them hard to get out of the container, hard to hold onto, and hard to wear. The noise cancellation and sound are both above average though. I like the charging light on the container. It communicates with color and flashes what the status of the product is, and isn't bright or hard to locate.  USB-C charging makes the base station charge up nice and fast. It holds the earbuds securely, and doesn't rattle or fall open. It's also a nice pocketable size and shape with no sharp corners, making the whole product especially portable. C…

I was skeptical about this being any different, but I ordered it as a Prime Day deal and I’m so glad I took the chance!  The headphone portion is so cushioned that I could barely feel a thing. They didn’t bother me while laying on my side, with my ear pressed against the pillow, at all. I quickly fell asleep, which is rare for me. The sound was also great and deep. I wouldn’t sleep in them and unfortunately that’s what I bought them for. For travel they would be great, couple hours, something such as this. I wouldn’t “gift” this item, although a great idea and concept, some people just can’t wear this version. I think they offer a version that has the controls on the side. Maybe opt for that one instead.

reviews.title: A blessing for dealing with migraines
reviews.text: While I do use this, with or without sound, as a regular sleep mask, I primarily got it for migraines. Depending on how I feel, I can use it to listen to a book, to white noise or gentle music to help soften the racket from barking dogs, or just as a mask. It's cool on the face, and a bit warm on the ears (which I like, since mine are always cold), and has very soft padding around the eyes so it doesn't cause pressure points. It does sometimes press on my nose in a way that makes me feel slightly stopped up, but I can usually adjust it well enough to minimize that. The little speakers are flat enough that, properly aligned, they don't hurt my very tender ears. I can't speak to the sound quality for music since I mostly either use them for audio books or white noise, but they're fine for that. Once of the best migraine-mitigation products I've ever found!

reviews.title: Pretty decent mask but couple of issues.
reviews.text: Pro's and Con's to be fair.  Pro's - Keeps all the light out! very effective soft and comfortable to wear. strap on back is adjustable and easy to adjust while on head.  Con's - if your wearing it to sleep and the voice yells "powering off" it will wake you up. The ear speakers do not line up with my eyes so the mask is sitting at a weird angle and not comfortable, if I move the speakers up then light is getting in from the bottom, but that just may be the shape of my head.  Overall, the mask is pretty good. Will keep and continue using.

reviews.title: No auto power off.
reviews.text: This unit does not have any form of auto power off when whatever you're listening to finishes. This is an essential battery saving feature as running the battery dry on a daily (nightly in this case) basis will quickly kill it.  The electronic components are also not secured in anyway on the inside and will freely move out of place causing the buttons to not do anything (since they're no longer on the circuit board).  Maybe it's just my face but the nose section also bleeds in light.  I do not recommend this unit on the battery draining/killing issue alone.

reviews.title: Blocks light well, easy to pair and use, very soft
reviews.text: I enjoy going to sleep listening to music, and recently I've started using a sleep mask, so I thought this would be the perfect solution.  The mask is very soft.  it is not a 3D mask where your eye lashes don't touch when you open your eyes. Hard to know that for sure from the listing.  There are thin speakers in the part of the mask that covers your ears.  At first I didn't think this was a big deal, but I woke up in the middle of the night and my ears were a little sore from laying on my side with the speaker pushing on my ear.  Since I didn't need music anymore, I switched to my other mask and went right back to sleep.  I don't mind a 2 mask approach if I can enjoy a little music as I drift off.  I have the volume turned really far down.  The sound quality is pretty good for a $30 sleep mask headphone.  So let's talk tech.  The Bluetooth was easy to pair with my phone.  Volume control…

reviews.title: These are SO COMFORTABLE
reviews.text: This is the second bluetooth sleep mask I have tried.  I LOVE the contoured eye portion.  It is so so so comfortable.  The sound quality is good, and it is very easy to move around the headphone pieces to get them in place.  But the sound cancelling quality isn't great.  I can definitely still hear my husband snore.

reviews.title: Works very well

However, I was able to use it more like a headband and it works well.  I can listen to my audio books or music just fine.  And, if I fall asleep wearing it I am not uncomfortable.

reviews.title: Nice Secondary Sleep Mask for Features
reviews.text: I was as skeptical with the sound quality as the rest of you.  I recently purchase Airpods 2 so my standards were stupidly skewed.  But actually... it's ok.  It's better than you would expect, not great but not too bad.  The earpieces are tucked within the ear mask so you can position it so it rests over your ears as loosely or tightly as you'd like it.  You can set up some white noise and it'll work just fine.  The blackout quality of the mask is very good, blocking out any light when I have it on comfortably on my face.  My primary cheap face mask has a ton of light leak, but this one I would use for sensory depravation or sleeping in the daytime.  One of the features to rate is noise cancelling - it is noise cancelling insomuch as holding a loud pair of speakers next to your ears, drowning out anything softer than it.  There isn't any.  Now why it's my secondary and not my primary.  T…

reviews.title: Sooo Soft!!
reviews.text: Its really soft and comfy. love the lil side pocket that holds usb charging wire, it does bother me at all surprisingly.  Sound good.

reviews.title: Super soft and comfortable
reviews.text: I like that this mask is very soft and comfortable to wear.  It's a little big on me which means light come in from the bottom, but it makes up for that in general comfort.  The strap in the back can be tightened if necessary.  I was able to adjust it so that it doesn't fall off of my face.  The sound quality is about what you'd expect at this price point.  It's a little tinny, but it's fine.  I don't think I will use the sound function much though.  It would be good if you live in a noisy environment to put on some white noise.  Overall, this is a nice eye mask.

reviews.title: Does the job
reviews.text: It's very comfortable and does exactly as intended. Audio quality is there but not the same as ear buds. I'm satisfied with it.

reviews.title: Comfortable but not perfect
reviews.text: This is my third attempt at finding a comfortable mask that has speakers so I can listen to my sleep meditations. This one is comfortable as a mask but for some reason it’s way too big for my face. The speakers are set far behind my ears and I can only hear one of them at a time. When I laid on my side the light came in so I tried pulling them lower and then I heard zero audio. The designers of these devices need to actually try them. These will join the others in my nightstand unfortunately as I continue to keep looking.

reviews.title: Not for smaller heads
reviews.text: I bought this so I could listen to relaxing music for when I sleep.  The idea is great and you can adjust it to fit, however, because my head is smaller in circumference (I guess, never really thought much of that before), the speakers end up behind my ears making it harder to hear without blasting the volume which nullifies why I wanted it.  So I would try and adjust the mask and lose the snug feeling on my head just to get a speaker in a decent area.  Also, if you're a side sleeper, while the mask itself is comfortable, the speakers hurt to lay on and you have to figure out how to adjust them for minimal pain.  I'd cut the speakers out just to have the snugness of the mask itself, but I kind of hate the idea of doing that since I'd still have the main part on the front. Overall, I guess it's great if you have a larger head than I or don't want a snug fit and are a back sleeper.

reviews.title: Soft, Good Sound, not tight enough
reviews.text: I must have a small head, because it is very loose on me, and if i tighten it up enough to be comfortable the velcro pulls my hair. Over all, good quality.

reviews.title: Super comfortable
reviews.text: I don’t normally wear a mask to sleep in. I just wanted it for the headphones. But I’m so glad I got it. Not only is the mask super comfy (it has a pillow ring around the eyes so it doesn’t actually press against your eye lids), but the headphones are so flat you can’t feel them. There’s a short little cord that attaches to the charger, but it can be tucked in the areas where the speak is and you can’t feel it. And you can move the speakers around to for your head. This is fantastic.

reviews.title: Love It But NOT Durable

Given that I've been VERY careful not to abuse it, I'm not certain I'm willing to keep buying a new set twice a year. 🤔

reviews.title: Who cares about brand names?!
reviews.text: These are seriously legit headphones. I've tested maybe six similar brand name pairs and these beat them all (because of the price). I can't speak to the longevity of them or the battery life because I've only had them a few days, but they are pretty solid! Sound is fantastic. Fits OVER my average sized ears. The have passive sound canceling just because they cover your ears and it's very effective. The buttons are large and work well with gloves on here in the cold Chicago winter. Pairing is very fast and easy as well. I would say the bass is a bit heavy but that can be adjusted using the EQ on my phone and as of now I haven't found the need to adjust it. Better too much than not enough in my book any way. Don't waste your money on more expensive headphones.

reviews.title: Stereo Bluetooth headsets are way better than they used to be ...
reviews.text: I've only had the August EP650 for a couple days now, and there are a number of quality, comprehensive reviews -- so I thought I would write something specifically from the perspective of someone who hasn't owned a stereo Bluetooth headset since they first came out.  The tech has come a long way, and I'm really quite pleased by how good these are for the price. If you're like me and have a bad recollection of the early days -- with the flaky connectivity and the terrible, tinny sound -- you'll be pleasantly surprised.  Build quality feels pretty decent for the price; comfortable; buttons are easy to find with the headset on, and I've been putting them on while taking public transit, without playing anything, just so I can concentrate on reading, and not the prattle.  So, thumbs up. If you've not been happy with Bluetooth cans in the past and don't want to spend too much to check them out…

reviews.title: Love the ease of use of these lightweight headphones!
reviews.text: I had never used earbuds for anything other than shooting, so didn't know what to expect from these small earbuds on a neck gadget.  THEY'RE GREAT!  The neck piece is very lightweight, so you forget it's there.  I haven't had a low charge message yet, so I just plug it in every few days or so just to be sure.  I use them probably 2-4  hours a day (in this crazy Covid isolation time).  Easy to answer a phone call with a button on the size, easy to lower or raise volumn in the same way.  The retractable cords are plenty long enough (I don't even extend them the entire length), and it comes with one set of extra foam tips (and you can buy bags of those anywhere that sells electronic gadgets). So all in all, I highly recommend these, especially for the great price!

reviews.title: Volume cranks loud enough to hear in an 18 wheeler
reviews.text: So my sister loves these neck band type headsets but she is always breaking them. I took a chance on these for her and this is the verdict. Love the way they fold up. Normal downside to these is the bulky aspect but these fold up nice and fit right in pocket. Sound quality is surprisingly good. The vibration to indicate calls is a nice touch and a lot of higher end models don’t have that. My sister drives a semi truck for work so its pretty loud in truck. Volume is great on these. They also have a nice carry case if you dont want to stick them in your pocket. The ear buds come out nice and smooth and feel like the mechanism is good and tight. Other models will tend to wear out so they dont retract properly after a while. No issues at all pairing with phone. Happy with purchase and would recommend.

reviews.title: Great for sleeping at night and listening to music during workouts
reviews.text: [[VIDEOID:200164e88244479fbc429d9154ede107]] I love these new headband headphones. I wear them outside under my winter hat or even in place of it. I also use them for sleeping and sometimes exercise as well. Having this piece is so helpful since I don’t have to worry about losing my earbuds under my hat or taking off whatever I’m wearing in the cold just to change what I’m listening too. The sound quality and noise cancellation is actually pretty good. The fabric feels good and is comfortable after long period of time. I don’t love the look but its not terrible. My wife likes to use this to go to sleep but it gets pretty hot if you wear it indoors in my opinion. Also good for blocking out your life partner if they snore a lot !  If you found my review or pictures interesting or helpful, please rate it as "helpful." I always enjoy writing reviews of products and try to give honest opinion…

reviews.title: Give this one a skip
reviews.text: Where do I start with this train wreck. I guess, I'll start with the intended purpose. It claims it's good if you have a snoring partner it's so noise cancelling, so I figure, during quarantine, it should be enough to let me hear audio over reasonable outside noise. Other headsets do. This one just looked more comfortable.  The sound level is terrible. On high it sounds like someone whispering from across the room. I kept checking that I had it on right and at one point I took the thing off and pressed the speaker right to my ear. That wasn't much better.  It's ok as a headband, but even for that I wouldn't give it props for comfort. I certainly couldn't use it to exercise, which I thought was one of the key selling points.  Really, don't bother. I'll make do as I have to, but better choices abound.

reviews.title: Can’t Match The Audio Of Full Cup Headphones But Good For The Price
reviews.text: My Bluetooth earbuds kept falling out when I tried to listen to music in bed. And, I certainly didn’t dare fall asleep while using them. I finally decided to get something more secure. This headband style “headphones” does the trick! At this price, the audio certainly doesn’t match the quality of name brand earbuds, but it works well and I will tell you that you get your money’s worth. Audio is a bit muffled and not especially crisp, but for listening to music as I fall asleep I actually found that more quiet and soothing. It takes a bait of adjusting to get the tiny speakers right next to your ears and they did not exactly line up for me, but were close enough. The speakers are tiny enough that I could sleep on the left or right side of my head with comfort. The charging port is hidden in a tiny slit and a little hard to find, but no problem if you know what to look for. These took slig…

reviews.title: First impression - great!
reviews.text: Just got these. they came with the battery 100% charged. I popped them on, easily connected them with my phone, and put on some ambient music just to test them out. They sound great, especially for the price. The headband, despite the product info saying the size is 29 in, is just snug enough not to be headache inducing. I think the 29-in specification is probably a translation issue, and it's probably more like 29 cm, so don't let that stop you from buying. I notice that because they are not particularly snug, if I put my hand over an ear to emulate putting my head on the pillow, the sound becomes much louder. I think I kind of like that you can adjust it in this manner and perhaps when I go to bed I will put another headband over this to secure them a little more tightly so I don't have the sound louder in one ear than in the other. For the price, they are definitely worth a try if you…

reviews.title: Perfect for my needs
reviews.text: This headband is made of excellent quality material that will keep your ears relatively warm in cooler weather.  It was very easy to link it to my phone and computer...just follow the instructions.  I bought it to use while relaxing and meditating and it works perfectly for those purposes.  You can pull it down over your eyes and it blocks out most light sources.  The only downside is that you can hear background noises pretty easily, which is understandable since they don't fit into the ear canal, and the volume on the earpieces is could be a little louder.  Overall, I am very pleased with my purchase.  It suits my needs perfectly.  Thank you.

Also they don't seem to work in all apps (for example it skips me to the next episode in Netflix rather than turning the volume up. User error maybe?) *If you go all the way up to the highest volume it beeps once very loudly, which you don't want if you're using it for a meditation app or sleep music. *There aren't a lot of instructions. I had to look at the pictures on the Amazon listing to figure out how in the world I'm supposed…

reviews.title: Helps Me Fall Sleep & Great Value
reviews.text: This bluetooth headband is an Excellent value for the price.  Easy to connect to any of my devices.  Great bluetooth range.  I need to fall asleep to sound while my partner needs quiet.  These get the job done for both of us.  I can hear it well without him hearing it at all.  I'm able to pull it down over my eyes too, with near blackout to help sleep.  I sleep on my side.  The internal speakers are right near your ear, so it can feel a little awkward at first.  But I quickly figured out how to adjust it and move around the speakers so that I don't feel them.  Not super easy to remove and put back in the electronics for washing, but it can be done.  Overall, would definitely buy again.

reviews.title: Best of the budget earbuds
reviews.text: I'm on my third set of budget earbuds and these are far and away the best ones that I've had. The design allows for them to stay on my ears whether I'm running or doing lifting. The battery life is pretty good, I typically use them for between 60 and 90 minutes at a go and I only charge the case every week to 2 weeks depending. The absolute best thing about these is they don't lose connection when you walk more than 7 ft away or when they're sync to your wrist and you only have the right earbud in. That was a common problem when using my garment on my left hand and running with only the right earbud in and other brands. But this one keeps connection the whole time when I'm running no issues. The sound isn't amazing, but it's still good enough that I would only notice it if I grabbed another much more expensive set of headphones to compare it to. Highly recommend for the price

reviews.title: Two Years and Still Incredible Sound and Comfort
reviews.text: I bought the Bose QC25 headphones in February 2015 and they're still awesome. The noise canceling couldn't be better, the sound quality is impeccable, and they are the MOST comfortable headphones that I have ever had. I use them in the house to listen to my iPod, which sets in a Yamaha dock that is connected to my Yamaha receiver. I also have my TV hooked up to my Yamaha receiver so that I can listen to the TV with the Bose headphones. They get a lot of use, but no abuse. I have not had any problems with the headphones, just the expected maintenance of replacing the pads after two years, but that was easy to do with the Bose replacement pads. From my experience I highly recommend the QC25 phones. Worth every penny!

I only use them for sleeping, though, not for exercising, so I can't say how easy or difficult it would be to remove the speakers and controller to wash the headband part.  Sound is fine. They don't go into your ear like regular earbuds, so you have to turn the volume up a little, but it does what it should. I haven't tried to control the volume using the buttons on the headband so I can't really rate that aspect. All in all, it does what I wanted it to.

reviews.title: I bought the least expensive band I could find, and was amazed at how good it is!
reviews.text: I bought this to use both at night to listen to calming sounds to help me sleep but during workouts. It's great, but the two earphones don't quite go over my ears, my head is small. However, that's no deterrent to me enjoying them. The headband fits well, it's light, and the noise cancellation is pretty good. The sound is really decent too. All in all, this is a great headband for listening to music. It's comfortable enough to wear all day. And the price is right.

reviews.title: Headband, controls, sound quality, charge stats--all exactly what I wanted
reviews.text: This resolved so many issues with other options. The headband is so very comfortable--wish I could buy 5 headbands without speakers just for the comfort for everyday wear.  What I really wanted was comfortable speakers for podcasts as I go to sleep or do tasks or just enjoy! These fit the bill. Volume is perfect. Bluetooth connection is quick and stable. I can do 2 nights before charging again. The buttons work well with podcasts, moving to next or previous episodes. I just ordered a second one.  Thank you and if there is a way to get just the headband, please let me know.

reviews.title: Best headband headphones for sleeping
reviews.text: I got this as a replacement to another headphone headband that had the controls in the wrong spot. I love this band!  I can listen to my kindle books, audiobooks, or television at night to go to sleep without interrupting my husband.

reviews.title: Not comfortable
reviews.text: This thing works well, but it’s not comfortable for laying down. I was hoping to wear it at night while falling asleep but there is no way to get comfortable with it on due to the small speakers inside. I’m not sure how it would work with exercise either because it’s pretty loose and I’d be worried to get sweat on it.

reviews.title: Adequate sound quality but difficult controls.
reviews.text: I use the sleep headphones because I listen to books to get to sleep. I need the volume quite high because I use hearing aids. This headset is adequate for my purpose. It’s very comfortable to wear, but the controls are not very sensitive.

reviews.title: Very Comfortable

Hubby's getting it for Fathers Day.

reviews.title: Excellent product
reviews.text: I LOVE this headband/ headphone unit. It's extremely comfortable to sleep in and blocks out almost all of the noise in my room (snoring dogs, husband's fan). I can use them twice between charges and I'm using them to listen to sleep music that plays for 8 hors at a time.

reviews.title: Sleep headband
reviews.text: I use these to listen to old tv shows that will put me to sleep. I connect to my iPhone and turn on Pride and Prejudice and fall right to sleep. if I wake up and don't go right back to sleep, I restart it. These do the job. I don't care about noise cancellation, since I am the snorer. You have to slip the headphone all the way to the back of the pocket and they will slip forward. The headphones need to stay over your ears or you can't hear from them. I have used them quite a few night now and really like them for my purpose. The "connecting" and "disconnecting" has never been louder than the regular volume. I recharge them every day, but they will last the 8-10 hours that I need them .

Some reviews talked about the headband having to be charged after 8 hours. I only charge mine a couple/few times a week. I do make sure it is off in the morning. Syncing it to my iPhone was super simple. The enclosed directions made it easier than pairing with…

reviews.title: It doesn't turn. on
reviews.text: The JBL Tune 500BT turned on once. Only once, out of the box. After pairing it and using it with a one-year-old 4K Samsung 55" TV for about one hour, we turned it off and charged it. But the red light continuously stays on, indicating that it is continuously charging. (The light is supposed to turn off when fully charged.) We have tried charging it using a 2.4W plug-in to an outlet, for a full 24 hours, and also directly into my iMac for several hours, but the light stays red. After disconnecting it, the light turns off, but the headphones do NOT turn on. We have tried multiple suggested factory resets from You Tube, but none of them, work, because they don't turn on. HELP!!!

reviews.title: Good for calls, music not so much
reviews.text: I am comparing these to Tozo T6. Pros: -Call quality is so much better than T6. Probably because of the location of the mic. -The controls are pretty much the same as T6 & easy to access. -Fit Is decent...right earbud kind of hurt my ear. Could be my ear could be the bud. I can't get T6 to stay in my ears for any significant length of time.  Cons: -No beep or sound when you hang up a call so I always have to look and see if the call ended. -Music quality in my opinion is poor. Between T6 and T9, T6 has noticeably superior sound.  It's not bad for a pair of inexpensive earbuds. They go on sale often for under $30. I am debating whether to return them or not since the call quality is so good. But the music quality just isn't doing it for me. That's the trade off.

reviews.title: Definitely worth the price
reviews.text: For $25 these are awesome.  I needed a pair of workout earbuds.  Sound quality was not a big need as I never know when I'll lose them.  Turns out the structural quality is quite good.  The sound is not fantastic but I do get to enjoy my music while in the gym.  I do need to play with the equalizer settings on my phone to make the sound better.  They seem to be capable of good sound, but I have yet to find that perfect equalizer setting. Still they are convenient and hold a battery charge for many hours.  If I lose the pair I've got I will definitely re-purchase these (if the price is still the same).

reviews.title: Great product, but not for swimming.
reviews.text: I loved the ear buds.  Everything was great, except the water resistant.  It is water resistant, but not good for swimming because when water touches it, it pauses the music.  In addition, when water gets in, the sound is blocked.  After drying out, they are back to normal.  For the price, this is a great purchase.

reviews.title: Amazing value. Great sound quality, and great features.
reviews.text: These are great earbuds - especially for the price. They're comfortable, and the silicone tips do a great job of noise isolation. The touch controls are easy and intuitive. I like the convenience of wireless and USB-C charging, and the stated battery life is 8 hours for music. Also, I found they held up a lot better at the edge of Bluetooth range than others I own.  The charging case is portable - easy to fit into a pocket or purse for sure. But most importantly, the earbuds seat easily and securely in the case, which I've found to be an issue in other similar products I've tried in the past. So no phantom connections or finding the earbuds didn't actually charge.  Overall, I'd definitely recommend these. I actually haven't found anything I dislike about them - which is rare for me.

reviews.text: Bought these to see if I could keep track of wireless earbuds. These are fine to have some music or a podcast at work or doing chores around the house but not to actually REALLY enjoy music. The sound is tinny and weak.  Not devastating as the price was cheap but I did expect  better sound quality than this.

Two major drawbacks are no mate what earbud I put in, they fall out constantly.  I bought headphone wing tips and it solved that proclamation.  Second is the buttons are EXTREMELY sensitive, so any adjusting or brushing of them say moving hair of my hair stops playback.  Otherwise decent battery, no annoying lights once they're connected,  and audio quality is great.

reviews.title: Great earbuds
reviews.text: I absolutely love these Tozo T9 earbuds. However, I have a problem I cannot seem to get solved. I wear them at work so I only use one earbud at a time. I loved my last pair, sony buds that I only replaced because the cord finally gave in after probably 6 or 7 years.  The complaints about putting these in are founded, but honestly, if you spend a little time practising, it's not complicated and you can find easier ways. Sometimes I'll put the cord over the ear first, then fold the bud into the canal. Other time, the opposite. I tug on my lobe with the thumb and ring finger and use my index finger to apply pressure on the body of the plug to seat it in my canal.  I do run with these in. They block a lot of sound, but not everything. I' pretty hyper vigilant about my surrounding when I'm running, so I'm usually very aware anyway. They're also surprisingly uncomfortable because the buds themselves are really thick and the hard plastic is actually jamming itself against my ear (no change in the latex piece helps this problem).  But mostly, they have no low bass (I listen to a lot of electronic music-- they're the worst for psytrance!) and are pretty much only acceptable for listening to podcasts. I lent them to a friend who was surprised that Shure made them because they're so bad.  Not worth the money! When I listen to songs I know, I am disappointed with the sound quality.

Inside that you're immediately presented with the odd looking earbuds and a starter guide (also round) that has you immediately trying them on and fitting the best sleeve size for in your ear. There are no extra sleeves obviously apparent, so time to dig deeper. Next up is the UFO. A large earbud like this needs a large charging case. This one is round and unzips like some of the nicer headphone cases, but it's also a hard case with lights and buttons. Nothing inside but a charging dock. Under it is a secret compartment (made less secret by the thumb holes fo…

reviews.title: Good Experience...But Only After Upgrades

I'd read about these having a high value-to-price ratio and being very comfortable, so I went in with extremely high expectations.  Unfortunately my first impressions of these were that they were awful. As compared with my other pair (an older model from Ultimate Ears) I found it to be incredibly difficult to get a proper seal. The sound felt tinny and washed out. And comfort? Quite the opposite: Pain.  I almost gave up, re-packed them, and send them back. But I decided to invest further. I bought a set of Comply tips and tried those instead of the stock tips. HUGE upgrade! I was able to get a great seal and the comfort level shot way up. reviews.title: 9yo is happy with them, so far so good!
reviews.text: I spent 2 hours trying to find reliable wireless headphones for my 9yo and finally decided on these. I read how important it is to get actual children's headphones because they won't go over a certain decibel (apparently kids are much more susceptible to hearing damage), but some looked too small, or had too many bad reviews, etc.  So far, these are working out well.  Out of the box, I couldn't get her new iPad to recognize them so I emailed customer support and they were very helpful and friendly, and even followed up after to see if their instructions worked.  They did!  So here's a useful tip: just turn off the Wi-Fi on every device in the house first. After I did this, the iPad picked them up immediately.  Then you can turn the Wi-Fi back on the other devices and you shouldn't have to do this again.

reviews.title: Great budget IEM
reviews.text: So I'll ride the hype train on this one. These sound very good. They have excellent clarity. Imaging and separation is good, soundstage is... well fairly small. But for $50 these may be the best I've experienced.  In terms of audiophile quality, these do beat the Tinhifi T2's (also same price range); from the perspective of fidelity of sound. The Tinhifi T2 is a very enjoyable headphone - it is just 'rounded off' and more Harman tuned.  Pros: Clarity and detail are great for this price range. Imaging and separation are good for the price range.  Neutral: Despite me saying these are more true to sound than the T2, these are V shaped. The low end is pronounced/punchy, and the upper end is pronounced. This can be good or bad depending on your taste.  Cons: I am new to the audiophile hobby, so I couldn't point to an exact frequency range, but the treble definitely spikes at one or more frequ…

reviews.title: pretty good
reviews.text: I'll give it a 4 out of 5.  for the price, it's hard to find anything better. pros:  more clarity than I expected.  usually headphones I buy tend to be boomy and muffled.  bass is actually pretty good and not boomy.  doesn't interfere too much with the mids or highs, and it hits pretty hard when needed.  not shrilly either, sounds relatively flat and not V shaped. Not very clinically detailed which makes it work well with all kinds of music and songs.  The voices that go through these things are also very intimate.  cons:  bass doesn't go low low, but I'm comparing it to my $2500 iems.  not as dynamic as high end headphones but for the price its good.  bass isn't as low where you can feel it in your chest (trust me, i've had some iems that convince me i feel the bass shaking my ribcages), but it's powerful.  bass is also surprisingly tight for dynamic drivers.  overall i knew what i was …

reviews.title: Unbelievable! Chi-Fi delivering overtime with these
reviews.text: Best sounding in-ear headphones I've ever heard, by a mile. I've owned the Bang and Olufsen H3, Sony XBA H1, Klipsch S4, X7, X6i, 1More Dual Drivers, Beats by Dr Dre Tour (wired), and Monster Cable's Jamz and Turbines.  The bass has lots of range and goes DEEP, in some tracks it even reminds me of my Kicker CVR 12' car subwoofer I used to blast about 15 years ago. It is not quite that overpowering, of course, and it balances out nicely with the other frequencies. The midrange is very present and natural sounding judging by how vocals and guitar strings sound. The highs are beautiful, they sound very accurate to me and present no sibilance. The overall sound is very rich and detailed, it allows you to follow specific instruments as you listen, and it even presents some soundstage (which I didn't think was possible in in-ears, maybe my aforementioned B&O H3 had some)  Overall these do have…

reviews.title: Best $50 I spent
reviews.text: I'm not a true Audiophile, I still listen to normal music, and have an internal PC sound card, etc...  I did study some audio engineering in a past life, and appreciate good sound.  These are by far the best sounding earbuds (IEM) I've ever heard, and one of the best sounding headphones in general.  It's got really good bass without sacrificing or muddying up the mid / highs.  In terms of sound quality it rivals my HD 660S (which cost 10 times more).  Ranking my gear based on sound quality alone: 1. HD 660S 2. THIS <==== 3. HD 58X 4. AKG Y500 5. Skull Candy Wireless Headphones 6. Bose QuietComfort II (I only use this for flights)  So I hope you can see how much value you're getting in the sound department.  The cable kinda sucks to deal with though, wish they had more traditional popular cables that don't tangle so easily. But I'm willing to deal with it.  Also, OMG!!! Mic works great…

reviews.title: Audiophile quality at a budget price!
reviews.text: I have two issues, and it is not with the IEM's themselves, but the company that sold them. First, the ones I purchased were originally returned. How do I know? Because whoever had them before me had worn them, and left ear wax on the silicone ear pieces. Luckily, they were not the size I wear so I made sure to wash all of the ones that came with the IEM's (included the dirty ones). And second, they went on sale two days after I bought them so I had to send an email to the seller to see if I can get the $10.00 off. UPDATE: 6/8/22 - Got the $10.00 discount!!  Other than those two things, they are excellent IEM's! If you look at the frequency response of these, and realized that they are tuned, they're great for someone in the mid 50's. As you get older, you notice that your hearing loses higher frequencies. Pretty much every frequency above 12kHz are gone. These are tuned perfectly for so…

reviews.title: Bad design
reviews.text: Most of these now a days have the headphone coil around the ear... What I want is just to have the same quality but don't make me spend 5 minutes trying to coil the cord back and not get in my hair. I just want the plug and play GO. The bass is mild on this, however... if you get rid of the coil direction and maneuver it how you want, you can actually get a lot of bass. Problem? You can't move around or the phones pop out of your ears. Remember they really want you to use that ear coil...

reviews.title: Very good for the money.
reviews.text: I grabbed these for quick field recordings with some zoom equipment. I wanted something smaller that wouldn't take up half my case when I was basically just checking to see that things weren't clipping anyway.  I have nothing but good things to say about these. reviews.title: Very practical
reviews.text: The Shokz OpenRun Pro are my first bone conduction headphones and I'm impressed. First things first, audiophiles need not apply. That out of the way, the OpenRun Pro pump enough volume to be useful for walking out an about, and for riding public transit. They do leak sound but it isn't like you're blasting music for everybody around you. People close to you may hear what you're hearing but even then, they really have to be nosy to get most of your audio anyway. Battery life is good - we can always hope for better but this isn't bad. What is bad is the proprietary charging cable with no way to buy spare cables. If that cable breaks, you have to buy the headphones again to get another cable. This is the one reason I cannot give the OpenRun Pro five stars.

features: Gold Standard of Sound: Custom silk-diaphragm drivers accurately reproduce music across a wider frequency range and cut out distortion to deliver sound that’s both Hi-Res Audio and Hi-Res Audio Wireless certified.

reviews.title: The sound is excellent, the features are convenient, but I found it not too comfortable to wear
reviews.text: I really like these headphones at first: the Soundcore app made them easy to configure and update, and in LDAC mode the sound was very very good.  So that was great.  But then I found that I couldn't wear them for long periods, and this might just be me, your mileage will definitely vary.  I wear glasses, and after a while over-the-ear headphones can make my outer ears hurt, and can make them hot.  (I have a pair of gaming headphones that I use for conference calls, that are a bit more comfortable, but even those I can wear for about an hour at most.)  So I'm rating these 4 stars, giving them full credit for sound and convenience, and taking a point off for discomfort, although that might just be a personal thing.

reviews.title: Constantly Turns Off For No Reason
reviews.text: The headphones have a function that automatically stops the playback if you take them off.  I don't see why this is necessary.  Either I have a second to hit stop, or I have way bigger problems than losing my place in a podcast.  It would be an easily ignored function if it worked right.  It doesn't.  Headphones constantly decide they've been taken off for no discernable reason and stop the broadcast.  Really annoying.  Will probably return them.  Don't buy.

I use these SoundCores to watch movies at night when the house is quiet and others are sleeping. They have linked every time to my tv (Samsung w/Amazon Fire-Stick 4K) within seconds of powering them on…they have never dropped a connection. I have only used them for 3 hours at a time…so battery life has not been truly tested yet. I leave them plugged in to charge after each use. I own the SoundPeats TrueAir first version (SPTA1) and have used that so much that the battery life has started to degrade.  At the time, I was going to get another pair but thought I would give the Taotronics Sound Liberty 88 (SL88).  The SL88 sound good but they have issues.  Then SoundPeats came out with the SoundPeats TrueAir 2 (SPTA2).  I immediately purchased a pair, as the SL88s were a bit frustrating.  In this review, I will compare all three.  Co…

One gripe, these buds do not tell you battery life, or when battery is getting low.  You'll notice sound quality will deteriorate and then - nothing.  Many times I'll use the right ear bud only for phone calls. Lately I've noticed the left one is turning off unexpectedly. I return it to the case and then reinsert it and it seems fine.  I've been happy tho with the longevity of the buds and the charging capability of the little case.  The little case- I'm sure I am going to lose it!  And the buds will be useless without it. I'd like to attach it to my phone but then I wouldn't be able to use the phone holder in the car (which I like and use a lot.)  Also, I'm glad it takes a type c USB cord. Hate the type b!

reviews.text: Not sure I've ever been happier with any purchase. First you should know these are semi-in-ear buds, which is to say they don't have a any kind of tip which is inserted into your ear canal. Nor do they site entirely outside and on top of or around your ear. Instead they have a bulbous end shaped to fit the chamber of your ear lobes with a sound opening pointed at your ear canal. Because of this, and the absence of a tight seal created by the silicon or foam tips on in-ear buds, this type of ear bud normally has poor isolation with mediocre sound including weak bass. But this Soundpeats Trueair 2 pair, whether thru deft engineering, or blood sacrifices to strange audio gods, defies this formula. The audio quality is AMAZINGLY good. And the bass, while by no means thumping, is clear and present. These won't replace my best pair of isolating ear buds for serious music listening, but they ar…

reviews.title: Great value
reviews.text: I was made aware of KZ through YouTube reviewer DankPods who highly recommended the KZ ES4 as a great choice for those on a budget. I connect to any Bluetooth device just fine, but it has a very small amount of distance. If I walk into another room to get something it starts cracking up. No problems with other headphones, just these. Fine for sitting at your desk, but there are better ones out there for the same price.

reviews.title: I am an Audible-phile and these are perfect for me
reviews.text: More people are listening to books these days and I am one of them.  I have a Kindle Fire with quite a few Audible books and these headphones work for when I am trying to clean the house and keep up with my book "reading!"  Yesterday I was washing dishes and listening to a great horror book.  That's about the extent of my multi-tasking abilities, but it was nice being able to keep up with a boring task like washing dishes and still be interested by the narrator of the story I was listening to.  I have always had good luck with Sony products and this one is no exception.  A great wireless headphone if you are looking to purchase one.

reviews.title: Fantastic product. No regrets. It does slip off though. Use a clip
reviews.text: This is just about the best pair of Bluetooth headphones for the price. The part of people mentioned about the headphone slipping off from around your neck is true. I saw this issue by using a clip that I had from another pair of headphones. For the price though, the sound quality is pretty good. The bass seems pretty punchy but not overdone. Treble in the audio is clear without sounding tinny. I love these and as long as they continue to be produced at this quality I will keep buying them if I need to.

reviews.title: Keeps disconnecting by itself....grrrrrr!
reviews.text: I bought these in hopes of them being a great headset. I got them and had hardly used them at first. Now I use them often and they just randomly shut off for no reason. No matter what you are doing, watching a movie, listening to music, on a call, ect they will completely shut off and your phone will start blaring whatever your watching or listening to, or a private conversation on the phone will be not so private after that. A real disappointment. They are also waaaay to long. Makes them awkward.  The keep going from side to side. The magnets that are in the ear pieces ARE NOT STRONG. They will not stay together. The music sound quality isn't that good either. I mean its alright, but not anything spectacular.  They do not have noise reduction either. People could still hear everything. And I would often have to speak louder, which can be exhausting. I will be contacting Amazon to get a …

reviews.title: No charging cable included.  So pretty much useless.
reviews.text: Really disappointed it did not come with a charging cable.  And I do not happen to have usb-c cable handy.  Very disappointed.  This makes product useless.

reviews.title: The worst designed headphones I've ever owned. Not functional
reviews.text: This sounds like a silly complaint but the wire between the earbuds is FAR too long. It ruins the headphones for all of my purposes. I have to replace them. Examples -  The wire cannot be worn behind your neck because the controls and microphone then wind up on your back. Instead you have to keep the wire on your chest and look like a nerd. Liveable but annoying.  When working our the longer wire bounces around more which exerts more force on the earbuds. This has a tendency to pull the earbuds out. I was on a treadmill a minute ago and just had to take them off entirely. They kept falling out and required constant adjustment. The earbuds are further designed such that you can't really wrap the wire around your ear for more support. Difficult to explain, you have to see it.  The wire also gets caught on things easily because it's so long.

reviews.title: Battery life is good
reviews.text: This headset is really good. It sounds amazing so I would suggest you try is that if you don’t like them you can send them back but I am pretty sure you’re going to keep them. They are the best. Thank you.

reviews.title: Extremely robust, gets the job done, not for audiophiles,

reviews.title: Great for the price, waterproof
reviews.text: They sound great, and I am moderately picky. These have a nice balanced, sharp, clear and adequately bassy sound.  The other day, I accidentally left one in my pants pocket. It went THROUGH THE WASH..... AND SURVIVED. Still sounds great. Recommend as a good, midgrade earbud.

reviews.title: Great sounding and inexpensive

Not sure if this adds to kinking but they shorted out one side in about a month of use.  Note:  These are used by a HS student.  That said, they rarely leave the house.  If they do, they get placed in the car before school.  They aren't slept in - put in the book bag, or similar.  Typically either in the teenager's ears or on the kitchen counter ore similar surface.  So not sure why th…

reviews.title: Audio quality not as good as I would like. Especially from Sony!
reviews.text: I have had many Sony devices in my life. A Walkman, a Diskman, a stereo system (or 2) and many headphones. All of them have been better than I expected for the price. Not this time. These were pretty poor quality. The battery life is great, they feel nice, they are very comfortable. But the bass is weak, and the treble is a littl hissy. The mid range is flat with no clear definition. Very dissapointing.

reviews.title: Nice Extra Set
reviews.text: I brought these to work so I could look like all the cool kids who wander through the hallways. They are easy to link up to your Bluetooth device. I also paired them to my laptop because watching training videos and whatnot is better with “earphones”. They are the typical comfort level and stay in my ears just fine. I really like the ease of pulling them off & letting them dangle around your neck. The only negative is that the volume module is too high up for me to see. I suppose I’ll get used to that, but for now I have to pull the buds out of my ear to adjust the volume. Guess I’m not a cool kid after all. 4 stars :)

reviews.title: Ok sound.
reviews.text: I wanted to have another pair of earbuds for the gym. Well this are not it. The sound is just OK. Nothing great of it. They have 2 consoles to manage volume, so they are a little heavy. And they don’t have any way to stay put on the ear when doing sport. The pairing with the phone is super easy and fast. I will say these are for just hanging around. By any means these are good for the gym.

reviews.title: Nice headphones and sound quality. A bit heavy while jogging though.
reviews.text: The sound quality of the headphones has good bass. It pairs with my Pixel 3 quite well. Wearing this stationary is something that works from my day to day use. However, when I tried wearing these my jogging or running, it can be fairly uncomfortable. With how your wear these, both sides can feel the weight, where you have the volume adjuster on one side and the other has the charging port.

reviews.title: Nice earbuds
reviews.text: I like these especially for travel.  They can be tossed around back of my neck or in my purse and not get all tangled up.  Very easy to use.  Sound is clear and charges quickly and easily.  The sound isn't great for music but will do instead of large earphone for travel.  I travel frequently and these are my earbuds of choice for flying.

I took a gamble and bought these headphones; they just arrived moments ago!  They came with a variety replaceable ear-tips. For the price, this is a perfect alternative to the expensive Shure earbuds.  *Hopefully I find them!!

I did superglue it back together and it still works but it's something that should not fail. That being said the Shure and Etymotics I had before only last 1/2 the time so I can't complain.

reviews.text: I have the previous version of the Tranya T10 earbuds and still use them for, mainly, at the gym. I decided to buy/try the upgraded T10s before giving them as a gift. The upgraded T10s, much like the previous version, come through with easy device pairing, great sound, and plenty of battery life both in the earbuds as well as the case. The IPX7 rating ensures that any sweat or other moisture (within reason) will not degrade the earbuds. The main differences between the two versions is that the newer version does not support wireless charging and does not have a 'bass mode/boost' (replaced by 'game mode'). Charging the T10s is relatively quick with the USB-C cable and I have power to last several gym trips along with any airplane travel. The sound is balanced in my opinion....plenty of bass despite the lack of 'bass boost' in the previous version. I did find myself using the T10s for seve…

reviews.title: I love, these, but you can't use them with xBox
reviews.text: These headphones are adorable and I love them, but they don't work for the purpose I bought them for. If you're playing alone and don't need the microphone, they're great. Plug the headset into the controller via the aux cord and have fun! But if you want to play on a team, as I do, there's no way to connect the microphone because it doesn't work through the aux cord. It works via Bluetooth and xBox doesn't.  I've read that there's work-arounds for this, like buying a dongle to connect to the xBox to make it Bluetooth compatible or routing the audio through your phone and connecting the headset to that, but that's a certified hassle when I was looking for "OMG cute + plug-and-play."

reviews.title: My kiddo loves it, I’d like better parental volume control
reviews.text: Got these fancy headphones for my kiddo before a trip. The battery life is awesome (if you turn off the flashing lights) and they fit comfortably. My kid loves them.  I really like that they collapse to take up less space and they come with one cord for charging, and an extra cord to plug directly into the device if it does run out of juice.  I have 2 small complaints. Most significantly, it’s really easy for the volume limit control thing to get switched. So I set it at the lowest setting, and my kid is able to turn it off just by messing around with the controls, I’d like the dB limit function to be more secure.  My second, smaller grove is that the charging cable is super short and tight fitting, so of course it’s more difficult for little hands.  Overall I’m happy with the purchase but would seek another option with better sound limit parental controls.

reviews.title: Highly recommend this bluetooth set.
reviews.text: We got this headset for my 4yo daughter to fly from USA to ZA. Sound is great and you can set it to only go up to a certain db, so you know your child isn’t cranking it up and hurting their ears. She loves the cat ears and that they light up. You can put the lights off, I did to save battery (I’m assuming it will) and also not disturb others on the plane. It is easy to pair to bluetooth and has a microphone, she was chatting to my husband on video call and it was very clear. Battery lasts long. All in all a really good purchase that did exactly what I needed it to.

So I have a pretty good idea of how things should sound and these far exceeded my expectations especially at this price.  I really enjoy listening to music such as The Moody Blues on these (good definition and the drums sound fantastic).  Of course you wouldn't use these for professional audio work, but for casual listening they are wonderful.  The headband is great too.  When covid happened I stopped going to the barber.  I've never let my hair grow this long before but decided that I like it this way.  However I have also discovered that long hair can be difficult to manage.  I figured that a headband could help with that an…

reviews.title: Not very loud. Speaker wires aren't long enough to accommodate larger heads.
reviews.text: Little to no noise cancelation.  The speakers are not optimally centered over my ears. I have a normal woman's head. The speakers just barely reach my ears. If I hold the speakers in place,  I can get the volume I need,  but I can't exactly sleep like that! I need to sleep with brown noise to drown out my hillbilly neighbors who gun loud motorcycles in the middle of the night, and play catch football in the street until midnight.  They are truly horrible. I can't really get the volume I need to sleep through the night from this headband.  If I only listened to music during the day, these would be fine. The stretchiness of the band is good and it's neither too tight nor too loose.  The fabric is very soft against my skin. The battery lasts at least 8 hours, but I haven't worn them to the end of battery life.

reviews.title: Wonderful wireless headphones without buds

reviews.title: Don't expect great sound quality
reviews.text: I was unsure about ordering this with the mixed reviews, some saying it has great sound and others saying the sound is not great. When it arrived, I noticed that on the box it says 30mm drivers, so I was hopeful that the sound quality would be good. 30mm drivers are the size that are in my headphones and those rock!  Well, clearly these are not the same as headphone drivers but one can hope.  So, the sound quality is not good at all. These distort on higher volumes, have a very tinny sound and lack any amount of bass one could hope for.  I'm still giving it 4 stars because on low volumes and for sleeping it's totally workable, which is really my main and primary use case for these.  We camp a lot and the sun comes up early so with the ability to cover my eyes will turning on some sounds to drown out the neighbors is very appealing.  They should work fine for my purpose.

reviews.title: Comfy Headband Headphones
reviews.text: This is a nice comfy headband headphone that has decent sound. This is my first headband headphone set so I don't have anything to compare it with, but I am very happy with this. I wanted this for sleeping and it seems like it will work great for that. The headband is comfortable and not too tight, which I like. The material is soft yet thin enough that it won't make your head hot. I was able to pair it easily and I'm not technically inclined. The sound seems fine. I like that you can remove the hardware to wash the headband. I'm going to get a lot of use out of this!

reviews.title: Can’t adjust volume.
reviews.text: First I want to say the fabric of this sleep headband is delightful! Unfortunately that is the only positive thing I can write. Don’t have this on and next to your ears when you power it up because a woman yells in your ear “Power On” and “Connected”.  My ears are ringing and I’m awake now!  But no worries, I’ll just put on some soothing sleep music and fall right asleep…. Nope. There is absolutely no way to turn the volume low. At higher volumes, there is fine control of how quickly you want your hearing damage to happen, but once you get to the halfway point heading downward it is just all the same volume. Also, the +/- buttons don’t control the volume, they advance the track or go back.  Seemed an odd feature for sleep headphones.
