reviews.title: Comfortable and clear reception
reviews.text: Feedback is they can't tell I'm talking on a headset.  I'm on the phone a lot with business and this works perfectly for what I was needing.  I have used several headsets in the past and the overall feedback was the same, "it's not too bad but I can tell you're on a headset" not so with this one.  I went with just the one ear so I could still hear things around me if I needed to.  I highly recommend this headset to anyone who spends a lot of time on the phone, it's comfortable and your ear does not get hot if you wear it for long periods of time

reviews.title: Great headset
reviews.text: These headphones are the most comfortable I have ever owned.  The ear cups sit flat against the ear, which feels more natural than the usual headphone with ear cups that surround your ear with a hot and sweaty dome.  I could only handle that style for a while and then my ears needed a cool off to dry out.  If you are using these headphones somewhere loud, like a train stop, the environment noises will interfere a bit, same if you turn the volume up bystanders will hear it.  But the lack of hot and sweaty ears is such a bonus so these other problems are easily avoided.  The headphones are instantly compatible with all smartphones with a headphone jack.  I used it on a Google Pixel and on iPhone 5's the sound quality was crystal clear, much better than any bluetooth headset I've ever had, and I've had plenty.  The USB adapter with the call controls worked great for my business calls GoToMe…

reviews.title: Beware of webex
reviews.text: So I bought these and immediately tried to use Amazon Music to test out the sound quality. My experience was, the sound would work well for 20-30 seconds then switch to very low quality with no low-end, and flip back and forth between bad and good quality, sometimes never switching back to good. I called Jabra support and they were very helpful, but we didn't come to a root cause.  I sent these back and received a new pair, they did the same thing.  I noticed in the system tray while testing sound, there was a microphone icon that said 'Cisco Webex Meetings is using your microphone'.  Long story short, when Cisco Webex Meetings is using your microphone, it seems to affect the quality of the headphones.  I don't know if this is an issue with the headset or not, but I feel like it's a windows issue caused by Webex.

reviews.title: WASTE OF MONEY
reviews.text: The headset is garbage.  You have to continue to monitor the sound settings so the input doesn't take in the office noise.

reviews.title: Bad Wiring
reviews.text: I had a Jabra headset below that I loved.  Unfortunately, my little guy broke it and I bought this as a replacement.  Definitely easy to plug-and-play, but the wiring is bad and the output changes throughout the call.  At times, sounds like they are in a tunnel, and other times it's very clear.  Wouldn't purchase again as that sound change drives me crazy.

reviews.title: Awesome!!!
reviews.text: Same as everyone-working from home due to COVID and a million and one meetings to go to.  Excellent sound quality and comfort for the price.  I’m not looking to invest in insanely expensive headphones right now (or maybe never) unless I need to.  Excellent product! I’m glad I purchased it.

reviews.title: Works ok, bit tight
reviews.text: Works well for zoom and other video/audio calls on my laptop. Wish it was more comfortable. After 30 minutes on a call my ears are tired.

reviews.title: Good, but needs a lower price.
reviews.text: This is a good headset for using with voice call software. That is the main advertised feature of the headset. I like how clear the microphone is for voice calls. The headphones are good, but they are very low volume. I have to turn the volume up way higher than I normally do for my headphones when I am wearing this headset. The mic is not flexible, so the mic goes right up to your face and I often worry that people will hear me breathing when I wear this. The mic arm swivels either way so you can put the mic on either side of your head.  The headband does not expand very far, so if you have a big head this may be a challenge to fit. The cable for this headphone comes in two parts; there is a 3.5mm part that connects to the controls, and then the USB cable comes out from the controls and can be plugged into any USB port. So you can use this with either a USB or 3.5mm connection. The head…

reviews.title: My machine moves on a daily basis so this is great! These headphones do the job just fine
reviews.text: I recently got a new laptop and, given the mobile nature of this machine, I wanted to set it up so I plug/unplug as few things as possible every time I take it somewhere.  Eventually I decided I was getting sick of plugging and unplugging from the headphone jack.  Okay, it's a first-world problem, but what often happened is I forgot to re-plug in the headphones and would end up making unexpected noise.  So I wanted a pair of USB headphones, the reason being I could just plug them in to the same USB hub that the mouse and keyboard is plugged into.  So now I just have the one plug to attach when I dock my machine.  My machine moves on a daily basis so this is great!  These headphones do the job just fine.  They do NOT require any sort of driver install (tested on Windows 7 and OSX).  Audio quality is better than expected, I suspect because USB provides power.  The little hand-remote is nic…

reviews.title: Excellent Call Quality!
reviews.text: These have spectacular call quality and work fantastic with Teams. I also use them on my phone because they sound better than my phone or earbuds.  I use them daily & they are holding up well. I like that the mic  can be used on either side & tucks away when not in use.  They are fun to use for watching movies too - better than my gaming headphones by MILES for sound quality!  The noise cancelling is amazing. I can talk on this set in the car with the windows down and the other person cannot hear anything but me.  I thought they were pricey, but I'm glad I bought them and will buy them again when these wear out. UPDATE: This company stands behind their product! After months of use, one of the ear pieces came off and a wire came off with it. When I reached out to customer support to see if it was fixable, they let me know my headset was in warranty and are replacing it. I didn't even know…

reviews.title: Excelent Sound
reviews.text: One of the options on this review asked about Noise Cancellation. This model does not have noise cancellation. It does, however, have great sound and a great microphone. The photos of the earpieces looked like they were hard and that worried me. They are a very soft cushioned ring around the ear, so don't be put off from the pictures. The red light comes on when you press the center button on the wired remote, but not automatically. The remote can be removed and used in a normal headphone jack.

reviews.title: Solid and reliable head set for Teams and Web Conferences
reviews.text: The sound and mic quality are very good.  I replaced a long used and abused USB based head set, and this is a good replacement.  I lift and set down my head set probably ten times a day.  I love the feature where the mic folds away as the ear cup rotates to lay flat.  This will definitely extend the life of this head set.  My only complaint is fit.  I have a larger head and the fit is acceptable but slightly awkward.  The ear cups shift during calls, and I sometime have to adjust them.  I decided to keep the headset nonetheless because the few cheaper alternatives I tried did not work very well with respect to sound or mic quality.  I suspect someone with a smaller head won't experience the challenges I have with fit.

reviews.title: Seems inferior
reviews.text: Something from the get go didn’t seem right. Product in a zip lock bag, no box, no instructions and appeared used. Product either a return, open box special or generic. Should have shopped around, paid premium. Very disappointed.

reviews.title: Looks cool, has reliability issue with cord
reviews.text: Someone else posted the wire issue and I have the same problem. The design for tension relief is hard plastic...that becomes a failure point. Also how the wires are routed internally. The design should use a soft plastic. Next don't buy if your head is larger, the design needs at least an additional centimeter. Overall don't recommend paying the price for a fancy looking headset that had design and reliability issues.

reviews.title: After a couple of months no clear audio
reviews.text: Worked only for a couple of months. Really disappointed after reading all the stellar reviews.

reviews.title: Not worth the price.
reviews.text: These are not worth the money. If listening to music, the bass sounds terrible and weak. Comfort wise, these are pretty nice, but make the ears a bit warm. They look better than they are. If you want some good sounding PC headphones for taking calls, listening to music or maybe even PC gaming, check out these. My company used these before we got the Jabra's and I already miss them. Check these out - - - - - >  Plantronics 204446-01 Blackwire C325-M Headset

reviews.title: Great Headset - Only one minor issue
reviews.text: Headset works great. Very clear audio and having an external volume/mute/hangup pad makes things really easy. Saves hunting for the correct window on the screen to mute and unmute making the conversation flow much easier. The only minor complaint is that the headset wire makes a sound in the right earpiece whenever it is moved. It is not an electrical sound but is almost like a stethoscope where every movement of the wire transmits a physical sound in the right headset where it is attached. I am not sure if people on the other end can hear the wire rubbing on my shirt or collar or the desktop, but I sure can.

reviews.title: Hurts ears
reviews.text: Ears hurt after using for about an hour. Sent back.

reviews.text: Wish the microphone extended out further

reviews.title: Won't stay in My ears
reviews.text: I wanted so badly to have these do everything the rave reviews said they would...maybe it's just my funky ears but I could not get a solid seal and I tried every conceivable combo.  I have no idea how anyone could workout with these.  I am sticking with my tried but true Spirit X by Anker.  They have a cord that sits on the back of your neck that I thought was bothersome until I tried these.  Why doesn't one of the wireless head phone companies make the wireless with the wrap around for the ears but without the cord tying them together?

reviews.title: Solid $100 TWS, just not for my use case
reviews.text: INTRO: Been looking for TWS earbuds for a bit now, since I've been tired of having to untangle and fumble with my current IEMs' cable multiple times everyday. They sound good enough for my use of mostly podcasts when I'm on the go and music for when I'm studying, but most importantly they're comfortable and isolate around 7-8/10. I've gotten a $50 budget pair, these, and a $130 pair so far (will have reviews for all of them). Looking for the aforementioned comfort, good isolation, and sound that doesn't noticeably offend.  SOUND: Probably the best out of the bunch, fun punchy bass was all I really noticed on first listen. Didn't care to really sit down and analyze these like I would headphones or IEMs that I use at home. Most wireless earbuds I've tried so far have a background hissing that I really really dislike, but these didn't. To be expected of a company that actually does well for…

I spend the first 15 minutes using these trying to pair and I usually just switch to a different set of headphones. These are a waste of $100. Buy something else that is reliable.

reviews.title: Not A Good Fit For Me
reviews.text: I’ve been using the 1MORE Stylish True Wireless Earbuds for almost 4 months now (July 2019). Based on the video reviews I watched, I really thought I’d like them. Unfortunately my experience has not been the same as most of the reviewers. The volume is not an issue for me. I do not need to blast my music or podcasts. The battery life has been good enough for what I use them for (cutting the lawn, listen to podcasts while the wife watches her programs on TV). The charging case is great when traveling. The big problem I have is w/the fit. I cannot get the earbuds to fit properly & seal correctly in my ears. I have tried all possible combinations of the ear pieces in the box. Because of this, there is no noise cancellation. Besides the mower being heard loudly, I can hear the television when my wife watches it. If I put in my wired Sony earbuds or my Phaiser BHS-730 BT earbuds, I cannot hea…

reviews.title: Finally! Great sounding earbuds that stay put!
reviews.text: I've reviewed more than a few sets of earbuds for Amazon through their Vine program. Some were quite inexpensive, some, not so much. My chief complaint with virtually all of them boils down to FIT. The darn things just don't stay lodged in my ear canals. I've even tried using those pricey memory foam ear tips. Those tips help, but then most buds don't fit in the charging case with them in place.  I just purchased these 1More Stylish earbuds and am really pleased with them. I was attracted to them for their claim that they would fit and stay fit... and they're close to perfect for me. I've not even changed the tips that came with them out of the box and have used them for several hours. Only occasionally do they feel like they will come out and a gentle push re-secures them. Only once did one fall out unexpectedly while I was on a long walk. For me, this is remarkable, almost a world reco…

reviews.title: The clear best buy for audiophile sound quality & battery life
reviews.text: If something approaching audiophile quality sound  is critical (or you primary reason for purchase), the 1More Stylish True Wireless earbuds are a best buy.  You have to spend 3 times the price (for the Sennheiser Momentum True Wireless) to get earbuds that sound as good or better than the 1More Stylish.  Period.  Nothing else on the market even comes close.  Treble is crisp and bright.  Mid range sounds are smooth and rendered with nuance.  Bass is true and tight.  And the 1More Stylish battery life is impressive (and far better than that of the Sennheiser Momentum).  Audio talk quality is also quite good - no noise cancellation - but not quite as good as recognized top performers such as the Apple and Sony.  People on the other end of the conversation have told me my voice comes through clear and undistorted. There are a few things that could stand some improvement, however.  First and…

reviews.title: Green with Crisp Sound
reviews.text: I got these for work. I was using the ear plugs that come with my iPhone and every time I had to stand up and go to the printer or do anything I had to take those ear plugs out. It was frustrating and kind of a bother. So I found these, I bought these for 2 reasons, 1) the price 2) they came in green. So when they arrived I seen there were different sizes in rubber pieces that I could change out to make them fit my ear comfortably. So I did that, and then I charged them for a short amount of time (this was about a week ago). Then I connected them to my phone, which was simple. And I tested them out. They have a crisp sound. When you power them on it also tells you when it’s connected and when you are done you just put them back in the case. The case apparently doubles as a charging station for them too. I have been using mine everyday for a week and they still tell me the battery is high…

reviews.title: So Sad...
reviews.text: These are so cute and sound great...they just did not stay in my ears and I could not get them to fully “fill” my ear as with my AirPods.  I kept trying to push them in further to get a sealed feeling.  I honestly couldn’t believe that a product with no fitting options (AirPods) gave me a better fit than the 1Mores.  And I tried all of the various eartip/o ring combos it came with.  I don’t see how people could exercise with these and them stay in. My son is trying them out right now but sadly...they’re probably going back.

reviews.title: Amazing range.  Good sound quality.  Comfortable.
reviews.text: -I’m not sure if it’s the the BT5.0, but these earphones have better range than my other wireless headphones. -As far as sound quality, I would give it a B.  Now I’m sort of an audiophile, so keep that in mind. -Overall, the best feature is the convenience.  Once you use them, you won’t pick up your other headphones. reviews.title: Revised review
reviews.text: I reviewed this the first week I had the pods. I am still impressed by the quality of the sound, pairing, device, and packaging. I have since used it for phone calls that are being recorded and have opted not to use them for such phone calls in the future. I did not buy it for phone calls, so it's not that important. It's ok for casual calls. My research shows that the quality for phone calls is rarely good. FYI, the sound is tinny and a little static, but intelligible. It works well for books on tape and movies on streaming devices. I did have to play around with ear things to get a fit for each ear. They have popped out once or twice. If it matters I wear a loose scarf/ headband to keep them in place (I do when I'm working out in the garden anyway). I still give to full stars at the price. So much better than anything else I tried.

reviews.title: Great for the price
reviews.text: Overall great value.  I don’t use them to drown out sound, but just enough to help me tune out other sounds around me.  As a sleep mask this item works rather well.  There is some light leakage for me around the nose, but it cuts out the greater portion of light and doesn’t put pressure on the eyes.  Sometimes the padding at the bottom needs adjustment so it’s not pinching my nose.  As a side sleeper, I was surprised that the speakers weren’t more uncomfortable.  It’s usually a few hours of sleeping on one side before they begin to bother my ears.  I typically only get about 5 to 6 hours of sleep a night and that means I often get two nights worth of play time at about 30% volume.  I was actually surprised by the sound quality, I expected it to have a more canned type of sound, but the speakers have a decent range.  The speakers do have to be lined up with your ears in order to hear much…

If it was adjustable that would help a lot. - so figured out that you can, infact, adjust the headphones around so they fit better. Super happy about that. This mask is also very soft. Only one issue though is I still have a small head so getting it to stay on is a little challenging but would recommend

reviews.title: these are fabulous!
reviews.text: A sleep mask with blue tooth speakers is just the most relaxing thing ever. If you have trouble sleeping then this is for you. It is a better way to listen to music, audiobooks, any sleep sounds. The flat speakers are right by your ear but it is not uncomfortable to sleep on your side. The  mask is adjustable and keeps out the light. You can adjust the volume with the controls on the front of the mask which is also where you charge it. It has longer battery life than most ear buds. It is rarely more than half done when I wake up in the morning. I sleep at least 8 hours. This is also helpful for people who get migraines and if you need to shut out other sounds. Perfect if you work nights too.

reviews.title: new and improved
reviews.text: I cannot express enough how much I love these! I like to listed to audiobooks as much as possible and sometimes ear buds hurt after a while or they fall out. This is great to wear around the house or to exercise. It's best feature is the flat speakers. You can sleep with this and be very comfortable, even if you are a side sleeper. Perfect if you like to listen to music or relaxation stuff while you sleep. You an wear it as a head band or to cover your eyes during sleep or a nap. The sound quality is not like that of most earbuds but it is pretty decent. The battery life while in use is at least 10 hours. It only takes an hour or so to recharge. These newer ones have better adjustable bands and it is easy to find where to charge.

reviews.title: Poor design on new version
reviews.text: They’ve redesigned the product. It used to have a usbc charge port directly on the main logic board. This made it easy to find and plug in the dark. Or, more critically, unplug at night. The new design uses a tiny usbc cable that you have to shove back up into eye section of the mask. At night when you’re sleepy and groggy it is frustrating to fish around to find the correct small wire to plug the mask back in.  Also the new version makes a very loud “disconnected!” notification multiple times a night, even while the audio continues playing.  It wouldn’t be so bad if this message wasn’t a thousand times louder than the audio currently playing.  If the designers clearly do not use their own product.

The instructions were less than clear about the initial pairing, but it was straight forward enough to get them paired, and they have had no trouble reconnecting when turning them on.  Unfortunately, these are FAR too quiet when paired with my Pixel 6 pro.  Even the loudest music with the volume set to max is well under what anyone would consider loud, and a vast majority of what I want to listen to when I am wearing these tends toward the more quiet end of things, and often is inaudibly quiet even at max volume.

reviews.title: Pass on these.
reviews.text: This is my third pair of Raycons via their website. I'm writing the review here to preserve the review.   My first pair was their E50s, which I really liked but the left randomly stopped charging. After contacting customer service and confirming all troubleshooting, they gave me a discount on another pair as I was out of warranty. I then got my first pair of Blue Fitness buds early September.  After they arrived, I felt the sound quality was great, loved the way they fit, awareness mode is a game changer, wonderful battery life, and they still worked independently which is a major need for me. Right away, I noticed some charging issues, occasionally they wouldn't charge in the case and I'd have to tap it gently a few times until the lights came on to indicate charging.  No big deal since they charge quickly and it only occasionally happened, figured it was from carrying them in my pocket…

reviews.title: The Search Continued - Eventually Chose Soundcore Space a40
reviews.text: I came to these in my search for earbuds similar to the Galaxy Buds +. I really Iiked them initially and felt the fit similarly was a long battery life. I realized, however, that they weren't disconnecting from the phone when I put them in their case, which meant they weren't charging. After reading some negative reviews, I realized this was a common problem. Many reviewers mentioned that it occurred after the return period, so I suppose I was lucky to realize it early. I sent them back, frustrated and disappointed, ordering my next choice, the Soundcore Space a40 earbuds. They fit almost exactly the same as the Galaxy Buds +, have excellent battery life, and charge quickly. I highly recommend those when these disappoint you.

reviews.title: Volume level solved
reviews.text: Paired with samsung TV.  These headphones have a button that disables adjusting the volume. It is located between the plus and minus buttons. It's basically like a lock button to prevent you accidentally pressing the volume and adjusting it by accident  If you press it, the volume will go off for 2 seconds and then come back.  That will indicate the volume plus and minus buttons are locked and even if you press it, it won't change the volume.  If you press it again, the volume will not turn off but it will allow you to adjust the volume again by using the plus and minus buttons.

reviews.title: Not noise-cancelling. Really thin sound.
reviews.text: I didn’t buy these thinking they were noise-cancelling, funny that Amazon asked me to rate that (non-existent) feature.  Despite some of the negative reviews about the build quality, I went ahead and bought these. They sure use a lot of plastic in the packaging… I went ahead and paired them to my phone (quick and painless) and gave the a test. What I found was sound that was really thin in the mids and highs, and while there was adequate bass, it wasn’t really punchy. It’s kind of like listening to music immediately after swimming while your ears are still full of water. I tried with several different songs and genres, all of them with which I am thoroughly familiar, and was seriously underwhelmed. I’d expect this kind of sound out of a $30 headset, but not at this price point and not from JBL.  I haven’t decided yet on sending them back but I’m leaning strongly in that direction. I’m go…

reviews.title: Uncomfortable to wear; poor audio quality
reviews.text: These headphones are very disappointing. I've never had high end headphones, so my standards aren't high and I'm not comparing them to anything expensive. But even by my low standards, the audio quality is very poor - it's tinny and shallow and there's no bass whatsoever. Additionally, the headphones are very uncomfortable to wear. They are tight and squeeze my head really hard. The band hurts the top of my head, too. You can adjust the cups up and down, but can't adjust the curve of the band. I'm a petite woman and my head isn't particularly large, so I can imagine what this must feel like on people with larger heads. While these headphones aren't as expensive as the high end ones, they aren't exactly cheap either, and to me they aren't worth that price if they are such low quality. I had to return them, and will keep looking.

USB-C slot location is just DUMB - why not to place it where most of the other phones have it - at the BOTTOM, not inside? Overall, a very mediocre device which only worth buying if it is heavily discounted (i.e. under $40)

reviews.title: This device DOES NOT have active noise cancelling

Other things I didn't like: it doesn't come with any kind of case. That's a minor issue, since I rarely use a case but it might be an issue for someone else. reviews.title: I was legitimately amazed!
reviews.text: Let's start by saying that I wear headphones about 12-16 hours a day. I do all my work from home and all my gaming and other hobbies wearing and using headphones. I'm not rough on them, but they get a ton of nonstop use.  I'm an IT professional and an amateur sound engineer as a hobby for my own music. Over the last decade, I've probably without exaggeration, bought 30-50 pairs of headphones/headsets. They always let me down no matter if I spend a little or a lot. Finally, I decided to just use my streaming mic (Blue Yeti) for work calls, and to get a pair of wired audiophile headphones. Audio Technica is a brand I know and know that they're respectable.  Let me tell you about how happy I felt the first time I put these on (earlier today)!  First of all, they weigh almost nothing. It really feels like you are wearing a cloud on your head, but not in a way that feels like they are going t…

reviews.title: Terrible headband design ruins an otherwise awesome pair of headphones
reviews.text: I want to like Audio-Technica. I really do. But they make is so hard to. Even if these headphones sounded excellent, it wouldn’t matter because of these stupid gimmicky wing supports designed to keep the headlines on your head. In short, they simply don’t work. They don’t have nearly enough spring tension to them and they end up up sliding down your head. I ended up tying them together with a strap to keep them from falling down my head. That lasted a week before I decided this is absurd. They’re going back. How absolutely awful designs like this make it all the way to mass production is mind boggling. AT needs to ditch this design ASAP. Aside from that, the cans are enormous. Like, unnecessarily goofy big. Finally, these are a little bright. The highs are a little too pronounced and can be quite harsh at higher volumes. Tried out a pair of Sennheiser HD 599s and every problem I had with…

reviews.title: A great set of headphone!
reviews.text: I had previously purchased a Sennheiser HD 380 which I hated because of the cheap construction and unbearable pressure from the ear cups.  But these are super comfortable, have some metal and seem to be well constructed...and they sound much better than the HD 380's.  I would have liked to have a screw-on 1/4 inch adapter instead of a push/pull adapter, and a replaceable cable...then it would have been a 5 star.

reviews.title: Great mixing headphones for the price
reviews.text: These are the second pair of open back headphones I've used so far, for mixing music, and for the price I am very pleased.  I had been using AKGs before, their entry level, and it was a little lacking in all frequencies.  But theses headphones proved what I would describe as a better all-around sound.  The bass is at a very neutral setting, allowing you to hear how the entire mix might sound after compression and mastering.  The highs are not too shrill. When I listen to the same mix in my Nura phones and or car stereo, the mix sounds great, and allows me to be able to identify areas that need to be EQd etc..  As for the way they fit, I would say that they could improve just a touch on the ergonomics.  While they do not cause ear fatigue (most important) they do tend to slip down, and I have a big head, so for smaller headed people it may be a bigger deal. That is really my only complain…

reviews.title: Amazing Sound.
reviews.text: Sound fantastic: highs, lows, mids. Great range. But if you're looking for anything noise with cancellation these aren't it. You can hear a good bit through these. The fabric for the ear cushions is very comfortable but not dense to keep out noise. The entire design is meant to be light. Keep that in mind. These are perfectly comfortable to wear for 6+ hours. Just keep a relatively quiet environment.

reviews.title: Good sound
reviews.text: The headphones were returned since they were way too big for my head and were not adjustable. If they had fit I would have kept them as they seemed to play well with my motherboard audio output.

reviews.title: Nice Airy sound and comfortable with very little Bass.
reviews.text: So I have not ever wore a pair of open-back earphones. Did a little research though so had an understanding of what to expect. These Audio Technica ath ad500x were definitely Airy when listening to music. I do like a little bass in my music and unfortunately these did not provide enough for me. I am not sure if it was because of the open back or something else but I had to return them. They are really light and comfortable. Also would have liked to have a removable cable so I could replace it with a shorter one.

reviews.title: Great value for money headphones
reviews.text: Audio-technica has improved a lot in the last few years. I was amazed by the quality of the headphones in such a low price.

reviews.title: Great headphones - cord is terrible
reviews.text: These headphones produce very good sound quality in my opinion - crisp treble and straightforward mids. Contrary to rumor, these headphones are not "bassless," unless of course you are comparing them to Beats or some other brand/model made to pander to the preferences of common bass-junky. That being said, the sound profile of these headphones is still quite bright compared to what you may be used to, which I don't have a problem with but some people may. These phones work great for gaming, especially if you're looking to more easily hear subtle movement sounds in an FPS setting.  The reason I didn't give five stars on this product has nothing to do with the headphones themselves, but rather the cord. The cord is a frustrating nuisance. Audio-Technica has inadvertently educed the shape-retaining qualities of wrapping ribbon with the cord on these headphones. Forever defying gravity and c…

reviews.title: Happy customer
reviews.text: Bought it for the kid, and he's super happy with it. No complaints from him, and you know how kids will complain if something is amiss. So I'll give it 5 stars and call it a happy purchase.

reviews.title: Goldilocks of headphones
reviews.text: Treated myself to high fidelity headphones.  I've had others like Graco which I agree sounds good but looks so bad I just couldn't keep them.  These look cool and I wanted to try the open back type which is supposed to be more natural.  Also I was intrigued with using these for FPS gaming b/c of the reviews that stated you could "hear where the bullets where coming from".  Very pleased so far.  The sound is definitely much better than the normal ear pods.  I can't really say that it's been a big help with gaming.  When used with my headphone amplifier, it's provided hours of enjoyment of music videos.  So I can't bring myself to go crazy on super high end anything.  This represents a great value, super cool looks, appropriately better sound.  I will say that the design takes some getting used to if you're used to headphones gripping your head, this is almost too lose but it stays…

reviews.title: This headphone is perfect for people with large heads
reviews.text: This headphone is perfect for people with large heads. It's interesting that you can hear everything outside while having the headphone on. However, it also leaks a lot of sound when listening with high volume.

reviews.title: Decent Cans!
reviews.text: Would give 4.5 but it's my first day owning them. These headphones sound great, the bass is there and the highs are there. But, they really shine with the mids, which is a decent leveling, although you can up the bass on your device, that really brought the sound quality up. I'd recommend wearing these at home, they aren't built as well as I had hoped and they feel a bit flimsy, but despite this, they fit well and sound great.

reviews.title: Great sound, but not the best fit
reviews.text: This is my first set of open cans and I love their sound. Great clarity all across the frequency spectrum. The sound feels comfortable and natural, but unfortunately the headphones themselves aren't the comfiest. There isn't must adjusting that can be done to the fit and I've found that these sit a bit too low on my head and thus end up making my ears sore. However, they are extremely comfortable for the first hour or so up until this point.

reviews.title: Awesome headset

reviews.text: These headphones sound amazing but unfortunately the wings that hold it in place on your head are held on by a thin piece of plastic that breaks easily. reviews.title: A good value

The bass response is acceptable and the sound is well balanced across the audible spectrum. Second, the cable is a very flexible and durable mesh fabric. It doesn’t kink and tangle as easily as plastic and is reinforced at the plug end. The headband is a light fleece type material - it tends to be warm, but that would be a plus outdoors in cold weather. reviews.title: Great Sound
reviews.text: I used the headset the first time doing yard work. The sound was Clear and I didn't have to crank up the volume to the max to hear it like my old set. reviews.title: Ergonomically superior and versatile
reviews.text: My new favorite headphones.  I connect with my phone, not just for phone calls, but even more often when I listen to podcasts while walking and need to adjust the volume, skip forward and back, or power it on/off, all without having to take my phone from my pocket.  The buttons are easy to find without looking and without using the wrong one.  I connect with my computer for un-tethered use during Zoom meetings or for watching videos.  The battery lasts a long time between charges, and is easily recharged.  The cables can retract quickly and easily if I need to free my ears for conversations, or when not in use so that they stay out of my way when I'm not connecting.  Its only imperfection is that I would wish it to have a greater range, in case I want to connect from the next room over, but I'm completely satisfied overall.

reviews.title: Hearing impaired specifics reviewed

The rigidity may hit volume controls on IC HA's. I was lucky with a good fit. I wish that the back was not so hard and allowed for more positions on the head. Sound variations and volumes again with a hard stop or maybe a special app for hearing impaired to allow for more sound with control over clarity. These are hearing impaired specifics reviewed.

I bought them so I could listen to podcasts at work without disturbing others and without having to have one AirPod in, which gives me a feeling of unbalance that I was hoping not having either ear obstructed would solve. reviews.title: Way  too quiet
reviews.text: These are just way way way too quiet.  I'll get them situated on my temples the best I can, crank the volume on my phone and the headset, but once I get going on my bike with moderate wind noise...yeah..I can BARELY hear the music. If you're using these in a stationary environment indoors, you'll probably be fine..but no way I would recommend these to anyone looking for something to wear out and about.  I shoulda know when "whisper" was in the brand name. Micro-USB charging in 2022 is also a loser move.

reviews.title: Youth does not indicate small
reviews.text: I can't find bone conduction headphones to fit my small head.  I tried these and they did not work.  I appreciate that they were able to be returned.

reviews.title: Not the best introduction to conduction headsets. Ok drivers, horrible microphone.
reviews.text: Good for general use in quiet environments, but probably not the best introduction to conduction headsets and not good for voice/video calls.  For the price, this headset is good. I appreciate the standard USB charging plug and the multi-functional volume buttons.  A huge negative is that the volume doesn't get that high; even with the earplugs in, it is faint. EQ range is not the greatest, but that is expected with the conduction headsets.  The microphone pickup is horrible.  Under good conditions (quiet room with no echo), the microphone sound like you are on the far end of a tunnel. In a room with ambient noise, conversations are problematic.

reviews.title: Extremely impressed with noise canceling abilities
reviews.text: I've used the ATH-ANC7B on several flights and have found that they do an excellent job blocking ambient noises -- specifically the drone of the plane's engines and HVAC system -- making it possible to listen to music, podcasts and movies with the volume set to normal levels. Even quiet passages in movies and music come through well -- never any need to jack up the volume.  On my most recent flight, the HVAC system was turned up so insanely high that the ambient sound level on the plane -- according to an app on my iPhone -- was 94dB! That's the same level of noise you hear standing 30 feet from a motorcycle. But the ATH-ANC7B reduced it to a mild hum and I was able to watch a movie with no problem. Whenever I took the headphones off it was jarring just how loud the plane really was.  Sound Quality: When listening on a plane the quality is perfectly good. But I wouldn't use them as every…

reviews.title: Would be a great gift! Guaranteed happy recipient.
reviews.text: I bought a pair. My colleague tried and then bought a pair. My husband borrowed mine and then I had to buy another pair. Just two days ago another colleague asked to try them and then ordered a pair. A GREAT value at this price, and even when they aren't turned on, I use them to just quiet the sound around me as I work in an open space. Plus, people often leave me alone to work when I have them on!

reviews.title: Hands down my go-to noise cancelling headphones for any situation.
reviews.text: I love these headphones. Great for airplane flights, road trips, and even just chilling at home. I recommend these, even compared to the more expensive brands on the market. These effectively block out background noise while providing superior audio. I really can't ask for anything more. In fact, I bought these in 2005, and I've borrowed other sets from friends, just to test them, and nothing yet has beaten these. I definitely recommend them - though of course, by now there must be an newwer version of this type, and of course that's worth looking into. I can only speak honestly about this specific type, which may not even be for sale any longer lol

reviews.title: Better noise canceling than Bose!

reviews.title: very nice
reviews.text: Work well, very comfortable, keeps out much of the ambient noise and then the noise cancellation works on top of that.  Good sound quality.  Only drawback is the size; case is twice the volume of the old Sony NC headset I replaced.

reviews.title: Doesn't block conversation as well as I'd like, but the price is still good
reviews.text: I bought these for flying.  It serves the role of blocking airplane noise quite well, but it does a poor job of blocking conversational noise.  In fact you can have a conversation with someone while wearing these even in active mode.  If you're looking for something to use to block out office sounds, you probably need to look elsewhere, but if you just want a quieter bus, train, or plane commute, this should serve you well.

reviews.title: Cans Crimp Ears
reviews.text: I bought these to replace an old pair of Denon noise canceling headphones that I loved but quit after 2 1/2 years (they are no longer produced).  I fly a lot and need comfortable headphones for the plane.  The Audio-Technica were solid in terms of noise canceling but I found them to be so uncomfortable that I ended up sending them back.  I could wear them about 30 minutes before I had to take them off.  Even when I loosened up the top piece they still felt very tight.  They were also heavy and I found them hot (I recognize this is kind of strange and I can't explain this phenomenon).  For me the discomfort was not worth it.

reviews.title: Just received mine.  Impressed so far.
reviews.text: These just arrived,  so I don't know about the longevity of these yet,  but so far I'm impressed.  The clarity with noise blocking on is amazing.  And for the price, I definitely could've ended up with only so-so quality. Definitely living up to the good reviews for now.

Independent reviews indicate the Bose headphones do a better job of noise cancellation and I do notice that it doesn't always block out a loud TV, for instance.  I have no regrets on the purchase though and am very satisfied that I am getting my money's worth from them.

reviews.title: hurt my ears

They were super comfy for the first 45min or so, but then they begin to hurt so bad, I can't wear them.  I have tried using them for multiple flights, and it's always the same problem.  I have used the bose quiet comforts in the past and never had this issue.  I am not a fan of bose products (overpriced and not necessarily the best sound), but I never got ear fatigue.  Now, I guess I am in the market for something new . . . .

reviews.title: I like it!
reviews.text: I have used the Bose noise-canceling headphones for years. My last pair disintegrated after a few years -- the soft plastic covering the cushions came off in flakes. Appalled by this quality issue - especially in light of the amount of money those headphones cost - I felt it was time to look for an alternative. So far I have been very happy with the Audio-Technica product. It is a bit bulkier than the Bose. But it sits equally comfortably on the head and ears, even on long transcontinental flight. As far as noise-canceling is concerned, I actually like them even better than the Bose. And you can listen to music without the noise canceling turned on. With the Bose I occasionally noticed some interference with radio signals in the area that resulted in a vibrating high-pitched tone, none of that with the Audio-Technica. Too soon to tell how they will hold up, but they seem to be sturdy. In…

I also like that it has two removable cords, short and long and a plane adapter. It can be used with the phone, tablet, computer. Noise cancelling feature is really powerful.  Five years later after the purchase:  sound is still very good. I got two other pairs of headphones, one is the latest model of Sennheiser for the same price and still Audio-Technica sound is the best. Still love it. Headphones are still alive after 5 years of use! Bad thing is that after all those years plastic on the left side got cracked, I think I damaged it by carrying it around without a case in a bag and throwing other things on top of it. Because of that the sound in the left ear disappears from time to time. I used a tape to push crack sides together and fix the crack. After th…

reviews.title: Very Good
reviews.text: I purchased these headphones because I have chronic migraines that are very sensitive to sound. My husband loves to play his music loud, so in an effort to compromise we ponied up the cash for some earbuds that didn't help at all; however, these headphones are so much better! Of course, nothing is perfect and some sounds still come through, but it's such a vast improvement we both consider this cash well-spent.

reviews.title: Trying to decide if I should return these
reviews.text: I just received these headphones today from Amazon.  I had tried these headphones at a shop in the airport a few months ago and really liked the noise cancelling and the sound quality.  What I did not realize was the annoying sound leakage from these headphones.  I'm not sure if people will be able to hear the leakage on a flight but at home everyone can.  I bought these primarily to use on airplanes but I need to decide if the leakage is bearable.  I'll try them some more over the next few days before I make the decision.  I got these on Black Friday week for a tremendous price and don't want to spend 300.00 for other quality noise cancelling units.

reviews.title: Waste of time and money
reviews.text: What a colossal waste of time and money.  I bought these so they would cancel out noise, allowing me to read or study whle my wife watched TV.  Not only did they not work they were less efficient than a cheap set of shooting ear muffs. SAVE YOUR MONEY.

reviews.title: Works excellent, just not very long...
reviews.text: I purchased these to replace a set of SONY Noise-Cancelling headphones that I forgot on the plane.  I rec'd them quickly and in excellent shipping packaging.  The sound quality was much better than what I was used to in the SONY, not really a comparison.  However, they have since stopped working.  No real reason to either, simply sitting on the plane, and the sound quit.  At first I thought the battery died, but I replaced it and when I turned it on, the sound is still gone, turn them off and the sound would returned but not with the noise cancelled... turn them back on and the sound stops.  Frustrating to say the least in that they obviously must be working somewhat or the sound would not be stopped from coming out just by flipping the switch.

reviews.title: Great product, great value
reviews.text: Hello prospective noise reducing headphone buyers. I used this product last night for the first time on a flight from Houston to Tokyo, and then on to Bangkok. I wore for about 16 hours and did not notice any discomfort to my ears (feeling of pressure or soreness). The ATH ANC7B greatly reducted amblent cabin noise (engine, crew noise serving meals). Voices do come through more than I had hoped, but this may just be outside the design parameters of this product. All-in-all I consider them a tremendous value, certainly as compared with the Bose equivalent and recommend them to anyone looking to make their flight a little more pleasant.  Just an update. I have worn out this one, and plan to buy another. Over 3.5 years it gave consisently good perforance. Maybe 50 wearings in all over that time. At 12-16 hours a clip that's a lot of use. reviews.title: Most durable ever!
reviews.text: My husband has to wear hands free device while driving. These were half price of his usual brand, and we were leery about them. Today, they proved they are the best in durability.  My husband drives a small fuel tanker, he was cleaning out a tank by flushing with diesel, 350 gallons to be exact. He didnt notice until he had finished that, that they were missing. He then loaded over 100 gallons of engine oil in the tank. He looked all over thinking he had lost them somewhere else. Then he noticed his phone was still paired! After delivering the oil, he searched the truck over thinking they fell under the seat etc. While cleaning the tank out he saw them there, laying on bottom of the tank, blue light still shining that it is on! He got them out, cleaned them up and they still work! Great sound too!

reviews.title: DURABLE, GREAT RUN TIME, GREAT SERVICE for a GREAT VALUE!

Now, I’m not an audiophile, but I listen to audiobooks and podcasts constantly. For that reason, I have 2 different pairs of SoundPeats. I own the Q30’s and Q36’s and have been overwhelmingly satisfied in the following 3 ways. This does not mean that they don’t produce outstanding music quality, I just wouldn’t be the best person to give an opinion in that regard.  If the following areas are important to you as they are me, you cannot go wrong with SoundPeats Products.  1. Durability - I’ve purchased other wireless earbuds at an equivalent price point and they last me, maybe 6mo before they fail. These headphones hold up to listening of 4-8hrs a day. (I’m fortunate to be able to listen while I work)  2. Battery Longevity…

reviews.title: These sound tingy and harsh
reviews.text: Years ago I bought some cheaper earbuds called vavamoov. I don’t think they’re available anymore, but the sound quality was fine or decent.  Unfortunately, these are pretty horrible. I’ve had to turn down the volume to cut down on the harshness. Even when I don’t, they’re tingy.  I wasn’t looking for audiophile headphones, and that’s not what I expected to get, but these are bad.  I’m wondering if buying some similarly priced earbuds with a brand name would be any better.  I head a pair of mmp wireless earbuds and wasn’t impressed, but they were certainly acceptable. I think those were around 60 bucks.  Anyway, I don’t have a good recommendation at the time, but these are a no go, for me.  They’re not good for talk or music. I’m giving them 2 stars because the seem to work. I love Australians, but the woman’s voice sounds pretty bad with the scratchy/tingy earbuds.

reviews.title: Long time customer...  Somewhat disappointed in Q30HD bass.
reviews.text: I've had the Q12 and the Q30Plus.  They both served me well.  I lost my Q30 plus, and just stepped on my Q12's (still working after 3 years.). They are definitely worth the price and I will enjoy then but just thought I'd put that out there for repeat customers.

reviews.title: Durable as hell, neutral sounding.
reviews.text: Not the best sound quality, they are kind of flat and neutral in the mids and highs with a strong bass roll off. What I really like is how well built they are. I use these every night to watch movies and to sleep to a podcast. I keep them on all night and then they get slept on and rolled around, so I usually kill headphones in a few months but these have held up nicely with zero issues. So what they provide in stability they make up for in sound quality.  Update: Over a year later and these are still holding up nicely! I'm very impressed. My opinion on the audio still stands. As someone who is a music producer and engineer I am picky about sound quality and despite the light bass frequencies these are a great sounding set of earbuds.

reviews.title: They're pretty good for the money.
reviews.text: The bass leaves a bit to be desired and the clarity could be better.. but they're comfortable and I spent around $40. They pretty seamlessly switch between my phone and Steam Deck when I want to change, I don't have to reconnect or anything. Though, they do randomly disconnect and reconnect every so often. The only other thing of note is that the volume seems to do some weird things with my Deck, but it might just be the Deck. Battery life on these is also pretty good, but note, you can't charge and listen at the same time. Overall, I'm pretty happy with these and would recommend them to anyone who doesn't need "the best" and just wants a comfortable set of cans for portable gaming or sitting in quiet rooms.

One has a longer playtime, great sound quality and more color options and is $25, and the other is $200, endorsed by a reality TV star.

Thus, using the headphones with an MP3 player while walking or jogging could keep you from hearing approaching cars -- if this is what you plan to use the headphones fo…

reviews.title: Fantastic lightweight headphones that can also be used for calls
reviews.text: The Bose SoundTrue is a lightweight headphone that has crisp clear sound and also works as a phone headset thanks to an inline mic with a 3 button remote. The bass is rich, but probably not enough if you like it thumping a lot. There isn’t any distortion and it does a good job of isolating ambient noise. I’m impressed by the sound quality for the price.  The inline buttons can be used for answering calls or for skipping through audio files. It even works to skip tracks on Spotify. It folds flat for storage and comes in a nice compact zip case, as it should for this price.  I like that the cable detaches for storage, and is hence replaceable – although the replacement is pretty pricey. But in my experience, the cord is usually the weakest link and it will be cheaper to replace that than the entire headset.

reviews.title: Worst microphone I've used in my life
reviews.text: Perhaps I got a defective one, I'm not sure. But it's literally the worst microphone I've used in my life. I see people in Youtube videos using it, and if I believe they're using it, it doesn't sound so bad there. But literally anything is better than mine: built in microphones, desktop microphones shipped with an ABS computer from 1999, $7 Zallman microphones, anything. I've tried it on multiple computers, it is the same on all. I've looked through the settings. The sound is very soft and faint, and when you turn the volume up using the gain feature, it gets all gainy, hissy, and unusable. I tried to make a video demonstrating this, but with so many microphones that I own, some of them I thought were recording and weren't. I may put that together later. I'm pretty lazy and don't want to bother putting this in a box and paying postage back to sender. Guess I just got shafted...  Addition…

reviews.title: Essential device to free you to chose better headphones
reviews.text: I don't know what it is, but as soon as companies add a mic boom to their headsets, the audio quality of the headphones seems to drop off, but the price doesn't. This wireless mic lets you turn any headphones or VR headset into one with a mic boom. And when it comes time to get new cans, you can just slap this mic on the new ones!  If you use VR and you have anything other than an Index (which has a very good mic), this is a game-changer. I've used all of the major HMDs, and they all have atrocious microphones, save for the Index. That isn't a big deal unless you are into social games, or like to stream.  The only feature I wish we could get is sidetone (hearing yourself). It's easier to speak when you can hear yourself, especially when using headsets that isolate outside sound. reviews.title: Great Mic But Expensive
reviews.text: This is about the best wireless mic you can get for your headphones.  It works really well, and setup is easy.  Sound quality is lots better than my last boom mic, and about as good as a Blue Yeti for simple voice comms.  The sticky magnetic bits work well on most headphones, but not at all on a perforated and very round headphone.  It did stay on a perforated flat headphone though.  Love that I can add a good mic to my favorite headphones without running extra wires.  Dislike the the power/mute button setup.  You hold down the button a couple of seconds to turn it on/off, but you're supposed to tap it to mute as well; getting the timing right to turn it off is some times frustrating.  Wish there was feedback when the mic is muted.  The red light comes on to indicate mute, but since the light is at the base of the microphone, by your ear, you're never sure whether you're muted or not wit…

reviews.title: Good at what they do, but didn't last
reviews.text: I am writing this review on the day the headphones died. 61 days after I got them. I was very careful with them, but they mysteriously died on my desk in the night. This fact is the most important part of the review. Aside from that terrible, fatal flaw I really liked them though. For listening to podcasts and audio books while working out they were great. You can hear the media fine, but also hear the world well enough to not get hit by a bus or anything. Battery life was great. Like maybe almost 12 hours. But none of this justifies them dying in only 2 months. A few downsides: because of their shape the only way to safely transport them is on your head. There's just no good way to pack them. Also, any pure tones are waaaay louder than anything else. So if you are listening to something at a comfortable volume on your phone and some kind of notification comes through and makes a beeping…

reviews.text: I've settled for traditional in-ear earbuds for many years and while I like their sound quality, they always hurt the inside of my ears after about 20 minutes of use and leave them sore afterwards, regardless of size. A family member recommended bone-conduction earbuds to me so I started looking for a pair for my birthday. I like these because they weren't cheapos but didn't cost a fortune either. Bluetooth was easy to connect and they are very comfortable. Only complaints are that they stick out from the back of my head and are not adjustable (so I can't lay down or lean back into a chair with them because they'll get pushed out of place), there is no mic, and the sound quality is not as good. I have to turn the volume up significantly more than I did with traditionals.

reviews.title: Three sets in a row, DOA. SKULLCANDY = CRAP
reviews.text: Over the space of a month, I bought 3 pair of these. Every set, the left was DOA. Would not power up, turn on, charge, or respond in any fashion. Yes, I removed the sticker over the charge port for the buds. I troubleshoot the system as far as I could without opening the case. I am a Systems Engineer. I deal with electronics all the time. I even verified voltage was present on the charge pins, and in the earbud themselves (1.5v, FYI). The left earbud simply would not work. This is a common problem with this product. I should not have to troubleshoot it, when I can buy a 20 dollar pair and they just work. Support from sellers and the manufacturer is nonexistent. Happily returned all three sets. I will go with the Anker brand, as I've invariably had excellent experience with their products. Skullcandy is trash. It's a shame, as the software upgrade feature seemed promising.

reviews.title: Interesting app
reviews.text: I've been using these earbuds for several weeks now, and they're as good as any pair I have. And I have several. They connect without issue and have good, clear sound. If you're looking for the intricasies of fine tuning, how good is the base and all that, I'm not the gal for you. However, I think music sounds great, and they're perfect for listening to YouTube vids on my computer and audio books on my phone. The app is interesting. At first I thought I could talk directly to my buds. "Hey, Skullcandy!" (First earbuds I've had with voice control.) But you have to use the app for that feature. Not quite as convenient in my opinion, although perhaps I was expecting too much. The controls are not touch, but require clicking on the individual buds to control them. You can also control them through the app, though. Instructions are clear and easy to understand. I was up and running in minutes…

reviews.title: Works great, and fantastic buy for the price.
reviews.text: Both my iPhone and my laptop use 3 ring 3.5mm plugs for headphones.  Since my work provided me with a Jabra Bluetooth headset (that I don't care for) and a wireless phone headset for my Cisco phone, I figured I wouldn't really need this, but thought it would be good to have a wired back up.  For $8, I expected something cheap, and while this doesn't feel high end, it sounds and works great.  Reading the comments, I suppose I got lucky, as the QC probably lets some buggier models through, but for the price I paid, I'm very happy with this headset.

reviews.title: Get some foam earbuds
reviews.text: These are fantastic at this price point and offer good sound and value.  If you're reading this, you're not moron or a sucker in buying $250 Airpods or even $100 earbuds from mainline manufacturers.  I upgraded from wireless earbuds with the wire connecting in back, but wanted true wireless since I'm at the gym or running 5-6 days a week.  The wire in back got annoying.  The build quality is solid with a really nice case and I like how they connect via magnet to charge.  Battery performance is always overrated with bluetooth stuff so only time will tell how long they truly last - that's why it's useless to pay top dollar for something with a non-replaceable battery.  The real key to all earbuds is to get some foam tips though IMO.  So much more comfortable, better sounding, and you get some noise cancellation as well - it really upgrades the sound.  Foam tips don't last as long with swea…

I just recently came back to buy another one and noticed it was around $40!!! That is crazy for this product! The seller must be confused! Here are the short, sweet points:  1) Ninety percent of the time, I use mine for running and biking with my iPhone/iPod. I sweat obnoxiously, and they still hold up against the "moisture" (which is an understatement). They're definitely durable. If you're that athlete hunting for "the pair", these are a solid bet to go with!  2) They really don't kid about the "ultra lightweight" aspect! These are amazingly lightweight and flexible, and that lends to an amazing fit. They don't hurt my ears (or head) from pushing or squeezing too firmly.  3) The sound quality is great for my standards. These compare (or surpass) any I've use…

reviews.title: no cord problems yet....
reviews.text: Reading the reviews confirmed one thing: If it weren't for the poor cord connection, these headphones would be incredible!  The fact that they were only $13...I figured I'd try them out.  I've had them for 3 weeks now.  I run 3x a week.  Like all of the other positive reviews, these things are incredible.  I'm amazed by their sound quality.  They are extremely light, and they stay in one place on my head virtually the entire run.  I've never had to fumble with them, or even worry about them during a run!  I've treated them like I'm carrying a raw egg on a spoon...so I haven't destroyed them yet by the dreaded "accidental tug of death."  If you are willing to take care of them, the $13 risk is an absolute no-brainer with these!!!

reviews.title: Light, good sound, beats competitors
reviews.text: I bought at least 5 different kinds of earbuds and over-the-head on amazon, ranging from $6 - $25, from SONY, Panasonic, Skull Candy, and Seinheiser.  This has perhaps the best price-to-quality ratio.  I can't speak to durability, but just on sound, this is quite outstanding.  It's ultra comfortable and super light.  For everyday, in-house use, it's great.  For airplane, at least get the earbud to isolate some of the ambient sound.

reviews.title: Sony MDR-W08L Alternative now available
reviews.text: Sony has somehow seen fit to discontinue the MDR-W08 headphones. Finally there is a viable alternative in the Koss KPH14 that was introduced in 2015. Available for around $12 each. The KPH14s aren't quite as good as the Sony but close enough and at a reasonable price.

reviews.title: Not very comfortable
reviews.text: I had a set of headphones that I loved but the died, and ever since, I have been on a quest to fnd a replacement.  I like the sound that these provide, but they are not very comfortable, so I can only wear them for short periods.

reviews.title: Good sound quality
reviews.text: I use these every day and they are comfortable and easy to use.  No pressure to ears or head.  I would buy more

reviews.title: Better Off With Something Else
reviews.text: I have bought this product numerous times and they always wind up shorting out slightly after three month which incidentally marks the end of the warranty period. I don't know if the are manufactured this way or what. I have tried to keep the cord straight and always make sure it is not twisted, but always wind up with a short nonetheless. I have bought this product numerous times, due to the availability and cost. Now this product costs $30+ dollars, when it used to be $10. Crazy and not worth the money. Honestly you are better off with another product.

reviews.title: Great Purchase
reviews.text: For the price these headphones are much better than I expected. They feel very breakable, but so far so good! They stayed in my ears perfectly while running. I bought them mostly to listen to audiobooks on my runs.

reviews.title: Super lightweight!
reviews.text: Bought a pair of these 15 years ago and they lasted all this time.  Actually, until my husband got too rough with them and pulled the delicate wires.  This pair is much more delicate in feel which worries me, but it makes them super lightweight, which I love. The old earbuds were bigger, and in my opinion not made for the human ear.  They really hurt my ears after a minute or two of listening.  This pair has smaller, super soft earbuds that are shaped to fit a human ear!  Without the sound you wouldn't even know they're on. The price is reasonable, but the sound could be louder/clearer.  There is no static, just not enough volume.  Maybe I need to remove the cushion on the buds?  Lastly, my old pair folded, which made it easy to fit into a pocket.  I really miss this feature! All in all, these are a great little pair of lightweight, comfortable earphones, with a decent sound.  The foldab…

reviews.title: Does the job
reviews.text: I wear a hat over them to keep them in place better, I had read the cord was short but risked it, I'm 5'8" I wish it was another 6 inches or so.  Also don't like the the cords come out the front of your ears, I prefer to tuck them back.

reviews.title: Best (cheap) headphones for the gym
reviews.text: I love how these "insert" into your ears...  the sound is delivered INTO your ears and not near them.  Especially good on plane flights where you can never hear anything.

reviews.title: Best earphones ever that only last a couple of months.
reviews.text: Like many other reviewers, I have found these earphones so frustrating because they are the best for running and the sound is great, until 2 or 3 months later when the sound goes out in one ear.  This will be my 4th purchase of them.  I'm going to try to get some kind of warrantee or refund next time.

reviews.title: awsome sound
reviews.text: I use these on my iphone in the gym because they don't fall out and the sound is amazing. I will buy these again for my son.

reviews.title: Great headphones for the price
reviews.text: These replace Sony MDR-AS35 and their immediate predecessors. Reviewers said they were better for one third the money. Reviewers were correct. The treble is perhaps slightly rolled off compared to the AS35s, but not in the annoying way it is with my old Sharper Image noice-cancelling phones. Sounds "softer" rather than "duller", if that makes any sense, but instrumental definition on Wagner is nevertheless good. Where the AS35s were better was in the user details: they fold nicely, they come with an extension cord (short for shirt, long for pants pocket). Unfortunately they break easily as well. The W08L probably won't last any longer, but at the price you can buy three for the price of one, which is what I am going to do shortly. In one word: a sleeper.

reviews.title: Practical and super lightweight!
reviews.text: Excellent product. The sound is something good average to good. They are fairly lightweight. The low depth is not very good. I recommend it for the convenience and light weight!

reviews.title: pretty good, for cheap headphones
reviews.text: These are pretty good headphones, considering what you get for what price you pay. Just a simple, lightweight pair of in-the-ear phones; decent sound with nice tones, not too tinny nor bassless. If you can't wear ear buds but need lightweight phones for exercise, you can't go wrong with these.

reviews.title: Premium audio with a couple of downsides
reviews.text: This is my first set of premium ear buds by Sennheiser. I prefer their over ear headphones, but I needed something more suitable and subtle for video meetings that are required for my WFH setting.  The pros that come to mind:  -Noise cancelation. I currently have a personal server running 24/7 in my office, and it sounds like a small plane engine. These ear buds completely eliminate the shrill whirring. The clicks of a mouse and keyboard keys are still faintly audible from time to time, though.  Sound quality - The sound stage on these is fantastic. There is a little sacrifice to the quality of sound with it being an in-ear device (think sounding a little compressed and less spatial in a way),  but the mids are warm and the highs are crispy (sometimes in a way that feels like your skull is getting a nice scratch, so if that's too much you can adjust in their app). The bass is fairly rest…

reviews.title: Very Disappointed!
reviews.text: The first set of earbuds that I received had multiple technical issues. The Transparent and ANC features did not work. When playing music it would abruptly disconnect. I sent it back and requested a replacement. When I got the replacement I got a used, dirty and opened box set. Once paired, it had the pairing settings of the previous user, “Richard”, still programmed on the earbuds. Now I am waiting for my third replacement and crossing my fingers that this time the will be no issues. I honestly didn’t expect this from such a high end set of earbuds and Amazon’s service.

reviews.title: Best wireless earbuds I've owned
reviews.text: I'm an audiophile and when I can't sit at home with my DAC and amp rigged up, these are the next best thing. The sound profile is clean and neutral, the bass is surprisingly powerful.  I bought these when my 3 year old Sennheiser Momentum TW 1.0s finally bit the dust, and this was a big upgrade. I live near downtown Minneapolis and the earbuds are surprisingly good at blocking the sound of a 8-lane highway I walk directly over on a pedestrian bridge. The earbuds are better than that older model at fewer (but still a couple) 1-2 second dropouts.  The worst thing about the Sennheiser TW 1.0 was the trapezoid, round shape that naturally would slip out between your fingers when you touch the buds or hold them. The TW 3.0's have a shape with parallel sides and there are these rubber fins used for ear-sizing and fit. Combined, these two design choices mean I've never dropped the buds onto the …

reviews.title: Better than the 2.0
reviews.text: I had the MTW 2.0's for almost 3yrs. The right bud just stopped working, wouldn't connect & wouldn't even power up. But this is after 3yrs of daily use, working out, getting them used thoroughly!! So I opted to stick with them since I like Senn's sound signature & have or have had several Sennheiser products in the past. These are slightly louder but definitely noticeable but keep the rich & detailed sound stage. The bass is perfect not overwhelming but definitely textured like on the 2.0's. I'm glad I ended up trading up but really had no choice since the 2.0's were done!

reviews.title: Amazing sound and functionality.
reviews.text: Great sound and convenience features. This particular pair was faulty but the brand is excellent and this particular seller resolved my purchase immediately.

reviews.title: Highly recommended
reviews.text: I preferred the Sony sound profile better then I do with sennheiser. The base is a tad heavier which is good if your listening to hip hop but anything else it's overwhelming and you can feel it within an hour or so but over all it's a great pair of earbuds.

reviews.title: potential to be better with some updates
reviews.text: ok the good is that the earbuds are great sounding for music, and have some great features such as wireless charging, multipoint connection, customizable equalizer, wind noise reduction, ear fins to help secure the earbuds which is great for  those  who have trouble with the fit. the bad  is:  no option for ambient mode on phone calls only noise cancelling which makes it hard to hear you own voice, touch sensors are not fully customizable only 1 option for volume, there is a tone when switching between ambient and noise cancelling which is confusing because you don't know what mode you in it should've been a voice prompt. Overall a great set of ear buds on the soundstage alone but for the price point  i feel there's some firmware updates that could improve the user experience.

reviews.title: La...la...la..drop.la..drop. la la drop
reviews.text: Great sound, smooth, clear and reasonably spacious. If you're a bass head, these won't do the trick. For those who want their ear drums at age 70, the bass and lower mids are solid, tight, and smooth. These are some of the most comfortable buds I've worn, unlike brands like the Sony WF-XB700, which feel like you have a rock in your ears.  The problem with these is the Bluetooth. It's terrible. Move 5-10 feet from the source and the signal drops consistently, at times dropping completely. I tried several sources from iPhone, iPad through a Windows desktop, and it didn't make any difference. Even though the sound and comfort are great, the continual drops make them impossible to listen to. Inconsistency is a problem for all Bluetooth buds, but this is intolerable.

reviews.title: Third time is a charm?!?
reviews.text: I bought the first generation of these and they were a total dud....the battery would drain out in less than a day so you could never count on them. You had to keep them on the charger constantly or they would never work. I was so hesitant to buy these after the first ones were a waste of money.  However, now that I have them and have used them for a few weeks I'm really glad they did. They fixed the battery problems from the first generation. I am nothing but impressed with these. The sound quality is unmatched for wireless earbuds. Samsung, Jabra, or Apple can't touch them on sounds quality. It's just a shame that I essentially had to buy these twice. The first generation should have been recalled. If there were other alternatives for sound quality....I wouldn't have bought these. I would have paid twice as much for something better just because I am still sour about the first generati…

reviews.title: Great Buds
reviews.text: Noise cancelling drowns out some office noise not all but you will only notice if your not playing music or not on a call.  The sound and battery life is great.

reviews.title: Lacks Multi-point connection
reviews.text: Lacks Multi-point Connection. A must have for what they're charging. Not worth what they're charging for these.

reviews.title: Comfortable
reviews.text: My husband spends a lot of time on the phone for work. He has been using these for phone calls since his headset has been failing him. For the most part, these have been doing well on his calls. Phone quality is above average, but not as good as the headset. They are really good for listening to podcasts and music. He has worn them while on the eliptical machine without any problems. Noise cancellation is good, but could be improved. They are comfortable to wear for long periods of time.

reviews.title: The Undisputed King of TWE!
reviews.text: Over the years I have tried all kinds of wireless earpods from the AirPods to their pro version to the Sony's mark 3 and 4 to Bose earbuds to B&E EQ and finally B&W PI7's, none, I mean none comes even close to the sound performance of the Senns 3's! They are loud, have a wide soundstage, and just sound fantastic! I am a previous owner of the previous two iterations and the 3's offer noticeable sound quality improvement, wireless charging, and a relatively smaller charging case. My only issue is that it is still big and bulky and not pocketable! For that I'm knocking down a star. Also the app could use a little bit of work. Other than that, another top notch product from Sennheiser!

reviews.title: I hated earbuds till I tried Senso
reviews.text: Honestly, I am not a fan of any kind of earbuds. My daughter likes the tiny ones that hang out of her ear, and I cannot figure out how she dashes around all day without them falling out. Senso solved that problem for me. Their earbuds wrap around my ears comfortably and securely so i can wear them while working out, cleaning house, baking, gardening and so on. Their wraparound style makes sure the buds are in place, delivering sound consistently. The sound quality is very nice too. I am someone who likes more lows than highs, and Senso seems to have a natural draw to the low sounds without drowning out the highs. I have been using my Senso's for two weeks now and I am hooked.

For example I listened to post modern jukebox version of all about that bass, and wasn't able to hear the bass being played, while my ears were bleeding from the vocals.
