reviews.title: Could not get it to fit my ear.
reviews.text: I have no idea what the designers had in mind with this thing; there is no way I could get it to stay in my ear. I was trying to replace a very old Plantronics headset that has served me well for years.  The charge connection never was very good on it and it finally failed entirely.  So I returned this thing and replaced it with another Plantronics unit that uses the identical ear loop as my old one.  The new one works as well as my old one and has a standard micro USB charging port.

reviews.title: THE BEST--THE BEST FIT BEST EASE OF USE HAVE 4 LOVE THEM
reviews.text: love these we have 4 plantronics earbuds  work great its the standard for time and ease of use  get about 7 hrs  the "70" series  (thin white line between black gets 11 )  silicone earpiece is barely noticeable can leave in 8 hrs no ear pain  these are the ones i recommend without hesitation

reviews.title: This device pairs easy and quickly
reviews.text: I am very picky on my headsets I what it to sound "Corded". This device pairs easy and quickly. It has a great design for charging cord. It's audible alerts are a great time saver and announce themselves at the perfect time. This is a high recommend. The four stars instead of five is because, as I said, I am very picky on the audio quality for the other person. I would still buy this in a heartbeat again though.

reviews.title: Bad battery life
reviews.text: I've had three of the PLTE500 and this one is different and very poor. After charging, I get maybe one hour of playing sound before it says, "Battery Low." Previous versions lasted hours, maybe 5 or 6. Repeatable, over and over. It's just a junky backup for me now :(

reviews.title: Very happy customer
reviews.text: I had one before,and my dog chewed it up after having it for 3 years,and had to have another exact one. Its very clear,great battery life,fits my ear perfect for longtime wear,sound quality is great. I love it the second time as well as the first one.

reviews.title: Don’t buy the “renewed” option.
reviews.text: Disappointed in Amazon. I knew this was “renewed” but never imagined it would come with NO way to charge it!  One ear hook and loop on unit - no other sizes included.  Charging strap included but no wall or vehicle charger to plug it into. What good is that?  Only good thing to say is that battery seems to be near new with seven hours operation on it according to auto announcement when I turned it on.  I’ll decide whether to return it after I see how much I have to pay for wall or vehicle charger.  UPDATE: Returned it for refund.

reviews.title: Poorly refurbished.
reviews.text: I knew it was refurbished and have bought refurbished Bluetooths before but this one isn’t put back together probably and hardly works. Can’t pick up phone calls. Very disappointed

reviews.title: Not an M165 or M180!
reviews.text: This is definitely nowhere near as good as the M165 or M180. Unfortunately had to order this one until the other two are back in stock (shortage currently).  It doesn’t announce specific callers, it doesn’t let you answer or ignore by voice, it doesn’t hold a charge for 7 hours talk time, the noise cancellation is mediocre and the sound is not that good. Have volume at max at all times and still can’t hear people well. It also makes crackle sounds when not in use and doesn’t fit as well.

reviews.title: Purchased TWO Units, Both Had Issues
reviews.text: I had two Explorer 500's, one of which I lost so needed a second headset.  This is a little newer so expected similar performance but unfortunately someone at the refurbishment shop isn't paying attention as both units I received had really muddy mic issues which were not happening with my existing headset so I returned both!

reviews.title: Great product

reviews.title: Quality and Low Cost minor PROBLEM

reviews.title: Nice headset for Teams meetings.

reviews.title: Revised: Had Problem, Co. Instantly Replaced with New Unit!
reviews.text: I bought the headset in 2019, 9 months ago. The audio seemed weaker than my previous, expensive Rocketfish  headset which my parrot broke. Two weeks ago, the mic on this unit failed during a call. I could hear, but no one could hear me. I knew the warranty was up, but decided to see if Wantek would give me credit toward a new one.  I emailed them through Amazon and they instantly offered a new replacement. They shipped it right away and didn't ask for the old unit back. I went for it, and am happier with the replacement. The other party sounds louder, so the unit I had was probably defective from day one.  About this unit: I was happy with the price, and how sturdy this headset is, especially the cord, which is about 1/3 thicker than the more expensive Rocketfish headset I had before. The mike boom is longer, too, and adjusts right over my mouth. It swings away if I'm snacking. :)  The s…

reviews.title: Very comfortable.
reviews.text: Purchased this as a replacement for one I’ve been using for a couple of years. As good as they are I don’t recommend stepping on them. Lightweight, adjustable and great sound listening and speaking. Easy in-line volume control. A lot of people I work with have purchased them in spite of being given a headphone from our employer. Excellent value.

reviews.title: Works with Samsung Galaxy S9
reviews.text: This is a great hardwired cell phone headset, if your phone still has an audio jack. This is not bluetooth and will not connect to any cell devices without an audio jack. Very happy and satisfied with it.

reviews.title: Awful. Sound is muffled and distant.
reviews.text: Found it difficult to understand what my colleagues were saying. Don’t buy.

reviews.title: Hasn't fallen apart yet
reviews.text: I've gone through many headphones that I've bought at TJMaxx in an effort not to spend much money on them. They've all broken.  This headset is lasting, and I like having only the one earphone. I don't use this every day though--just once or twice a week for Zoom meetings. But when the meetings are several hours long, I find I don't experience a sore ear, nor does the stabilizer that sits against the skull over the opposite ear begin to irritate. I get terrible migraines from any headset that's too tight or poorly constructed, and so far this headset hasn't triggered one at all.  The sound quality is much better than other headsets I've tried. Now I find myself irritated at people who aren't using headsets, because their sound quality is awful.  It's so easy to swing the microphone up and around and switch to the other ear, if you need a change. The price is incredibly reasonable compare…

reviews.title: An alternative for after Apple breaks your bluetooth...
reviews.text: Anyone who's used iPhones long enough knows this - it's just a matter of time before Apple cranks out a buggy IOS update that causes something on your phone to go wonky, and it may take them quite a while to fix it (if they do).  In my case, IOS update 14.7.1 caused my then perfectly working Bluetooth on my phone to pretty much crud out - nothing that uses Bluetooth works properly now, disconnecting regularly, etc.  I'm not alone - tons of other comments online from others who have had the same or similar issues after that update.  Apple does the usual "really??" bit (they know).  Anywayyyyy... I have to use a headset when on the phone, so bought this along with an adapter so that I can plug it into the iPhone's charging port and use it as a wired set since the phone no longer has a plug for this (thanks again, Apple).  Works great, overall.  I mean, it doesn't feel like a $100 headset, …

Now, what i had to do to get a good fit in order to get the good sound was to replace the included crap cable with a nice braided and balanced cable for $19…..then, I threw the included eartips in the trash because they suck and wont help with fit issues. I bought some premium tips that i like to use for $15. So…$35-$40 for the iems and $34 for cable and tips which increases the final cost of this iem to around $70 or so dollars. Is it still worth it in the sound quality and tuning area….HELL YES!! They are great little budget iems even if you spend a little extra to get a proper fit and seal. Recommended!!

reviews.title: Adequate Sony MDR-W08L Replacement...but still not the original.
reviews.text: Like most others here, I'm seeking an adequate replacement for the now iconic Sony MDR-W08L Vertical In-The-Ear Headphones. These certainly have the style right, and fit on the head very similarly to the Sony's, but they're still not the Sony's. That being said, they're the closest to anything else I've tried thus far.  As others have said, they definitely squeeze. I wear a 7 1/2" ball cap, and they are a bit uncomfortable in my ears. I'm hoping that after repeated wear, they will start to stretch a bit. If they just weren't so snug in my ears, they'd be worlds more comfortable and get 5 stars from me.  The sound is great for the price. Not as dynamic as Sony, but for $10, you can't beat it. Nice and loud too. I will probably buy again.

reviews.title: It Is a Clamp Your Head and Ears Device
reviews.text: I currently have a Sony DR-BT22, a MDR-A30 and a MDR-W24.  I also had a countless number of Sony headphones and earphones from the good old days.  The Sony's from the good old days sounded really great.  I try to find one that is as good as any of the Sony.  This Koss KPH14W is not it.  The spec printed on the box is as follows. 3.5 mm plug 4 feet long cord 100 - 15,000 Hz 18 Ohms 104 dB SPL  This Koss sounds average at best.  I think the best I can describe the differences is that the Sony's sound like an expensive 2.1 speaker system with clean sound and house-shaking bass.  The Koss is just a very average 2.0 speaker system.  It is not FM/AM radio bad.  It is just average.  Your car radio sounds better.  The fit of the Koss is very bad.  It is for kid with small head.  The Koss is at least an inch shorter than the Sony.  The plastic material is hard plastic.  It clamps to my head and i…

reviews.text: I can't explain it, but my daughter goes through headphones like tissue paper. My suspicion is that most headphones are simply not meant to be used as often as she uses them (she plays Roblox and listens to music when she plays). Another annnoyance is sometimes when touching the screen to turn the page, a word will be highlighted and will continue to be highlighted until you turn the Nook on & off (if you succed in turning it off); this is NOT to be confused with the normal highlighting feature.  I went to the local B&N store several times and was unable to get help. Once I was told that if you didn't unplug the Nook from the charger immediately after reaching 100% charge, the above problems would occur.  Another time, I was told that these complaints were frequent with the…

Bottom line: they're great if you just want to try out bone conduction and have some cash to burn, but it might be smart to buy something else if you want an all-around good pair of headphones.

reviews.title: Amazingly helpful, high-quality sound!
reviews.text: This product is simply amazing! I initially ordered this because my wife sometimes has difficulty hearing, and finding a set of ear buds that work well and that are comfortable is a real challenge. I thought that this product looked like it would be much more comfortable than ear plugs, and that it just might work as well. I was surprised. It is, indeed, so incredibly comfortable to wear. It is easy to put on and fits any size head: my large head with not much hair, and my wife's "normal" sized head with long hair. The sound quality is what was most surprising, however. It is perhaps hard to imagine that one could hear well without anything actually being in your ear... but that's exactly what happens with this product. Add to all of this, the Bluetooth technology is handy and easy to use with any Bluetooth enabled device. I give this product my very highest recommendation!

I thought I'd made a mistake connecting the Bose factory cord to the head unit because the sound quality was so much WORSE on the Bose over-ear speakers than on the Dollar General super-cheap in-ear speakers. Buyer beware.

reviews.title: Truly wireless is AWSOME. Doesn't fit everyone. Independent earpieces would be great.
reviews.text: The earpieces are wonderful for music. You need larger ears for the fit to work (my wife cant get it in her ear). For me the fit is very secure. I can exercise without worrying that it will fall out. Once you have a truly wireless earpiece, you will never want anything else.  For the downside, I tend to listen to just on ear bud so I can still interact with the world around me. My one complaint is that the right earpiece is the "master" and the left earpiece cant function independently. If I want only one ear piece in, the right has to be it. The left only functions if i'm wearing the right earpiece. This is a problem because they only have a 3 hours battery life. If I could put the right one in the case to charge and pull out the left it wouldn't matter. I don't carry corded earphones anymore so when the right earpiece goes dead, I am seriously annoyed.

reviews.title: A bit bulky, but great for music, movies, health monitoring
reviews.text: Technology has come such a long way.  I thought these would be good to use as stereo buds for music from my Kindle, phone etc.  But, what is really neat is the fact that you can use it to monitor your heart rate from your phone.  This is amazing.  Without the need for an arm band monitor.  The set comes with a case that actually is used to charge the buds.  You can charge up to two times on a single charge.  This is great.  Next, is that you install the Jabra Sport app on your phone and when paired it monitors your heart rate and takes you through many tests to assess your health.  It comes with 2 sets of 3 of buds and 3 sets of ear wings.  The buds are gel or foam.  I like the memory foam because you get better base and also isolation.  I also tested these through my Amazon Fire Stick.  I paired them, turned on a show on Hulu and was able to hear amazing sound.  The part I kind don't li…

It's a strange feeling, sometimes I felt they are loose and will come off, but they don't! I am using the default medium sized covers on them and the medium gel ear covering. 2. If you are in heavy Bass, these ones are not too "bassy" so heavy hip hop or bass sounds may sound less heavy, but overall sound experience for me was totally much better than all…

reviews.title: 3 decent pairs very cheap
reviews.text: Considering the low price for 3 earbuds I was prepared for much worse.  These aren't premium headphones, but they don't feel super cheap either.  I like them. Much better than the type of earbuds you might receive in a free promotion.  The plastic feels a little light-weight and brittle, but otherwise the look and feel of these are pretty good.  They have a volume slider, which is a must-have, and a built-in mic.  The sound quality is pretty decent as well - definitely not tinny, but don't expect a booming bass response.  Comes in 3 colors, which is fun.  Like most headphones, the cables are the weak point and will fail eventually.  It only took me 5 months of near-daily usage for the cables to fail in 2 of them (I seem to have misplaced the third pair).  I'll try out a slightly more durable brand next time, but I still think these are a great value for light usage.

reviews.title: The Moondrop Chu is dead. Long live the new king.
reviews.text: Well the Moondrop Chu's reign didn't last long. These WILDLY outclass everything under $50. They wildly outclass a lot of stuff under $200.  For starters, detachable cable. I hate the fixed cable on the moondrop chu's with a passion - it's all silicone rubbery and tangles, doesn't stay in place, doesn't stay tied up in your pocket or backpack. The chu's come with a microphone, which is the only thing it has going for it, but if you REALLY need a cable, these are still a far better deal with another $10 spent on the cable. This cable is nice, comfortable, wraps up easily around 3-4 fingers and stays coiled properly.  Then, eartips. The Chu's "springtips" don't really fit quite a few people, myself included. They were so bad that the chu's sounded downright broken until I got some better tips on them. The Zero's come with about five different size of tips that were no problem to find a com…

reviews.title: Fantastic First IEM w/ Insane Value
reviews.text: These were my first entry into IEMs and I really enjoyed the experience. Coming from Google Pixel Buds Pros, these were a significant improvement in sound quality but given the abundance of excellent budget headphones in the chi-fi market, I can't comment as to whether they're better than any of the others you'd find for a similar price.  I also really like the USB-C 2-pin cable that it comes with. It has a subtler finish compared to twisted cables and it also has a built-in mic that works well enough for calls. I actually bought a higher end set of IEMS and ended up using the Salnotes' cable since similar cables cost 1-2x the price of the Salnotes themselves.

reviews.text: Spousal unit, who wears a headset due to his deafness, was VERY happy with this headset.  He said the sound was much clearer and distinct (i.e. voices), a huge improvement over his older (two sets of such) Sony headset.  And, that was on the first day we had this headset. Frankly, I was a little hesitant ordering this set as I was not familiar with the brand but went with Amazon reviews, deciding to order this headset.  I think my initial instincts were correct and I should have paid attention. The first day was great, then everything turned sour from then on.  The constantly blinking red light was our first clue of trouble, then the headset would not make decent contact with the charging unit/transmitter: on and off, on and off, etc.  Finally, the unit started shorting out during use, beeping in his ears and the red light on the transmitter-charger was constantly blinking. reviews.title: Basically perfect, fantastic wind ANC, perfect case

The sound quality uses 1more's app to do a "sounds" hearing preference test. I would prefer a proper EQ option but it works well enough. I prefer real audiophile iem's and headphones, but enjoyed the Galaxy buds on bass boost, they almost hit like planar magnetics. These are about 80% there. They're totally serviceable, with the only standout being a pretty good technical performance, with genuinely solid imaging and separation. They absolutely do need the soundID set up though, I hate the stock tuning.…

reviews.title: Only Good If You Are Totally Stationary
reviews.text: Overall, I thought the headphones were pretty good. Had to read the instructions a few times to understand what they meant, but finally got there. When I tested them out in a stationary setting, in my office, and then riding an exercise bike, the sound quality was OK for the price and there was good noise reduction. But, my need was for headphones I could use while walking or jogging on a treadmill. Although the treadmill noise reduction was acceptable, the headphones could not handle the up and down motion, either of walking or jogging. Each step resulted in a 'thud' sound in each side, like something was moving in there. I tried being stationary and just moving my body up and down rapidly and got a similar but less loud sound. It was so loud, it covered up what I was trying to listen to. Amazon accepted them back as a return. Disappointed, as they seemed to work at first.

reviews.title: Not What I hoped but sadly what I expected
reviews.text: Can not say I did not give the Cowin headsets a good try. The E7 Pro is the second set I have owned. Well anyone can have this problem so I purchased the upgrade to the wireless ones I had thinking the E7 Pro would be updated. Pro: works great for 6 months. Pro: look great. Pro: noise canceling works great.  Cons: NOT comfortable (a change from the previous version) Cons: After 6 months starts interfering with laptop causing huge lagging issues Cons: has two buttons the BT and the NC the only one that worked for me was the NC Cons: about the 4th month every time I put the set on it would say 'needs charging' within a couple hours.  From experience for anyone looking for an affordable good quality headset with NC I say don't, just don't. This is not what you want.

Today, PWK's passion and principles still grace every product we make. Enjoy your Klipsch headphones for their flat frequency response, controlled directivity, low distortion, high-efficiency and, as our founder intended, for their ability to connect you with your favorite music.

The Image S4 utilizes our renowned duel magnet driver technology to deliver strikingly realistic sound and cover a wide frequency range with dynamic detail. With award-winning acoustics and jaw-dropping bass response, the Image S4’s bring the concert experience to you, wherever, whenever.
Live the Music

Long May You Rock

reviews.title: Terrible.
reviews.text: Do not buy these, they are a complete waste of money. I have literally bought these four times and all four broke in a short period of time. They sound pretty good, but they're poorly constructed. One if not both earpieces will go out within a matter of months. I suggest you spend a little more and get some actual quality earbuds like the Etymotic Research HF5 Portable In-Ear Earphones. They sound a lot better and they have a superior design.

reviews.title: Great bass, okay fit
reviews.text: Bought this for my 15 year old son as a birthday present.  He picked them out, so it was easy for me.  They have great bass and sound clarity, allowing him to listen to music at a much lower total volume (which I love as a parent).  Therefore, great sound at a reasonable price.  The tangle-free cord is great, and strong.  The last set he had (not this brand) pulled apart at the plug, so durability was a strong requirement.  The only issue at this point is that they slip out of his ears with the slightest pull on the cord even though they fit tightly.  We are working on methods to clean the silicone covers without making them slippery.  For the volume-lowering sound quality alone, I recommend them.

reviews.title: The Best!
reviews.text: I've been using the first set of Klipsch S4 earphones for years without problem. I saw the white version of the S4-II at half the price of my original S4's and decided to get these as a backup pair. For this price nothing can beat the quality of these gems. The comments others have made about the cord moving being audible when moving around don't happen to mine at all. They sound crisp and clear with a full balanced tone even when I move around a lot. I think one very important factor that many are unaware of is that these earphones need a break in period just as the original S4's did. This break in will "season" the sound of these tiny speakers. You will notice a world of difference in sound quality if you will just do the following: Plug in your earphones to a good CD player and adjust the volume to about half the sound level you listen to at the highest volume you prefer, say …

The earbuds are solid and weighty but not heavy enough to be uncomfortable in the ear.  The only thing I wish it had would be different size ear pieces for different size ears, as they are slightly small in my ears and slightly big in my wifes ears. But the comfort, fit and soun…

reviews.title: They are just okay
reviews.text: I really liked these at first because they worked well, charges correctly, and had easy volume changing capability. But the more I have used them, the more I've been irritated with them. They will randomly stop sometimes - they haven't been touched or removed from my ear. Sometimes it's pausing the media on my phone, and sometimes the sound just goes out and will continue 5-10 seconds later but did not pause. When listening to audiobooks or podcasts I have to rewind a bit to listen to parts that I missed because the earbuds decided to stop working. They are comfortable in my ears, but have a habit of falling out. Not great for working out because if I move too much they get loose and fall. Overall disappointed, but they work I guess.

reviews.title: Review by Allyson Ware
reviews.text: These headphones work really well. I love that you can touch them to pause or turn up the volume or even different things while you are on a phone call or picking up a call. The battery is amazing. I also love that you can hook them up to different devices with ease.

reviews.title: Great sound quality
reviews.text: I have pretty sensitive ears, so can detect when there sound quality isn't as good as expected. These are great though - super high quality crisp sound. Used these for a range of different music, and whatever I played sounded great. Also took these out for a run. I've had problems before with earbuds falling out, but these held in place well, and even when out running (with background noises), the sound quality was very impressive. Far less expensive - and therefore better value - than AirPods in my opinion.

reviews.title: High quality, small package
reviews.text: Great sound, fit my ear really well, which is something I rarely get when I buy headphones. They are a bit bass-y so if that's not your thing, buy a different pair of buds. The charging case is super small, which is wonderful. I have another pair that have a large charging case with days worth of battery, but I'd rather have the tiny form factor. These will probably be my new go-to buds for a while, very pleased.

reviews.text: This is one of the worst product experiences I've had in a long time. I did a ton of research on the front end of this purchase and understood going in that the battery life on these headphones wasn't exceptional, but I knew I was only going to use them at the gym. I charged them as per the directions and went for a run. The charge lasted 15 minutes. I had this happen several more times and contacted Samsung to get a replacement pair. I do really like the fact that you can slide the headphones back & forth so they rest on your ears properly.  The other thing I really liked is they dont rest directly on your eyes. I have been using earbuds for the past two years, but for various reasons no longer wish to use them. So I ordered SleepPhones, hoping they would eliminate the need for uncomfortable ear buds.  I have tried these for two nights in a row. Both nights I woke up with the cord around my neck; the band had shimmied to the top of my head (read: speakers not where they need to be); and I was sweating from the fleece (maybe I need to wait to review until the temperature has dipped below 80 degrees where I live). Plus, the speakers only offer any significant volume when my phone volume is turned on high--even then, I wish I could get it a bit higher.  I was really hoping these would be a good alternative to earbuds, but I think I will continue to b…

reviews.title: Best Sleep Headphones I've Tried (Update at end of review)
reviews.text: I fall asleep to audiobooks, and have tried a lot of speakers and headphones with mixed results.  My husband bought me these AcousticSheep SleepPhones recently, and what a difference they make!  They're very comfortable - okay, the mediums are a little large for me, but I've found a way to position them so they work perfectly.  The speakers are thin and pliable, so they're comfortable even if you roll over and lie on them, and the sound is pleasant - not too boomy or too shrill, and you can move the headband so you can listen in both ears or only one, if you prefer.  The one catch is that the wires leading out of the headphones are pretty thin, and judging my previous experience using many headsets and speakers in bed, they're going to break inside at some point.  Then I'll either have to order more or perhaps do a little creative wire work and attach new, stronger wires.  I'd be perfect…

reviews.title: Comfortable, but difficult to adjust
reviews.text: These are fairly comfortable, but there is very little tolerance in finding the 'sweet spot' so that you can hear the audio. If the speaker moves only a few millimeters, then the audio is muffled and difficult to hear, if you can hear it at all.  I spend more time trying to nudge the speaker into the right position than anything.  The headband also has a tendency to slip down over my eyes, perhaps because I have a very large head. All in all, these are a neat concept, but just too finicky for realistic use.

reviews.text: These headphones started falling apart and malfunctioning within only days of use! First, the little black cover on one of the earbuds fell out, exposing the metal insides. Then, the sound got significantly quieter on one side, causing the total sound experience to be very imbalanced, favoring one side. Drives me nuts! I thought it might have been related to the cover falling out and messing up the sound seal, so I removed the cover on the other earbud as well (it came out way too easily!) but that didn't solve the problem. The sound is still imbalanced, much louder on one side. It's way too annoying to listen to this way, so I'm gonna have to throw them out.  Oh, and they weren't particularly comfortable either. After about half an hour, my ear canals start hurting. That was unfortunate, because the earbuds really are quite small, but I guess I have really small ears...

reviews.title: I really liked them for sleeping but they died
reviews.text: I wasn’t looking for noise canceling headphone, I used these to listen to meditation music while I sleep. These were perfectly fine for that.  I don’t think they cancel any noise. The sound quality is fine though. However, my husband can hear my headphones if he isn’t also wearing his. The volume buttons were fine.  My one issue is they died after 3 months of use. Other than that I loved them.  But I just expected them to last longer.

reviews.title: Not to be dramatic, but..
reviews.text: This product has been life changing! I am a total night owl and my partner needs to be up at 6:30am. In order to fall asleep earlier, it has always helped me to listen to a podcast, but playing anything out loud makes it hard for my partner to sleep restfully. Regular earbuds would either get lost or tangled in the sheets - so these headphones solved all of my insomnia problems! They are quiet enough to not disturb my partner, and comfortable enough for a side-sleeper like me! They also hold their charge for multiple nights in a row without needing to be plugged in.  Absolutely recommend.

reviews.title: Volume is way too quiet
reviews.text: I’ll start with the pros. The headband is super soft. I love the feel of it and the headphones are very flat which is nice if your a side sleeper. I found the headband to have plenty of stretch and to be very lightweight. I also did not find it to be hot at all. However, I bought this to watch movies in bed without disturbing my hubby and the volume simply is not loud enough. I have it turned up all the way and can barely hear what I am watching. Once you do get to maximum volume the headphones emit an EXTREMELY LOUD BEEP. It startles you and makes me wonder if the beep can be that loud why on earth are the headphones so quiet? They are obviously capable of being much louder. I admit I have not used these for sleeping. If your purpose is to listen to quiet music, a sleep story, or sleep sounds I think the volume will work perfectly for you. If your purpose is to watch movies or listen to…

reviews.title: Comfy and Perfect for My Needs
reviews.text: These are super comfortable and work perfectly for listening to audiobooks, music, podcasts, etc., while lying down. I find these to be perfect for nighttime listening as they are more comfortable than headphones, and earbuds never stay in my ears. I can lie in any position without worrying about the discomfort of headphones or earbuds poking me in the wrong place or digging into my head. The headband is stretchy and soft, and large enough that it doesn't easily slip off. I do wish I could control volume from the headband, the buttons that you would think control volume, only skip forward and backward. But I just set the volume on my device and it works perfectly, loud or low enough to hear, depending on my environment.

reviews.title: Very comfortable for falling asleep
reviews.text: This is the second pair of sleep phones like this that I've bought and I am hooked. I like the cozy comfort of the band around my head and the sound quality is solid. I like to listen to sleepy stories and these allow me to fall asleep on my side with no discomfort. I generally don't keep them on all night -- I wake up and slip them off usually, but it would be fine to sleep with them on all night, if you're lucky enough to sleep all night long!

reviews.title: Excellent sleep headphones
reviews.text: I use this product to block out the sounds of late night video gaming and movie watching in my home so I can get sleep. I turn on a sleep sound and can peacefully rest without the sounds of yelling, explosions, and gunfire keeping me up all night.  They are comfortable and big enough that I can even pull them down over my eyes to block light as well. Charging them is easy and one charge usually lasts me two nights of constant use. I highly recommend!

reviews.title: Best headphones I have ever had
reviews.text: With Bose, you never have to worry about the sound quality.  It is excellent as usual.  The 3 different sized of ear pieces provided allow for a personalized fit.  They stay in place during all sorts of activities (running, yard work, etc..) and the soft earpieces are very comfortable.  The cord is split into 2 pieces which can be very convenient at times.  Without the extension, it works perfectly for an arm/exercise band.  With the extension, you can stick the phone in your pocket, backpack, etc..  and have some cord to spare.  The connection between the extension and the main cord is large and will make the cord feel heavy at times.  My ONLY complaint is that the cord is made of a very "rubbery" material and it tends to catch on itself (if you wind it up when not in use, it is a little tough to untangle it).  Other than that, I love these headphones.  I liked mine so much, I b…

reviews.title: Favorite running headphone, worth the splurge.
reviews.text: I've had these headphones for over 2 years with no complaints. I used to go through headphones on a monthly basis, but Bose provided me with the quality and durability I was looking for with sport headphones. I one time accidentally put these headphones in the washer and dryer, because they were left in my pocket, and they still work with no defects. (Sweat-proof and maybe even waterproof) They are great for staying safe while running or biking outdoors, while still providing excellent Bose sound quality. I like the interchangeable earpieces for the perfect fit and comfort while running. There is no need to readjust or worry about the earpieces falling out or getting yanked out. The versatile cord length was a bonus for less cord hassle, but if this product were to be upgraded I might suggest a flat cord for less tangle during storage.

The silicon support puts just enoughf pressure on your ear to hold the earbud in and not create discomfort. Sound it's decent nothing extraordinary. Now the annoying part; I'm just 5' 11" and cannot use the earbuds wihhout the extension cord without constantly having the speakers pulled out of my ears by the weight of the phone...if I were to add the extension cable the cord becomes to long and  looks ridiculous and clings around things all the time... Bottom line 150$ is way to much for this item

reviews.title: This is BOSE?!! Tell me it isn't so
reviews.text: Pros: 1. Snug fit. It doesn't fall off my ears 2. Cool color. 3. Nice armband 4. Extra extended cord 5. Seems very durable  Con:  1. Definitely not Bose quality sound. Treble is horrible. Lots of revebraring noise. I have used cheaper and $100 earbuds and this one is among the worst when it comes to sound quality. Beats by Dr. Dre beat this by a mile. The sound quality of this is comparable to the stock earbuds that cane with my iPhone 3GS.  I should have taken the advise of the negative reviews. Can anyone recommend a sport headphone with good quality sound? I also tried the blue monster sport immersion headphone - with in line mic - and I had to return it as well because of sub par sound quality. One would think that expensive headphone have excellent sound quality - I was wrong. The new iPhone earbuds have glowing reviews. Anyone tried it yet.

reviews.title: Pass on Bose
reviews.text: Left ear bud stopped working - contacted Bose and since they're out of warranty, the only option they provide is a discount (25%) on a new pair of headphones.  Why would I spend ANOTHER $100 on a pair of ear buds that fail?  Thanks but no thanks.  Very disappointed in both the quality of the product, the customer service and the fact that the would only offer a discount on a new product.  I will never buy another Bose product.  Not worth it.

reviews.title: Avg. headphones, terrible armband - not iPhone 5 compatible
reviews.text: You will have to call Bose and pay and extra $10+ to get the armband made for the 5 - it's the same cheap material that keeps sliding down on your arm. Like others have mentioned before on the sound quality, it sounds "tinny" and lacks little to no bass. The silicone ear pieces are nice and holds the buds in very well.

reviews.title: Semi-professional sound monitoring and video games
reviews.text: I use this to monitor/produce music and play Fortnite. I know it is a weird combination, but I wanted a simple solution: basically, good headphones that happen to have a microphone on them. I like this better than my Audio-Technica ATH-M20x professional studio headphones. The Audio-Technica are good and flat like I want, but the bass level is much too low for most modern realistic playback. These CM 500s have a more realistic (but less flat) bass. Much better for my mixing. As far as Fortnite, the mic swivels down and I can ask my son to come revive me. That's pretty much what happens when we play together: I get killed, and he carries me through the game. I'm what he would call a "bot". Anyway, I like that the microphone swings up and down without needing to bend it. I expect it to last longer without breaking with that design. I'm very happy with these headphones.

reviews.title: Don't waste your money
reviews.text: Horrible!!! I bought them for studying and to also bring with me for an overseas trip. They not only do NOT reduce any noise but they are extremely uncomfortable to wear for longer then 30 mins. I wouldn't pay $1.00 for these.

reviews.title: Avoid these. Non existent noise cancelling, uncomfortable. Can find better for the money.
reviews.text: Got these at a kiosk before a 5 hour flight. I'm really not a big fan of ear bud earphones, especially for a long flight. Previously had a pair of earphones in the same pricepoint that had decent noise cancelling abilities, and thought these would be ok.  First off, the sound is pretty decent, good bass, and overall good sound. The nice cancelling function is non existent. You may as well not even turn the feature on, it does nothing.  Second, they are not that comfortable. AS they are a bit too small after an hour or so they begin pressing on your ears and it gets uncomfortable.  I wish I never bought them

reviews.title: Only cancels about 5% of noise
reviews.text: I thought "They're cheap, why not?" I expected that Sony would at least make a semi-descent product, but I was wrong. They only cut out about 5% of ambient noise. I tested them in a lot of different environments and it didn't perform well under any circumstance.  I compared them to a pair of low-end headphones ($20) to set a baseline, see below.  Test: In flight - no noticeable difference between each pair While driving - slightly better muffling of midrange noise, but slight (2% better) Fan on high & low - slightly better canceling of low freq noise (2% better) In crowed auditorium - slight better muffling (1% better)  They barely did any better than the cheap-o, non-noisecanceling, over the ear headphones I got for half the price.  The biggest thing I noticed is that the very little amount of noise that was actively cancelled was replaced fully by a hissing sound. This made the headset…

reviews.title: They feel great. I'm not sure if you can get anything ...
reviews.text: They feel great. I'm not sure if you can get anything better for this price.  The colors seem random but they actually look pretty cool. The sound is great!

reviews.title: No noise cancellation, poorly made. Stay away.
reviews.text: These headphones have no noise cancellation. The only thing that happens when you turn the switch on is the volume is reduced. I purchased these in the Miami airport yesterday, I had left my shure in ear, that actually work, at home. I was simply amazed at how falsely these are advertised. I cannot return them because I am now in NC and Sonys warranty only allows for exchange or repair. Replacing a bad product with a bad product is not a solution. Spur of the moment purchase bit me. The fellow next to me on the plane had a Bose set and wanted to hear these. He was also shocked. You can actually hear everything just as well with the headphones on your head or off your head turned on or off. Terrible product. There should be a class action suit against Sony for false advertising.

reviews.title: Complete Waste of Money
reviews.text: Purchased these while in Japan. I wish I would have saved the packaging. I tried using them on a flight to Hawaii. I would estimate that about 10% of the ambient noise was reduced, total, when turned on. I tried watching a movie on my tablet and couldn't hear any sound from the movie whatsoever. I actually thought the headphones weren't plugged in because there was a total lack of sound. I then plugged them into an iPod and couldn't hear any music whatsoever. I arrived at home and threw them in the garbage. Had I kept the packaging, I would have returned them. Even a few dollars in store credit would be worth more than these headphones. I figured since they were Sony, they'd be decent. I guess you get what you pay for. I got a $40 donation to my garbage bin.

reviews.title: hissing sound when active in a silent room
reviews.text: i have a few pair of active noise canceling headphones. this set has an issue, hissing when on. i did not take them on a jet, so i can not fully comment on normal condition use but i use my other ones in the office to block out noise sometimes and none of them hiss background noise like these do. i did not wear them long enough to comment on other topics like extended wear comfort, ear cup comfort etc. first and foremost they must block noise, these created noise where there was none. i will also point out my pair was rectified, not new.

reviews.title: noise cancelling non-existent
reviews.text: These do not actually cancel any noise.  The sound quality isn't awful, but again, they are not actually noise canceling, and for the money, you can get a better pair of headphones, without the non-existent noise cancelling, that will do a better job of isolating noise.

description: True high-fidelity requires reproduced sound to be as close as possible to the sound of a live performance. Etymotic's earphones have the highest response accuracy of all in-ear earphones. ER4P-T is intended for sound engineers and audiophiles in constant motion and can be used with portable devices without an additional amplifier. The ER4P-T has 10dB greater output at high frequencies and 13dB greater output at low frequencies than the ER4S. The higher sensitivity of the ER4P-T has made it the most popular in ear monitor on the market. Included with every pair of ER4P-T in ear monitors is an industry-exclusive channel matching compliance graph signed by the Etymotic engineer who precision matched and custom tuned the balanced-armature drivers. Every pair of ER4P-T earphones is assembled and tuned in the United States.

reviews.title: A decade with the ER4S
reviews.text: My pair of ER4S is about to turn 10 years old.  I thought enough time had passed to finally write an Amazon review.  Heh heh.  I was the second person on Headwize.com (before there was a Head-Fi) to get them and post comments.  I've used a seemingly endless number of headphones over the years: Sennheiser HD580, Denon 950, Sony 7509, Sony 7506, Sony MDR600, Koss ESP950 electrostatics, about half a dozen Koss dynamic headphones, one pair of Stax, Ixos' top of the line 1001, Pioneer's top of the line DJing headphones, two models of AKG studio headphones, JVC's former top of the line (only available direct), HN-7506, both versions of the Extreme Isolation UR-29, and a seemingly unending number of cheapos bundled with music players.  Whew!  So what do I think about the Etymotic Research ER4S?  I think it is frankly without peer amongst those cans I've heard.  It is flat, transparent, resolved…

reviews.title: 10 year user endorses Etymotic ER4S
reviews.text: I got my first ER4S set 10 years ago and a second set a couple of years later to ensure that I would not be without some ER4S. Both sets are fine after all this time and use but I want a 3rd set!  IMO, the single best thing about the ER4S is their durability. I've literally owned dozens of earphone sets and all but the Etymotics that I continued to use eventually bit the dust. Usually it was a cord discontinuity most likely very near the plug. I've replaced countless cables and plugs, pulling out my soldering iron and rummaging through my collection of parts. Once I got the Etymotics I had put all that behind me. Not once have I had a problem with the ER4S cables or plugs. The only times I have experienced cutout of a channel was when a filter got clogged, which has happened a few times. It's pretty simple to replace a filter, and they give you extra filters and a tool to remove the old …

reviews.title: I Took the Pepsi Challenge
reviews.text: Pulp Fiction Metaphorical Comparison...  LANCE (to Vincent):  "...Now this is Panda [ER-6], from Mexico. Very good stuff. This is Bava [ER-6i], different, but equally good. And this is Choco [ER-4P] from the Hartz Mountains of Germany....but this one...(pointing to the Choco)...this one's a little more expensive...But when you shoot it, you'll know where that extra money went..."  IMHO, the same can be said about the ER4P's: You'll know where the extra money went. Spending the extra $$$ is well worth it. Yes, I've purchased all three (for my iPod) and settled on the BBME (biggest-best-most EXPENSIVE). My hunt for a fantastic IE set has finally come to an end. Keep in mind, before experimenting with the Etymotic series, I've previously owned Sony's (MDR-EX71SL & MDR-EX81SL) and onto Sennheiser (CX300's). If you're on a budget and like lots of bass, the CX300 top both Sony models.  As far …

reviews.title: Good, but still not great bass.
reviews.text: After reading all the reviews, I took a chance and bought the 4P. The presence is simply amazing and they're a lot more comfortable than I had anticipated. And they are loud! I've been searching for earphones that delivered isolation, a well-rounded sound and comfort, and thought I'd found them in the 4P model. I had previously owned the Etymotic 6i and found the bass lacking. The 4P delivers more bass, but less than I had expected. I have been using Sony's MDR-NC11A for about a year and, to my ears, they produce less presence than the 4P but seem to deliver a "bassier" yet not muddy bass sound, and cost about half the price of the 4P.  PS - the 4P model shown on Amazon with the red and blue earpieces has been replaced by pure a black model, making distinguishing the left from the right very difficult.

reviews.title: Crystal clear sound but light on bass
reviews.text: I've owned Etymotic ER4P and ER4S earphones for over a decade now. These are among the best sounding earphones or headphones I've ever heard, especially for classical music. They are somewhat dry and analytical but not harsh at all. The sound is absolutely crystal clear. Bass is light but very nice sounding. I actually prefer these to my Westone ES5 custom IEMs which cost four times as much as the Etymotics. Isolation is great with the triple flange tips, so long as you have a good seal. The isolation is sufficient to listen to quiet classical music on airplanes. One thing to note is they get more comfortable over time, and if you moisten the tips before putting them in your ear they feel better. Overall, I highly recommend these earphones. However, if you're looking for a bass heavy presentation you should probably look elsewhere.

reviews.title: Best headphone/ear phones I have ever owned
reviews.text: At first I did not like them at all and thought they were fakes.  I thought the sound was tinny or it was very muffled.  The problem was that I was not putting them in my ears correctly.  There is a video on how to do that.  You have to open your mouth and pull back your ear a little.  Now that I have learned how to put them in properly I am enjoying the unbelievable sound from these in ear phones.  I use them to play PC video games like counter strike and starcraft.  I HEAR EVERYTHING!  I know where players are because I can hear them.  The ear buds are that accurate.  When I use my other ear buds at work(I used to really enjoy them) they just don't compare anymore, not even close!  The price tag on these are high, but in my opinion... well worth it.

reviews.title: Just ok
reviews.text: Cord way too long. No way to skip song or pause tunes from headphone cord. Even their headphones half the price have this function. Sounds great, but would have easily given up a bit of quality to be able to pause music without removing phone from my pocket.  Update: Finally retired these headphones. I went with RHA and from my untrained ear, I think the RHA's blow away Etymotic. Guess I just like the bass!  Couple more points. The main cord gets twisted like an orange 50 ft extension cords. It is so thick and not very bendable. Also, the earpieces get deformed over time. They are squished when stored and come out misshapen. This never happened on my HF series and had those for years. I really gave these headphones the benefit of the doubt... have been a huge Etymotic fan over the years. Maybe these are designed more for in-studio/inside use??

reviews.title: Great earbuds, but not all purpose
reviews.text: I love my ER4Ps but they aren't for everything.  The sound is great, and I love the noise canceling.  If it was just this then I'd give it the maximum number of stars.  Issues: I only wear ear buds to work out, so when anything taps the cord it acts like a microphone sending noise to the bud.  They do not stand up to constant working out.  I've been through 2 sets already, each one lasted about 2 years before a wire disconnects from the green barrel (both failed in exact same spot).  When the 1st set broke I sent it in to be repaired, which cost right about what a brand new pair would cost.  I'm pretty sure they didn't even bother repairing it and just sent me a new pair.  When the 2nd set broke I tried to take the barrel apart to reconnect them which was a terrible idea :).  Summary: sitting still -- effing awesome. running -- lots of *thump* *thump* *thump* from the cord bouncing on yo…

reviews.title: another pair of Etys
reviews.text: Not much to say.  This is my second set in 7 years.  Love 'em. Tried the $99 Bose - didn't like 'em so gave them to my kid. If you're a bass freak you will not like these.  If you're an audiophile who wants to hear all of the subtle tones - as if you were listening live - then I believe you"ll like them a lot. Only bad thing is noise if they rub on your clothes.  I hook the cords over my ear and run the main cord down my back.  That works great for yard work, skiing, biking, etc. I always use them when traveling by airplane - makes the world go away.

reviews.title: Accurate monitors for sure.  Highly Recommend.
reviews.text: Hello all, I purchased a set of Etymotic ER-4Ps around a month ago. ( September 2009 )  I have listened to a wide variety of music from a few different sources.  Primary music focus for very critical listening: Movie scores/Classical/Jazz/Psy-Trance. Sources include PC/Laptop/iPhone/Amplifier.  These in ear monitors allow a lot of details to come through.  They do a nice job of isolating ambient noise.  They will also let you hear every single tick and crackle in a cheap PC integrated sound card.  On a nicer PC sound card or real amplifier they sound great.  They are efficient enough to play very well from an iPhone.  ( I need to use an adapter as they will not fit direct to first gen iPhone )  I have listened to the James Horner score to Sneakers countless times since the score was released.  I know its details better than any other album.  It is my own reference point.  In my home ster…

reviews.text: If you are like me, you are struggling through the various reviews to divine what the review considers great sound and how these compare to the real world (versus a recording engineer loving their URI's all mid-range.)  In most cars, I would configure the audio system (on a -5 to +5 system) Treble +5, Mid 0 to -5, and Bass +5.  I believe at low volume, a system should give you the dynamics of sitting in front of an orchestra, not just acoustic guitar and voice. Pros: -Fantastic sound These give very clear, bright, life-like sound, (This may be a problem for those of you who want deep bass, as some is lost, or at least not amplified as it is in Beats by Dre, and that type of bud). -Great fit, great options for ear tips. -Narrow diameter driver channel is less painful after long use compared to wider channel ear buds  Cons: -Stick straight out of the ear canals - can't sleep in them or wear under a beanie, and any pull on the cables really torques in your ears! -Picks up wind - the braided cable and the part of the bud sticking from the ear both pick up wind noise. reviews.title: Excellent sound and confort
reviews.text: I just got mine and was worried after purchase due to so many bad reviews about SRS and NoiseGard quality plus the low volume. I tend to agree with SRS... it sounds worse, so keep it off... the volume goes down and spatial sound is not noticed. However, Noisegard does an excellent job for it is real purpose... it is not build to eliminate all kinds of noise, but those constant and of background like air-conditioning devices, airplanes and my grandmother when sleeps :) for those noisetypes NG 2.0 simply rocks... maybe Bose is better but not so better as you would avoid to buy. That being said, it could be cheaper (That is why i do not give 5 stars). Remember that not only batteries are replaceble by user but it uses the same as other models... for me that was priceless as i also have the MM-400, so if one battery dies i can reuse the one in MM-400.

reviews.title: Great sound, battery life OK
reviews.text: Great sound, battery life OK, I would purchase a spare battery if you intend to use these for a long period of time.

reviews.title: Decent headphone for traveling
reviews.text: This is a very decent set of headphones for traveling. I bought these as an "upgrade" to my old pair of Bose because of the noise cancellation feature and the sound quality. While the noise cancellation on these headphones is not 100%, it is more than sufficient for airplane travel and keeps out most of the background vibration, muffles unwanted conversation, crying babies etc.  It has an added feature called SRS that makes the sound a bit crisper. This is especially useful when the noise cancellation feature is engaged, as this can be lost when the background noise is loudest.  It has a rechargeable battery that is more than sufficient to do a long haul overseas flight. It charges on a standard USB phone charger. The earphones also have a built in volume feature and bluetooth connectivity for wireless use if you want to run it off your phone. One of my favorite features is a &#3…

reviews.title: Very nice headphones. Bought as a Christmas gift for my ...
reviews.text: Very nice headphones. Bought as a Christmas gift for my daughter to take on a recent holiday travel. She really likes the sounds, the fit and battery time. I tried them out and was not surprised to find that these headphones were excellent. The sound is very clear, crisp and detailed--just what I have come to expect from Sennheiser. Everything fits fairly nicely into the included travel case. I have purchased other Sennheiser products and would highly recommend. My other option was Bose noice-cancelling bluetooth headphones. However, based on other reviews between the Senheiser and Bose, coupled with my experience with both, I chose these. Don't think you would go wrong with either brand, but I trend towards these based on my experience. Hope this helps.

reviews.title: Recommended
reviews.text: Great sound.  Strangely, I have difficulty pairing it with my iPhone to use the bluetooth feature.  It takes a few tries.  I don't understand why; I have two pair of the Sennheiser MM 100 bluetooth headphones and they pair easily.  Otherwise they have great sound.  This is my first pair of noise canceling headphones and I'm finding that feature quite useful.  As some other reviewers mentioned, the loudest setting is still not super loud, just barely loud enough for me. I wish there was a way to increase the volume a bit more.

reviews.title: IQ HOME ENTERTAINMENT warrenty support has been worthless
reviews.text: the warranty support from the seller  IQ HOME ENTERTAINMENT has been worthless.  they asked me to return a defective battery to them for replacement a couple months ago but the only action is the same old repeat emails about the manufacturer can't provide them a battery.  the headphones actually sound great so I gave up on IQ HOME ENTERTAINMENT and just ordered a battery which came right away.

reviews.title: Only one complaint -- loud is not very loud
reviews.text: These travel headphones sound stunning. I'm used to listening to music through a lot of noise. Having a backdrop of silence, and pure music on top of it, makes a world of difference. While I've mainly used the wire connection, I've tried the Bluetooth wireless connection as well, and did not notice any difference in the sound quality. Both sound superb.  The headphones come with a travel case and a battery charger. It all fits together compactly, yet the headphones are easy to pop out and put on, and can be worn in comfort for several hours.  My only complaint is that loud is not very loud. Maybe I'm doing something wrong--the headphones are not pure plug-and-play, and I misplaced the manual and have been too lazy to track down instructions online. Even with the sound being a little softer than I would like, these headphones make music a lot better.

The sound quality is about the same as I have experienced with earbuds.  You can move the ear pieces around inside the headband to get them where you want them.  They are also removable to wash the band.  It is winter now so I cannot say if they are hot in warmer weather.

reviews.title: Great for Travel and Kids!
reviews.text: I bought these for my 10 year old (he has large head) for iPad use in the car. We've gone through two or three pairs of regular over-the-ear headphones in the past year or two. I think we've finally found a winner! Sound quality is good, quality of the materials seems good and, best of all, they can get smashed in the seat pocket, stuffed in a backpack, sat on or tossed around the car without damage! He can even fall asleep in them and not be uncomfortable. They do make his hair a little crazy but definitely not a concern for a child. :) Highly recommend.

reviews.title: Comfortable!
reviews.text: These are as advertise and very comfortable, I do get a headache when I wear them, but I think that's just because I get tension headaches very easily. I didn't read the description correctly as it only applies to certain softwares.

reviews.title: Love these!!!!
reviews.text: I absolutely LOVE these headphones.  They are a little big (which also keeps them from being uncomfortable) but what an amazing way to sleep with headphones without the pain of ear buds or the discomfort of bulky headphones.  The material is lightweight and not hot. The cord is super long which is nice when you move around without pulling your phone off the bedside table.  Highly recommend.  Sound quality is good not great but you can hear clearly.

reviews.title: Best Sleep Headphones I’ve Found
reviews.text: I think I have tried every pair of sleep headphones on Amazon and here I am back again with my very first pair. I even bought a wireless charger so I can use these wired headphones with my phone while it charges. If CozyPhones would make a headband with a little more padding and offer a Bluetooth version of the phones, ideally with volume control in the headset, they would be perfect. I’m still going to up my rating to five stars, because even though my princess-and-the-pea ear lobes are sometimes still angered by these speakers, and I do very occasionally pull my phone off my nightstand with the wire, they are the best I’ve found. I probably won’t bother trying any other brand of sleep headphones unless they can prove the speakers are as thin as CozyPhones.

reviews.title: Great Product
reviews.text: Lightweight and easy to adjust headphones to fit exactly where my ears are. Very comfortable; barely able to feel the speakers when lying on my side. Good sound quality. Husband says he cannot hear anything -- I was worried about sound bleeding through, but this is not the case.  My only complaint is that the fabric makes my head warm, but that is only a very minor issue. I heartily recommend these headphones.

reviews.title: So happy I ordered these! Highly recommended.
reviews.text: Exactly what I wanted! Very lightweight and comfortable for this side-sleeper's use, and the sound quality is surprisingly good. I'll  order again for sure. The only recommendation I'd have is to make the band adjustable; it's a little large, but works just fine anyway. I'd definitely recommend this CozyPhones product to anyone who might ask.

reviews.title: If you have to wear headphones for work, try these.
reviews.text: I moved from the Plantronics to the Sennheiser and so far, it's been a win for me. The primary difference between the Plantronics and the Sennheiser is the lack of the weak link on the cord. Where the cord plugs into the dongle went intermittent on two Plantronics headsets.  The Sennheiser avoids this by eliminating the cord. The headset can connect via BT to the phone and via a USB dongle in my laptop to the computer. This eliminates the weak point but means the headset is not charging while in use. That problem is basically eliminated by the super super super fast charging on the stand. I can plug the headset into the stand for 15 or 20 minutes and get a full day's use out of it.  I'm pretty much not finding anything concerning about the Sennheiser. You do have to pop off a piece of the earphone on the mic side to perform updates but that's not really a problem. Also, I'm a bit clumsy …

reviews.title: Lightweight and easy to configure
reviews.text: I use this for work conference calls and what I like the most is that they reconnect automatically. I have had many blue tooth devices that make you re-sync every time you restart your system - not these. They are very comfortable and easy to configure. Much better than being tethered!

reviews.title: They work great!
reviews.text: I use these headphones all the time for webinars and they do a really good job. I love the sound quality and I really love the fact that they're wireless.  The only issue I have is trying to make them work while I'm listening to music. I can't seem to make them connect then. I'm sure there has to be a way, but I haven't figured it out.

reviews.title: Works great with IP phone, very lightweight.
reviews.text: Sound quality is great.  Pairs with the Cisco Communicator IP phone that I use at work without a hitch.  But I can't figure out how to listen to music when not on the phone: it seems to be attached ONLY to the phone.  The headset is very light weight, so no big groove in the top of my head, or squashed ears, but I have to be a little careful because if I turn my head real fast, they slip, or slide off completely.

reviews.title: Super Sensative
reviews.text: Works well and has a very decent battery life. The only thing is that if you toggle between a phone and a laptop, and ask these headphones to choose when switching from a call to a conference call or zoom session, the headphones will do that back and forth. This gets to be a battle between which bluetooth signal is going to win. So you'll hear the message: "phone 1 disconnected" more often that you want to. The solution is to shutoff the bluetooth feature on either your phone or laptop, when not using either.

reviews.title: Perfect for what it is intended for
reviews.text: I bought this specifically for conference calls. I'm in noisy environments often and needed something that would make my voice clear to other people on the call. This cancels out all background noise and allows me to speak with clarity, regardless of the noisy environments I may be in.  Battery life is great, charges fast, and the headphones are very light which make these comfortable to wear for long calls.  No, these are not for listening to music and you shouldn't expect audiophile quality sounds from them. But what they're built for, which are canceling out noise in voice calls, they're A+

reviews.title: the quality of voice is good but noise cancelling is not good and volume is low on macbook
reviews.text: I needed a solid headset for the office and decided to try this headset.  It was connected to a new MacBook Pro and didn't work out well.  The volume was too low to hear anything and the noise cancelling didn't work that well.  I was still able to hear a lot of background noise and the only way I know this is because I made a recording using the headset and then ran the output through the MacBook speakers.  I would not recommend this headset for Mac users as there's no software available and the volume is bad.  One positive note is that the quality of the microphone is good and I would have kept it but the noise cancelling and the volume are bad.

As someone who occasionally wears glasses, the pressure does end up giving me a slight headache after 45 mins when pushing the frames into my temples. But when I wear contacts, no issues whatsoever. Over the last few months, I'd occasionally pull them out and have another listen to see if my ears or brain had adjusted to their sound... Nope...  UNTIL I pulled off the pleather covers on the ear cups, and removed the foam and VOILA, they were transformed from "ugh" to "not bad for $10!" reviews.title: You Get What You Pay For
reviews.text: I wasn't convinced that I needed to pay Sony or Bose prices to get a good wireless headset, so I bought a couple value products to give them a try, at $40 and $110.  Truly a waste of time and effort.  I won't list their bad attributes beyond poor sound, build quality, fit and noise cancellation.  But the takeaway is that quality costs money.  Get out your checkbook.

reviews.title: Avoid.  Too much money for a far from perfect design.  Too easy to pinch hand.
reviews.text: I would never recommend these.  While they work functionally well, they are super annoyingly dangerous.  I constantly pinch my fingers in the area where you fold and unfold.  They even have a warning but you can’t avoid it.  They also fold down much more bulkier than my other headset.  For the price I would expect a way better design.

reviews.title: Very impressed with these headphones, best I've ever owned
reviews.text: After having used these headphones for months I can say they're the best I've had the opportunity to try for their price point I'm impressed. Ended up paying $79 in used condition for them at the time, received them in what seemed like brand new condition. The noise cancelling is fantastic, there's a few instances it won't block out everything but it does block most, such as cars, fans, people talking, etc.  The side touch feature is my favorite part, though. Being able to skip a song, go replay one, pause/play and answer calls on the fly is fantastic. The overall sound quality is great, the ability to use the Sony app to play with the equalizer is also fun. Ambient sound is great for listening to music and holding a conversation, and the microphone seems to work good for calls as I haven't had anyone complain about voice quality yet. Overall I'd give these an amazing rating and would su…

reviews.title: Great sound quality, no leakage of sound to annoy my wife :)
reviews.text: I'm the wife and I bought these for my husband to use when I need to relax rather than hearing the TV, etc.  at screaming level.  His last pair leaked, and the whispers I caught were pretty annoying.  He can now watch anything at any time without me wanting to throttle him, so it was a win/win purchase.  :)

reviews.title: Insane value headphones. Sold my B&O H4 for these.
reviews.text: I had a pair of B&O H4 that weren't bad, but I bought these as a second set and my dad and I, whom are somewhat audiophiles, did back to back testing. They were near even - if anything an edge to the Sony. The difference? You can pick these up for $100-150 and the B&O were in the $350 range. Anyways - apples to oranges. Noise cancelling is very good. Not the best outdoors especially with wind or at the gym if you walk past an industrial size fan. The bluetooth connection can get funky in very cold weather for some reason too (I set to best effort vs best quality to help). Comfort is amazing, design is very good and hasn't aged in my opinion. They're significantly heavier than the XM3 or XM4, but if I'm not comparing them to anything, I've never felt like they were too heavy or uncomfortable. If I wear them for hours straight while being active, my ears will start to get warm, but that's …

reviews.title: Best Bluetooth sound canceling headphones out there for my money
reviews.text: These are with a question the best sound canceling headphones that you can get out there today. Sound canceling is very effective, but one of the features I find the most useful is actually it’s Bluetooth microphone accuracy.   I use these frequently on conference call (as I work from home) and these are the ones that everyone comments as having the best sound quality. Especially on the other end.   Another major plus is battery life. They seem to go forever on a charge, will easily last me the entire day.  I had a previous set for a couple of years and only bought a second set because my wife washed the first one. :-) Can I recommend highly enough.

reviews.title: Incredible Sound
reviews.text: These headphones are perfect for me. I'm not a huge basshead, love my boom bap songs and all but I've always preferred ACCURACY over something that'll make my brain tingle. That's the h.ear on 2's. If you want an experience that shows you what the song is suppose to sound like then these are for you. Don't get me wrong, they definitely serve well on the bass end, perfectly so in my opinion. For those that prefer the bass, along with other EQ's, is adjustable via the sony app.  Noise cancelling is good. It's not the best-of-the-best but when my music is playing I can't hear anything around me which is all that matters to me.

reviews.title: Save your money and time — buy something else
reviews.text: Do you enjoy buying products that don’t work? Do you have time to take out of your busy day to return items you order online? Well if you answered “yes” to either question, these are the earbuds for you!  But if you’re like me and just want things to work as advertised and would prefer not to waste your time, I suggest you look elsewhere. These earbuds look nice but feel a little cheap, which isn’t a shock given the price. The problem is, they don’t work. At least they didn’t for me. You can hear fine, but if you try to use the microphone to talk to anyone, you’re out of luck. So, back they go.

reviews.title: Exactly what I needed
reviews.text: I’ve used headsets previously for work calls and my ears start to hurt after prolonged use. Plus they are bulky in my work bag for days I might go into the office. I never wanted to spend a bunch of money on something either. These are comfortable and small. They come with both regular USB and USB-C connectors making it super convenient to work with. I only use them for calls and trainings and the sound quality has been great. Haven’t listened to music so I don’t know how they perform with heavy bass. I’ve been delighted with these earbuds and have been recommending them to colleagues.

reviews.title: Comfortable, GREAT sound and noise cancellation
reviews.text: I did a lot of research and read loads of reviews before finally settling and purchasing a pair of these.  I use them every day at the gym & they plug right into my elliptical & I LOVE them.  First of all, I have small ears and I am usually in pain or totally uncomfortable with the ear buds within 20 minutes or less.  The different sized ear bud options that come with these allowed me to select the smallest ones, which I push into my ear, and I have sound cancellation so that I only hear what I want on either my ipod or the Elliptical's TV.  That helps since the gym has lots of background noise.  I did have the 'thumping' from me moving quickly on the elliptical, so I put the headphones on with the cables around the back of my head, and that totally prevents it.  I will totally buy these again if I need another pair, but I have already bought 2 pairs as gifts!  The cords are really nice …

Very happy with my purchase- Highly recommend!!  *********UPDATE  So they did work great, still do, HOWEVER, the little plastic came off like a month after using them. So they sound good but they are really cheaply made. Guess you get what you pay for :S.

It makes carrying around the earphones that much safer. Usually that is how I broke most of my other earphones. But I am very happy with the quality of this product so far. Highly recommended for the price.

reviews.title: adidas RPT-01 Sport Headphones
reviews.text: I wear headphones when I work outside, spring through fall. By the end of fall, that year’s pair is pretty nasty from hours of daily use and me sweating in them. Of course I clean them, but it’s impossible to *really* deep clean headphones.  So that’s what drew me to the adidas RPT-01 Sport Headphones: the description advertises “removable, washable knitted ear cushions.” Knit covers I can wash? Hooray!  But there’s no instructions in the box on how to remove the ear covers or the headband. It turns out the cushions aren’t as removable as advertised.The ear cups twist off the headphones (a gentle, counter-clockwise turn), but there’s still an inner plastic rim. I thought I’d be able to wash the knitted cover itself, but nope. And I nearly tore the cover trying to figure out how to remove it, until I found the manual online.  I can’t figure out how to get the headband all the way off. The…

reviews.title: Nice headphones, expensive, small
reviews.text: These are nice looking and sounding headphones but they are small and, in my opinion, overpriced.  More about the headphones.  - Sound quality. The have some nice mid-low and low end oomph. There is some crispness there that masks some of the high end lack of articulation. They aren’t terrible on the high end, respectable actually, but for the price I would have expected more. - Price. List for these are higher by a third than what I feel is reasonable. At a $150 I feel these aren’t quite worth it  at $100 these would be a much easier recommendation. - Design. These look and feel pretty good. The charcoal heather design is very sporting and really fits what Adidas was going for here.  I also like the small reflective details in the 3 stripe logo. - Set-up. Pairing was a cinch with my iPhone. (Though at this point in Bluetooth tech that is expected.) - Sports features.  Water resistant an…

reviews.title: ALMOST perfect
reviews.text: These  adidas RPT-01 Bluetooth Sport On-Ear Headphones are almost perfect.  First let me tell you why I had to take off a star. The fabric on the headphones is almost identical to their shoes, and after a while is actually irritating to the skin. On top of that, because these aren't a complete over the ear headphones and just sit on the ear just adds to this discomfort.  Other than that these are SO sharp. They look great but I have to tell you the sound quality really surprised me!  I am definitely happy with these!

reviews.text: I ordered the ‘adidas RPT-01 Bluetooth Sport On-Ear Headphones - New’ for review as I am a sucker for wireless headphones. My initial thoughts right out of the box were that these are solidly built, lightweight and beautifully designed headphones. They look and feel "high end". I’ve now had these for nearly a month and feel that I am ready to share more.  First I would like to comment on the fact that these are touted as “Sport” headphones and my idea of “Sport” headphones are more of the "in-ear" earbuds, which fit much more securely and do better in the “head-shake” tests. I honestly don’t see these working for anything more extreme than jogging. Don’t get me wrong, they do fit well and are lightweight but just don’t quite pass the “head-shake” test haha. reviews.title: They're great for the gym
reviews.text: I'm in love with these for the gym.  I don't find earbuds comfortable in general, but these are somewhat better than average, so for people who don't have issues usually, they'll be great.  I do audio classes from Aaptiv. Some involve a lot of jumping and bouncing. Some, like yoga, involve putting the headphones in an unusual position (think downward dog and the headphones sort of danging). They stay. No matte what, they stay. I run. They stay in. I do cat-cows. They stay in. I love not having to keep adjusting them.  The sound quality is excellent.

reviews.title: I am really enjoying these headphones
reviews.text: First of all my experience has always been good with Plantronics.  They make first class merchandise as my experience over the years has shown.  I was glad to have a chance to review their headphones as I was pretty sure it would be a good product. The Bluetooth connected immediately.  No problems at all. The magnetic catch on the earphones keeps them together.  I really like that. They sit flush on your ears and are discreet.  Very comfortable wearing them and listening for long periods of time. You get eight hours of listening with the noise cancelling feature enabled, without that you get 10 hours approximately on a charge. You receive 3.5 mm of cable for corded listening. I recommend these without reservation.
