reviews.title: These are NOT bone conduction headphones
reviews.text: The only thing these headphones have going for it is a respectable battery life.  Everything else is just a disappointment, unfortunately.  I've been trying to find a good but affordable pair bone conduction headphones because I keep a headphone on my head almost all day while I work and write my code but I end up shutting the rest of the family out and miss half of the conversations going on in the house.  When I discovered open ear bone conduction, it seemed to be the perfect solution.  So far, I have not found a good one.  The specific problems of this pair of headphones is that it is not bone conduction.  It is a simple pair of speakers set next to your ear.  There is no bone shaking going on.  With bone conduction, you can put in earplugs and still hear the audio fairly clearly, with these, the sound is clearly muffled and hard to make out.  In addition, there is a half-second delay…

reviews.text: [[VIDEOID:308036344b0adb926e6495d7c8a38b13]] These are nice.  love that they don’t go in your ear but sit outside.  Means that you can hear the world around you.  It’s good sound quality but I feel safer using these because it still allows you to hear around you.  Overall they’re nice and it’s easy to use. I like them

reviews.title: It is uncomfortable to wear and I have to pay for returning
reviews.text: The vibration pieces are very thick and the portion over ears pinches my ears.  It is pretty uncomfortable to wear the earphones.  I have to pay for returning shipping makes it very inconvenient.  Amazon only refund $3.99 for return shipping.

reviews.title: Not Bone Conduction
reviews.text: I have tried a few "bone conduction" headphones. The way you can tell if they are bone conduction is because you can still hear the sound with earplugs in. These are not. These are speakers directed at your ears. There re much better actual bone conduction sets available at this price point.

reviews.title: Excellent choice for water sports and for safety purposes
reviews.text: PROS  1. These headphones are really different in appearance from regular earbud-type headphones, but they are oddly attractive in their design.  2. They are great for swimming in a pool or in any outdoor body of water, because they are extensively waterproof. They can be submerged to a depth of 20 meters (65 feet). This means they can be used for snorkeling and scuba diving.  3. They do not fit in the ear. Instead, sound is conducted through the cheekbone. I don’t understand the science behind this, but it does work.  4. They have the ability to play audio files from a built-in 32GB memory card.  5. When not submerged in water, they have Bluetooth capability. When underwater, you have to use the built-in memory card.  6. This type of headphones are outstanding for safety purposes. People who walk, jog or run on public sidewalks or, especially, on deserted park paths/trails, are taking a…

reviews.title: Good quality for the price - good for work settings
reviews.text: We are using these for our resort staff, we all use radios but don't want the guests to be able to hear what we're saying.  This is a great, price friendly option.  The overall quality is lacking a bit but it's difficult to complain because these are priced reasonably.  They fit fairly well on different head sizes.  We are just using them for communication, not for music.  The sound quality is very good, as is the microphone.  I will never go back having something in our ears, the open ear function is the best, especially in a work environment.  It's so annoying to be talking to someone and they can't hear you because they have an ear bud stuck in their ear!  These eliminate that problem.  They charge up quickly and have been lasting thru an entire shift.  I'm very happy with them.

reviews.title: Less than the sum of its parts
reviews.text: Some products turn out to be better than the sum of their parts. Some go in the opposite direction. This is one of them. While in theory this could have made a great bluetooth earbud headset, it has inexcusable issues for a 2014 product that as of review date costs around seventy bucks. The biggest issues:  1) bluetooth pairing and connectivity. It feels like using one of those old Bluetooth 2.x no-name-brand devices of a few years ago. Pairing doesn't work the first time. Typically you have to turn things on/off until it finally makes a connection. Reconnection with previously paired devices is not always smooth either. Music playback has occasional issues (eg quick resume after a pause sometimes gets you a few seconds of jitteriness before it starts playing normally again). The previous three Jabra bluetooth devices I used were much better than this, even lower priced ones. The same ph…

reviews.title: I've heard better sound quality on a disposable headset you get on ...
reviews.text: Seriously these are a complete joke for $50+, I've heard better sound quality on a disposable headset you get on an airline. The people who gave these anything more than 1 star are probably used to listening to music through a wire and a tin can.

reviews.title: Found alot better for $20 bux...level u $30...syllabus $20 and jarv joggers $15 all on amazon
reviews.text: Not very loud...very uncomfortable...hurts back of ears and canal...ear hooks come off/detachable and very easy to lose...10$ to replace...plus they don't attach to clothes or anything so you can drop them and not even know

reviews.title: Not useful for gym or anything, really.
reviews.text: They fall out of your ears constantly (the square part the earbuds connect to are too heavy) - don't have a very long battery life.  The plastic guides that are meant to loop around the back of your ears don't fit well either.

reviews.title: Still too loud on the lowest setting!!
reviews.text: Just bought these earbuds recently to use with my iPhone 5C and iPod Touch.  The volume, on the lowest setting, is still too loud.  I've contacted a customer service rep but she was not helpful.  Anyone else with this problem? Have any tips? Otherwise they will be going back.

reviews.title: Comfortable, Great Sound.  Almost too loud.  Better than the more expensive brands.
reviews.text: Great sound and good fit.  In my case, using my iPhone 5, they were too loud.  I could not get the volume low enough to hear anything around me.  The sound quality was great.  Very clear, good bass.  Worked better than the more expensive pairs I tried.  Very comfortable.  Unfortunate that I could not get the volume a little lower.  I tried all the settings on my phone and nothing would work.  If you're always using them at the gym or in a loud environment they'll work great.  Not so great In a quiet environment or outside running/walking when you want to be able to hear noise around you.

reviews.title: Just ... meh
reviews.text: These are, well, okay. The sound is fine, and they paired easily with my phone, but I don't find them comfortable to wear (the bit that is supposed to go over your ear is always a hassle, and never comfortable), and they don't feel secure when I have them in. I also find the back part annoyingly long and floppy, and I don't care much for the control switch. I much prefer my Avantree Joggers if I'm looking for a Bluetooth headset (while jogging or not).

reviews.title: Skip them.
reviews.text: We own several pairs of headphones.  Wired and wireless.  With mic and without.  Thus far these are by far our least favorites.  They're less than comfortable.  More importantly they simply do not work for us.  We're in a city.  Sometimes we talk on the phone outside where you're competing with traffic, voices, etc.  They headphones simply could not hold up to that, which is daily everyday usage here.  They neither blocked out any outside noises nor did they have a good enough sound quality to compete with what was around us.  Another common use of the headphones in our house is to help keep us entertained while in the gym.  They were used for that once before being thrown in a drawer.  I simply cannot find any reason to recommend this pair.

reviews.title: I actually find the Jabra earbuds hit or miss with comfort -- I have had bluetooth devices that were less than comfortable after
reviews.text: I have never tried other wireless bluetooth earbuds but I have tried plenty of standard earbuds.  I actually find the Jabra earbuds hit or miss with comfort -- I have had bluetooth devices that were less than comfortable after about 15 minutes.  Theses earbuds are great for running with however, and didn't hurt my ears after an hour of running.  The pairing was very easy to do with the Samsung Galaxy S3.  My only critique is that this is, ultimately, a splurge item -- a wireless headset is hardly what everyone needs. Still, it's a nice item of convenience.

Actually feel they're better built and more comfortable than the Plantronics Blackwire headset they replaced. Just wish it had the same support for Microsoft Teams that the Plantronics had. I haven't had any complaints about the audio quality.  Besides that they work fine.

reviews.title: Works Perfectly As Expected for a Microsoft Certified Headset
reviews.text: Got this 2 days ago and wanted to use it for a day or so before posting. Yes...it's as comfortable as reported by others and works well with noise suppression and excellent microphone output as reported by listeners.

reviews.title: Awesome
reviews.text: I love this headset absolutely love it. The noise cancelling is top notch everyone says I sound crystal clear and they can't hear anything in the back ground. This plug and play nothing to install which was great. I use it directly to my PC or directly into my cell phone. The cord is a very nice length so if you like to stand and talk no worries. I make over a hundred calls per day use it for zoom meetings no issue it's the perfect office headset.

reviews.title: Basic and comfortable
reviews.text: This is a very basic headset, I am using it as my backup for my fancier (more expensive headset) and so far, I think it works well.  The sound is good enough for conference calls, a bit tinny sounding with music.  It does a pretty good job with noise cancellation and it folds up small enough to fit into my overpacked carry-on bag.

reviews.title: Good single on ear headset and boom microphone
reviews.text: This is a decent boom mic and in ear headset, more comfortable than dual on ear headsets. The USB attachment has a bit of noticeable delay, but the analog direct attach TRRS audio works well. My only complaint is that is often hard to get enough volume in a single ear headset without wearing an earplug in the open ear.

reviews.title: Comfortable and noise cancelling
reviews.text: This headphone is very comfortable on my head and ears. Without plugging it in, the surrounding noise was reduced. Once I did plug them into my computer the sound quality is very good when listening to a movie. The controls are easy to understand but not easy to use. Pressing to turn on Bluetooth lowered the volume instead. I couldn't get my cellphone to connect via Bluetooth. I also didn't like that the controls did not show battery levels or that it was recharging. The only way I know that Bluetooth is on of off is via a 'voice' in my ears. This is also the only way I know if the battery is charged or not.

reviews.title: Works well
reviews.text: PROS  1. It has a noise-canceling microphone. 2. It is comfortable to wear, although can be a bit hot on the ears in some environments. 3. It is relatively light-weight, given what it is. 4. It has a 3.5 mm jack, which can be connected to a PC, Mac, or smartphone. 5. It is easy to set up.  CONS  1. These headphones do not fit entirely over the ears, so in a particularly loud environment, noise could get through, causing difficulty hearing. I do not have an issue with this myself.

reviews.title: Very good mic and sound
reviews.text: I had not heard of the Yealink brand before, but I needed to demo some of these for work.  I utilize microsoft Teams most of the day and was interested in a teams certified device.  These Yealink devices are really just fantastic. I have dogs and kids in my house, and live on a busy street.  When I am using these headphones no one can hear anything going on in the background but they all say I sound like a RADIO DJ because the voice quality is so clear and in their ear. Excellent.  If you do any kind of Teams usage all day, these are your best bet. The teams button automatically launches meetings, and the USB controls let you mute and pickup/hang up callers.

When it did connect for the calls, the other caller could barely hear me and it would go in and out, even if I had full service. Sadly, these were not worth it for me…

reviews.title: Great earbuds
reviews.text: These ear buds are great. They connected to my phone and computers easily and reconnecting is essentially automatic. The sound quality is extremely good.  The three preset EQ settings were easy to cycle through. There was a strong bass when needed and since the ear buds do not have active noise cancelling, there is no underlying hiss. They fit well, with 3 sizes of silicone tips provided and they were completely secure. As a result, the passive noise blocking is competent and far better than a pair of the original Apple iPods I used.  In an experiment, the battery in the earbuds alone lasted for several days, using them a few hours each day. The charging case can provide about 4 recharges to the ear buds, meaning that in my regular use, I would need to recharge the case less than once a week. The USB-C to USB-A charging cord is provided, but not the adapter from a power outlet to USB-A. …

About what you'd expect for a pair of $60 headphones.  Reasonable dynamics high and low with what feels like an emphasis on the mids.  They won't blow you away but for the price and the fact you're likely at the gym or a crowded space, they get the job done. - Fit. It is so convenient not to have to worry about cords.

reviews.title: Finally the waterproof headphones that don't leak or fall out!
reviews.text: I've tried about 10 different headphones for swimming; all of them either leaked or were falling out.  I guess my ear canals refused to follow the evolution theory of Darwin and remained primitive.  But finally I found something that even worked for me.  I've been swimming with these amor about 2 years. These headphones have a very nice snuggle and comfortable fit, they don't leak or fall out after 45 mins swim in endless pool (I haven't tried them in a lap pool).  The only peculiar thing is I found that if I wear them in proper orientation (that is left channel to left ear) I couldn't hear anything out of the left bud!  However, when I reverse them and wear them "upside down" with right ear channel in the left ear, the sound is perfect and the buds still don't fall out.  Short cord doesn't interfere with strokes or get tangled up.   These come with a myriad of different shapes a…

reviews.title: Love These Headphones.
reviews.text: Used the earbud type waterproof system before.  These are a tremendous improvement.  Flip turns don't affect them, they stay in place, and (bonus) keep the water out of my ears.  I would recommend them to anyone who struggles with the earbuds. Definitely worth it.

reviews.title: I was able to find the perfect fit for me
reviews.text: A quality product...worth the money! A wide assortment of ear tips are included. I was able to find the perfect fit for me. The sound quality is great. I use mine for swimming.

reviews.title: Just what I needed
reviews.text: The first time I tried it out of water, and it sounded great, then I tried one of the earbuds but when I was swimming my laps the sound kept going on and off on either side. I got worried that I'd have to return it right away. Then I went back home totally frustrated and tried all the earbuds in the different sizes. I finally found ones that seemed to fit the best and ever since then it's been perfect and no more sound going on and off. I also like how the ear buds stay on the posts tightly and don't come off in my ear canals.

reviews.title: Good quality
reviews.text: I waited till I had this a week or two with doing laps several different sessions to review it.  Wow! Finally a headphone set that doesn't cut out constantly.  Worth the money.  No other brand would keep the water out and those would cut out and get annoying having to try to adjust while swimming.  If you are really wanting to have music while doing laps, this is worth the investment

reviews.title: Quality has declined
reviews.text: Since 2016 I have purchased 7 of these for myself and as gifts. In the past I gave it a 5 star review and recommended them in person countless times. Sadly I feel the quality has declined. The last two pair did not last as long. My last pair lasted only 8 months. They no longer come with a protective case even though the price is the same.

Everyones ears are so different, but they come with several versions of silicone tips so it's highly likely you will find something that will work.

reviews.title: Bone conduction are the all around best!
reviews.text: These bone conduction headphones are truly the best thing for all uses (aside from swimming) as you can listen to your music, audio books, etc. but at the same time, you can hear what's going on all around you.  So if you are jogging or taking a walk around the neighborhood, you can listen to your tunes, but still hear and be aware of people and vehicles around you.  I mean, a big, burly guy may feel safe running with earbuds stuck down in his ears so he can't hear anything else, but for most of us, it's important to be aware of your surroundings when out walking/running.  Need to hear cars coming, need to be aware of people running up behind you...it's just that important and I can tell you this Mojawa bone conduction headset will deliver excellent sound without sacrificing that awareness of what's going on (in hearing) around you.  Excellent price, too!

reviews.title: These Sound Surprisingly Well and Comfortable
reviews.text: These headphones have been great. I was concerned about the clarity of sound but it is very good. I usually need to set the volume at 25-40 percent for clarity. There are a few cons but I think most bone conduction headphones are similar. They do not work well at all on airplanes but that makes sense. The band is also not adjustable. reviews.title: Clear sound with distortion free bass
reviews.text: I have tested many earbuds that range in price from $10 to over $100, and I must say these sound very decent in this price range and better than some that cost twice as much. They are very bass-midrange centric, but the sound clarity is superb, and they have not distorted at the loudest volume I could stand. I heard instrumental detail I would not have expected in a pair of $25 earbuds. I thought the heavier bass and midrange would seem unbalanced and bothersome, but it wasn't after listening to a range of music for a few hours. I haven't tried them on phone calls yet, but if the music sounds this clean and clear, I am sure my phone calls will as well. I will update my review if it doesn't live up to my expectations. So far I like these earbuds a lot and highly recommend them.

reviews.title: Unfortunately mine arrived broken - unable to charge
reviews.text: I plugged it in right after I received it - usually JVC is a good product and I wanted to get these paired with my Kindle so I could listen to my Audible books.  It charged all night, I saw the red dot when I plugged it in, the next day I unplugged it and tried to pair it.  Kindle on, ready to pair...can't get the earphones to come on.  Plugged them back in and wow...after about 12 hours, these are showing they hadn't charged at all.  Obviously, there's something wrong with the internal battery or the connection to the internal battery.  Nothing I can do about that, but be sure to check yours right away to be sure there isn't something wrong.  I'm very disappointed with what I received.

reviews.title: Great sound for the Price !

reviews.title: You have to get use to using Bone Conduction headphones
reviews.text: I found it very difficult to locate the correct spot for good listening. This is not necessarily a defect of the headphones but more likely my inexperience with this type of headphone. The front of my ear felt like it was vibrating with the music which was not an enjoyable feeling. Of course the sound quality varied as I tried to find a good location on my ear. The instructions say nothing about the microphone. If someone received this headphone without seeing the product write up on the Amazon page, they would never know you can talk through the headphone.

reviews.title: Comfy, good mids and highs
reviews.text: I'm wearing these now and they're quite comfortable to wear for extended periods. Connection was easy. I wish they had more control buttons instead of just the one. The charging port is also in an odd place (presumably to keep people from charging while wearing) (it's on the left ear-pod). Sound quality is a little funky and I guess to be expected on a cheap pair of headphones: the biggest thing is that they don't reproduce bass really at all, I can feel the bass hits when the pod hits my ear, but the bass isn't making it to my eardrum; at highest volume there's a bit of distortion but they don't really get /that/ loud; otherwise, at low-medium levels and for treble and mids, the sound reproduction is excellent. I suspect I'm going to like these more for podcasts and audiobooks than music. If you're not into really bass-y music, and you don't need substantial volume, these will probably …

reviews.title: Has great sound when positioned properly
reviews.text: This headset is too big for my head.  When I put them on where it’s comfortable I can hear things pretty good but when I shift the speakers back a little the sound becomes much more brilliant.  Unfortunately there is no adjustment to be able to have the speakers line up with my ears.  Pairs with Bluetooth easily.  Charges fast and seems to last a long time.  Easy to turn on and off too.  I’m scoring these as a 5 because they are very nice and comfortable with great sound and mic clarity.  Just be aware that they need a large head in order to use effectively.

reviews.title: Really shines while wearing hearing protectors
reviews.text: This is my first set of bone-conduction headphones, so with that important disclaimer out there, up front and center...  I like this headphone set pretty well.  I was a bit perplexed by them at first, as, similar to other reviewers, I was a bit puzzled about the seemingly relatively loose fit on my head, relatively low volume level, etc.  My "ah-ha" moment came when I lightly covered my ear canals with my fingers while wearing them and streaming music - the audio level was greatly boosted!  I bounded off to the garage, grabbed a clean set of my favorite hearing protector plugs and put them into place, put on the headset, adjusted the volume, then turned on my big ol' air compressor - easily the noisiest thing I have in my house & shazam!, I could easily enjoy my music while in a high noise environment, even at relatively low music volume levels!  I have used connected hearing protectors …

reviews.title: Love these!
reviews.text: I really love these headphones. I don’t like to stick earbuds in my ears as I have my daiths pierced and it can be very uncomfortable to wear earbuds. Earbuds also tend to block out sound around me for the most part and I like to be aware of what’s happening around me. This is the first time I have tried bone conduction headphones, and I really like the experience. I do find that I have to turn the volume louder than if I had earphones in my ears, but I’m OK with that. I feel like the price is really reasonable considering the technology. I gifted a set of of these by a different brand name to my father for Christmas, and he absolutely loves them. They make a great gift!

reviews.title: Weird but effective, comfortable for long-term wear
reviews.text: I have what is apparently a larger-than-normal head (enough so that buying non-adjustable hats is a no-go), so I wasn't sure how bone conduction headphones would work for me- while I still don't know if all bone conduction headphones would work, this particular pair worked quite well  for me and also worked for multiple other folks. The piece that needs to be in contact with your bone is actually pretty independent of the flexible but not flimsy cable that runs behind the neck to connect the two earpieces, so head size is less of a concern than I thought.  While the audio is better on more focused headphones(over-ear or in-ear), the audio on this is more than sufficient to hear without drowning out the world around you.  My husband could hear a little of the music I was listening to, but not so much that it was disruptive.  Overall, these are a decently-priced foray into bone conduction …

reviews.title: Good in a pinch and rather flexible
reviews.text: This will work with any phone or PC with a 3.5mm (1/8") headset jack.  It will also work in any USB C port (again on a phone or PC) via the included adapter.  That makes it handy tool in my work bag, as I can hop of on Zoom or Teams call on my PC either directly via the 3.5mm cable or my phone or laptop with the adapter.  That flexibility makes it a great backup to my Bluetooth headset.  As a primary headset, this is lacking in terms of comfort, volume, noise cancelling, and much more.  It's more of a minimal viable product than daily tool.  Since I use it mostly as a backup, it's a fair tradeoff.  If I had to use this daily, I'd be looking for another headset.

reviews.title: Very comfortable!
reviews.text: I love that the ear cushions on these are really comfortable and I enjoy having them on. The headband cushion is also really comfortable  I like that you can move the ear pieces themselves so they can flip up and put them around your neck and still hear well. They're easy to adjust to your head and it's easy to remove the USB part at the control so you can use the 3.5mm port instead. I don't like thar if you're using the 3.5mm port you lose the controls though. Also these do not fit over your ear just on them so it doesn't block very much noise however they do have good sound quality and a good mic. The metal part on the top of the headband is a little flimsy but they still work well. My husband uses them for online gaming on his computer and my son uses them with his switch and tablet. Overall decent quality headphones for the price!

reviews.title: Hands free music and talking
reviews.text: Nice sound quality and it is very comfortable. I can talk on my phone or listen to my favorite music

reviews.title: Nice multi-connector headset works great for web meetings & for audio voice over without USB adapter
reviews.text: We got this just before a trip and used it right away to replace a set of ear buds. Using the 3.5mm adapter, this works well and avoids the audio latency introduced by using the USB adapter. The headset is quite comfortable and includes a cushion between your head and the metal band that gives it a bit of tension to stay on your head. The foam cups fit on your ear, not over your ears. I prefer this Nuroum design as the headset is smaller and lighter than my old ham radio headset, though I have to give the nod to my old ever the ear JBL headset for comfort over very long sessions. The Nuroum ear pieces fold and the headset tucks into a handy cloth drawbag. Definitely more portable for trips than our JBL over ear headsets.  The boom mic has good sensitivity and the position is easily adjusted. The audio signal wire comes off the left side, at least that's what my audio test told me. Though…

reviews.title: Great Earbuds
reviews.text: My bro loves wireless earbuds, so was looking for one to give him as a birthday gift. I have seen many expensive ones but this one caught my eyes to the pricing and has features/shape I was looking for. As show in pics it comes in a cylinder type case, my brother loved it. It connects phone easily via bluetooth. Charging is also great, we tested with  listening continuously music for few hours.  Sound clarity is pretty clear and bass was good too. It fits in to ear perfectly as shown in pictures, even during your exercise or running they hold good. They did give additional caps for different ear sizes. It has left or right symbol on earbuds and  also on case, so we don't get confused every time when we put it back in case or ears. Overall I liked this product and a great gift to my bro..

reviews.title: I wanted to love these
reviews.text: i was so excited for the long battery life, but they have not lasted me more than about 8 hours instead of 13. No matter which ear cap I use, these are always falling out. One of the ear buds seems to disconnect often and it is incredibly frustrating! If you have to pause the sound often, these earbuds are not for you! If i push my hair behind my ear, there is a good chance it will pause, but there is a lag so sometimes you don't know if you touched it hard enough and tap again, then the earbuds get confused and might disconnect. I had really wanted to love these! I had bought my husband a pair before mine arrived, thats how much I wanted to love these.

reviews.title: Generic earbuds in a strange case
reviews.text: I've reviewed many low cost, generic earbuds, and what sets these out from the rest is the somewhat strange case.  While most earbuds come in a more familiar case - a  box with a lid. You open the lid, and the earbuds are inside, charging (if the case is charged).  This case is different - it's a cylinder. You turn the cylinder to expose the earbuds, one at a time. When each earbud is exposed, you can take it out (or return it to the case when you're done using them). I've discovered that it isn't particularly hard to accidentally move the case to expose the earbud. So far, none have escaped from the case, but carrying it in a purse or pocket could possibly expose an earbud if the case turns to expose the earbud.  Sound was good - not great.  Sound cancellation wasn't particularly good.  Phone calls were okay, but people on the other line picked up background noise.  In short, these won'…

reviews.title: True Wireless Stereo BT 5.0 Ear Buds w/Charging Case-Compact,Touch Controls,Great Sound,IPX5
reviews.text: I love listening to music and really enjoy a great pair of ear phones to use. These have a very nice fit and stay in for me quite well. I found these to be very comfortable for long wear. These are smaller than many earbuds without the tail I see on many. They have a total of 3 sizes of silicone eartips and 2 different ear retention bands to help hold them in. The look is stylish and discreet. I loved how these had very good sound! Pictures 1&2 what I received; Picture 3 charging with my own longer cable.  The Bluetooth 5.0 pairing connection was easy to make with either my phone or iPod device. Range was as good as most similar style earbuds without dropping out over a room away. I experienced no trouble and if the connection dropped due to distance, reconnection was automatic. The touch controls were flawless and simple.  These sound crisp and clean with great mids, vocals and high end…

reviews.title: Good wireless ear buds
reviews.text: I use wireless earbuds often and it is important to me that they have good sound, are comfortable and have long battery life.  These ear buds meet all three requirements well. The sound has great quality that I like.  Earbuds are very comfortable to wear since I wear them for many hours during the day and at night when I'm in bed. I like the tube design.  Seems sturdier than flip open cases that rely on a small hinge.  I like how I just have to twist the tube to open it up.  Convenient and better, in my opinion. I like to use these to help me sleep by playing music from about 10 pm to 6 am.  The battery easily lasts that long. I put them back into the case for a charge in the mornings.  I haven't had any time where the battery has drained.  Can go at least 4-5 days before I need to put them back into the case for a recharge. Highly recommend these to others who rely on wireless ear buds.

reviews.title: 300 Dollars Though?
reviews.text: While I am impressed with these headphones, I cannot find anything to justify the price point.  They feel good on my ears. I usually don't wear over the ear headphones but haven't had any comfort issues. I like that there is an application where you can customize the equalizer (among other things).  I'm more of a bass kinda gal so I appreciate being able to turn it up. I also like that I can control the volume and skip songs straight on the headphone so I don't have to fool with my phone.  I like the way they look but they aren't very "trendy" they are literally the same color throughout the product. I'm wondering if they are trying to appeal to an older customer base. The single color does look clean.  A big plus for me that it uses the same charger as the Samsung S10 so I know I will be able to charge them wherever I charge my phone such as my car or work desk.  Overall, a nice headpho…

reviews.title: Jabra 85h head-to-head with Bose 35
reviews.text: If you’re looking for unmatched sound reproduction in a very quiet music room, neither the Bose 35 nor the Jabra 85h is competing in that studio monitor class.  These are yeoman everyday transit use with great sound quality. It’s the noise cancelling depth that shuts out the chaos that makes the two exceptional. Ambient sustained engine/crowd noise will wear you out. That’s what makes noise cancelling central for me.  Noise cancelling – Jabra is the first headphone experience every bit the equal with the Bose 35. Other noise reduction players competing in the price bracket don’t come close. The Jabra and Bose cancellation are different. Audible net cancellation is so close to the same that I can’t discriminate. Bose noise cancelling has a sort of over-pressure feeling that I don’t notice in the Jabra. It’s not a discriminator or fatigue element either way for me. If you know what I mean,…

reviews.title: Great all around headphones
reviews.text: These are great. I live in an apartment and got them so I wouldn’t bother my neighbors with loud tv. They work great and have insane battery life. So far I’ve had them for about a month and only had to charge them once. Haven’t tried them for work on teams yet, will get back to you on that. Very comfy and easy to pair. So far so great.

reviews.title: Wouldn’t stay connected to BT devices
reviews.text: The sound quality is very good. The controls are awkward and every minutes or two the Bluetooth connection would fail and then reconnect.  I returned it due to this major tech flaw. BT headphones that don’t stay connected to BT devices.  No thank you

reviews.title: This is my go to headset now.  I'm using this more than my Sony's Or Plantronics
reviews.text: Comfortable to use for extended periods of time for me.  I'm wearing these for several hours at a time.  When you fold them flat, they turn off, extending your battery life, which I like.  Jabra App gives you options for sound.  People can hear me fine when I get phone calls, and I can talk to them while I have both earphones on my head.  I was using the PLT pro 2, since they put the music on hold when I take the headset off.  they get a touch warmer, not much.  So far the sound canceling is great.  I can't hear the neighbors or the construction that is happening next door.

reviews.title: Still amazing...
reviews.text: Used to have a pair of the white/gold ones & loved them. Was very sad to lose them. But! "Santa" saw fit to bring me a new pair.

reviews.title: Size is an issue
reviews.text: These are really great headphones BUT they are a lot bulkier than say Sony or Bose headphones.

reviews.title: Better than my Bose QC35s in every way
reviews.text: Very intuitive controls, Noice-Cancelling (ANC) is strong, sound quality is great, and most importantly they firmly stay on my head without actually feeling like theyre there. Definitely recommend, especially for the price.

reviews.title: These are pretty nice and work great
reviews.text: I've had these for quite a while now. I am amazed at battery life... they seem to never "go dead".  The sound is good.  They aren't REALLY loud/powerful, but plenty loud. I wear them when mowing to reduce the mower noises and to listen to music while mowing. I've also worn on an airplane and they really cut down on the noise the plane makes.

reviews.title: Good for music, not for Zoom on PC
reviews.text: Great pair of noise canceling headphones. Love the sound on these and how it cuts all noise around me out. I bought these for work from home with the intention of using them for zoom calls.  Unfortunately they do not work for zoom. I ended up having to use the laptop mic when using these for zoom. Also, when you use the provided 3.5mm cable, it does not work for the mic, super disappointed in that.  Giving these 4 stars since they don't work for zoom calls on PC. 5 stars for sound.

reviews.title: Not entirely thrilled
reviews.text: While these are generally good, I found three things I don't like.  They aren't comfy. My Corwin cheapies are more comfortable for long-term wearing.  They don't block sounds as well as I wanted. I am listening to legal proceedings for transcript editing, and I need to be able to hear without background noise . Even at the highest level of sound blocking, environmental sounds still break through.  I'm not saying they don't help. Maybe my expectation of "sound blocking" is too high. I just wonder if for the price there isn't another that is a little bit better.  Finally, you can only connect them via Bluetooth to your phone, not your laptop. As a result I am tied to my computer by a cord connection. That is really a problem. I cannot even check the battery level without disconnecting from the computer cable and connecting to the phone. I don't know if that is the same in other products in…

reviews.title: Block out the world, or barely let it in...
reviews.text: What an upgrade! I’ve had Beats for years, but got these for Christmas & I think I’m in love. I can’t tell you about all the nuances. I don’t hear them & I don’t try. That’s not the point for me. The point is to listen to my music & feel immersed & these do it perfectly. What’s better is they go around my ear, they don’t. Which helps immensely, as my ears have issues with pressure on them. So, they are comfortable, they sound amazing to me, & the noise cancelling is great. I wish I could use it more, but I tend to have these on when I’m out & about. Which brings me to the app that you get to pair with them. You can either choose what setting you’re on or let it choose to automatically decide where you are. I love the hear through option. The ability to feel like I do not have them on & there is just music playing around me. So, all in all, best choice I made to switch.

reviews.title: Nicely done
reviews.text: I'm not an audiophile, so sadly I'd recommend looking at another review for details on the audio quality of these headphones.  I personally think it's great, but I have aged ears and just want to be up front about that.  I think what has really made me warm up to these headphones is that I can tell a lot of effort went into some of the more subtle features of the headset.  For example, you turn them off by twisting the headphones so you can lay them down flat.  Turn them back to the 'over-the-ear' position and the headphones come on.  Not only that, but when you put them on a voice tells you how much battery you have left.  To put it another way, unlike my other wireless headphones, I don't have to find the nearly-invisible button to activate them.  I think the noise-cancelling is good, too.  If I had one criticism it's that when you use the smart-phone App to configure the headphones th…

reviews.title: The Best Headphones ever
reviews.text: Sound quality is amazing. It is wireless which allows for freedom of movement. The earmuffs are large so it covers the entire ear. This provide great noise cancellation and the wearer can just focus on the sound. When wearing these head phones, one feels as the real world is far, far away. Fully charged, the head phones can last about three hours of continuous usage. One of the best head phones I have ever used.

reviews.title: Great sound quality
reviews.text: These are great headphones.  They’re everything I hoped that they’d be.  The sound is really nice and high quality.  They pair seamlessly with my devices also.  Highly recommend.

reviews.title: Noise cancellation works fine, sound range a little narrow
reviews.text: First, although the earpieces look big they are a little tight on the ears instead of covering the ears like the Bose.  Appearance is really rich looking, so that lives up to the price.  Found the sound range a little narrow, short on base and high treble.  The controls take some time to get used to.  Tried using on a phone call and the other end said I sounded distant and hollow.  Did pair with 3 different devices with no problem.  Was listening to my PC and was able to answer a call on my phone (Note 8).  Also paired with tablet and can switch back and forth with no problem.  All in all, a good product with a few limitations.

reviews.title: My New Daily Use Headphones
reviews.text: I have been looking at Noise Canceling headphones trying to figure out which one to get. These are just about perfect.  The Active Noise Canceling works very well. I have tested it on the Plane, long car ride, next to a room AC unit, settling down to sleep. I was able to get some sleep on my last flight thanks to this headset.  They work best when there is something playing even softly. My previous headphones could not be turned down low enough in a very quiet environment or up enough in a very noisy one. The Jabra 85h can handle that range. The microphone quality on phone calls is comparable to my old Plantations Voyager v5200. I was much happier once I realized that the headphone can be adjusted for head size.

reviews.title: Great headphones!
reviews.text: These look great and are very comfortable! They are fairly light weight and so can be worn all day. The sound quality is really good. They come in a really cute case just as an add bonus.

reviews.title: 5 stars
reviews.text: Just got to use the on the plane. The noise canceling feature works very nicely. The music sounds crystal clear. It was super easy to connect to my phone and my Alexa. Alexa also works well. I love the take it off and the music pauses feature. The case is really ncie. They were very comfortable on the plane. They are very sleek and nicely made. I also have the Bose equivalent and these are just as good but with some better features. I’m not pro at headphones, just a regular person who loves music, and I am thoroughly enjoying these headphones. I have some great pictures I took of them when I first got them, will add when I get back home. And will also have another chance to use them on the plane again. So far I love these! I guess I’ll add a quick pic from the hotel safe via my phone. 5 stars from me!

reviews.title: Wow
reviews.text: Wow just wow these are great headphones. One of my favorite features the headphones auto pause when taken off ears and auto resume when put back on. The music is comparable to a car with a sound system. Call quality is great and the person on other line can hear you even if you whisper because of the 9 yes 9 microphones in the headset. It is Alexa compatible although i don't use it. Love the auto turn on and connect feature just by unfolding the headset turn off same way by folding up. The battery life is amazing and charges rather quickly.  Comes with a nice carrying case. I could go on and on about this product and highly recommend it.

reviews.title: Not bad for the price
reviews.text: These are some pretty good in-ear headphones. They work only with iPhone so make sure that is what you are buying them for. On the cable they have a multi controller that allows you to control your phone, answer calls, end calls, repeat calls, has a microphone built in, play, pause and advance in the track. It also allows you to adjust the volume when you play your music. I wouldn't even bother with headphones anymore that don't provide these extras.  The sound quality of these is pretty good. They also came with some extra rubber covers so you can find the one that makes them fit best in your ears. The price is right for these too, so all in all a pretty good deal.

reviews.title: Simple and better than paying Apple more directly.
reviews.text: Very basic, but very useful set of headphones if you're stuck using a lightning connector.  I really hate Apple for this (as well as many other things), but if you you're stuck, you're stuck.  The only thing I can say is that now you'll need a second set of headphones for a mini-plug anywhere else, including the plane.  So you might prefer a lightning connector to mini-plug adapter.  But these are at least reasonably priced enough that you can probably afford a pair of each, although it's still annoying to have to drag both around.  The ear pieces are comfortable and nice.  The headphones themselves sound fine, although of course no headphones are really amazing, especially the ear-bud type.

reviews.title: Here's how to get it to work with Linux
reviews.text: To use the Logitech unifying receiver and link other compatible devices (as well as this keyboard) on a Linux computer, look for and install an app called "Solaar." I found it just by doing a search with Synaptic package manager. Install both Solaar and the Solaar GUI (graphic user interface) to make it easier to use. Once you launch Solaar, you may have to unplug the Logitech unifying receiver and plug it back in to get Solaar to detect it. And you may have to switch the keyboard (or other compatible device) off and back on. Once Solaar is running, it puts a little hiding widget on the lower left of your display screen you can click on to access the settings.  As far as the keyboard goes, it works great and the key action is quiet and comfortable. I like the ergonomics too. I still use a wrist rest since I like more wrist elevation than what the built-in rest provides. All in all it's a…

reviews.text: What more can I say that hasn't already been about the Wave design?  It's comfortable, ergonomic, easy to use, and helps me to get my keystrokes in faster. No need to get this if you already have the Wave, but if you don't, or you're absolutely dead-set on getting this for the extra features (via software) and Unifying setup, then this is a great keyboard to consider.  It's easy to use right out of the box; had no issues whatsoever (batteries included, too).

reviews.title: Everything works except the keys!
reviews.text: Very attractive keyboard. Bluetooth is good, ergonomics are good, even sleep  mode works well. There is one glaring problem. THE KEYS DON'T WORK!!!! - Clicking a key does not produce the letter, number or symbol. It doubles the character and adds a blank space -  creating 3 characters er click. - It happens so often I have to use an old keyboard to correct the problem.  The typing using the keyboard was so problematic, I contacted customer service, and they replaced it. I have thrown one in the trash and now I'm considering throwing the other in the trash.  The keyboard is cosmetically wonderful, but if the keys don't work correctly, what value is it. I will reach out to customer service one more time.

reviews.title: Better than expected
reviews.text: This is a good keyboard.  It connects easily to a Mac and the key touch is much like the Apple version.  It connects to three devices which is helpful and switching between them is easy.  The internal rechargeable battery is convenient although I cannot yet advise the life of the charge.  The only negatives are that awaking the Mac and inserting your password requires patience as there is a delay and the keyboard is configured to work with Windows and Mac OS so a few of the keys are oddly place.  Overall it has proven to be a good choice.

reviews.title: Works Well with Mac!
reviews.text: I bought this product because I wanted a keyboard that was the same as my Macbook Air and it works great. Compared to the official Apple keyboard which is over $100, this is an amazing alternative, especially with the ability to switch between 3 different devices. I currently have it connected to my phone, macbook and ipad and switching between the 3 only takes a couple seconds. On the downsides, it's definitely a lot bigger than normal because of the number pad, so keep that in mind just in case you're planning on getting a bluetooth keyboard for traveling. Since I'm not taking it around everywhere it works great for me but I wouldn't say the same if I had to carry it around with me. Also the up and down arrow keys are a bit small but that's my only complaint and you can get used to it. Don't let that deter you though as you can always use programs to bind keys to have different outputs…

reviews.title: Key Top Labels Are Just Painted On and Wear Off Quickly
reviews.text: I have one major gripe about this keyboard.  We've had it less than a year and the letters are already worn off of four of the keys.  It's a quality issue; the key labels aren't etched into the key. they are just painted on top of the flat key.  So they wear off very quickly.  I expected better quality from a Microsoft keyboard and also for this price.  Also, we aware that this keyboard is too big for many women - my wife has a hard time using it.  Due to those two factors, I'll be replacing it soon.

reviews.title: Paid 32 bucks in 2015 and it's dead now in March 2021
reviews.text: 3/26/2021:  Now dropping my rating to 1 star, and you have to be off your rocker to pay more than ten times what I paid for it back in 2015.  32 bucks.  Yep, that was the price here, and it was never great.  Today it simply died.  No fix would work, and I am in no way surprised.  Overpriced, way overpriced junk!  9/28/2016:  I'm updating this review and dropping the star count here to 2 for a very simple reason:  The letters on this keyboard are almost all worn off!  I have had a lot of keyboards in the past 40 years, from typewriters to the dozen or more computers I've owned, and I have never, ever had a letter on a single keyboard wear off, or even get dim from use.  So while this thing is comfy, and I definitely know where all the letters and numbers are on a keyboard, I find it unacceptable and frankly bizarre that the lettering would wear off on this keyboard.  I'd recommend buying …

reviews.title: Disappointing performance
reviews.text: I was so disappointed with this product. I do a lot of typing daily and end up with sore fingers and wrists. I need a keyboard that's more ergonomic, so I tried this due to its popularity and high ratings. Unfortunately, the keys are stiff and hard to push, especially the space bar. The angle isn't quite right (for me), so I had to stretch and strain my hands and fingers even more than on my straight keyboard. It was a total bust for me. My husband likes it, so he's going to use it at work. Otherwise, I would be returning it for a refund.

reviews.title: A Fantastic Upgrade
reviews.text: What's not to like?  I upgraded from a Microsoft Ergonomic keyboard that was about 15 years old.  Nothing wrong with it, but I wanted new.  I think I actually paid much more 15 years ago than I did for this upgrade.  Lots of competition out there. Why did I go back with to Microsoft?  My first one lasts 15 years before I got tired of it.  I actually use it at my school (I'm an elementary school teacher).  It has a USB port plug instead of the old system round thing.  The keyboard actually syncs in with our Microsoft operating system that our school district has just upgraded to.  So my interface is smoother.  It has a newer ascept of a wrist rest at the base of the keyboard.  It is actually higher than the keyboard.  Look at the pictures.  Your wrist just rests in a perfectly natural place.  This is so worth a few bucks.  I know that iPads and other laptops make up the larger market now,…

reviews.title: Only slightly less than Perfect!
reviews.text: My decision to purchase this keyboard was based on a glowing review by someone that had been using his keyboard for a few months. I was seeking a keyboard that was quiet and ergonomic (fatigue-diminishing and user-friendly). My old H-P keyboard, after 4+ years of daily use, had become so "clattery" that it was a nuisance; plus, I'd worn the lettering off several keys! This new keyboard, though not 'whisper-quiet,' is definitely quieter. It took 2 or 3 days to get used to the different hand positioning and smaller "Enter" key, but was a breeze to adjust to. I'm hoping now to find a quieter Mouse! Would recommend this to anyone using a keyboard for several hours each day and in need of the relief provided by a soft-touch keyboard and quieter keystrokes.

reviews.title: Comfortable, but not very robust.
reviews.text: This is a very comfortable keyboard to type on, but there is one major problem  Compared to other rubber dome switch keyboards I've owned, this one is susceptible to damage from liquids like none other. Just a few drops of water will cause the plastic circuitry sheets in this thing to burn out and cause keys to register improperly. I've owned two of these and they both suffered the same fate.  This is in contrast to cheap throwaway keyboards that have had an entire glass of soda dumped on them and been no worse for wear after a good inside and out wipe down.  I used Microsoft Natural Ergonomic keyboards for years but I just couldn't justify purchasing another. I'm not expecting a keyboard to hold up to a monsoon, but a few drops of water?  I still have the previous Natural Ergo model from Microsoft as my backup keyboard. Works fine after several years of use. I only replaced it with the …

reviews.title: Fast keyboard, quality switches, compact
reviews.text: I've been using this keyboard for a few months, now and am glad I switched from a standard keyboard to this mechanical.  The reason I switched, was because I needed to free up some desk space and also needed to break from my habits of using the 10-key pad.  Both of those things were addressed with this, but I found that my typing speed has increased with the more intentional keystroke.  My accuracy is improving, as well.  Being at my computer for 8-10 hours a day and preferring to use a mouse as little as possible, this has been a great purchase.  What I like: - Fast and responsive mechanical switches - Compact size, due to lack of 10-key pad - Solid base that won't flex or move around the desk - Long braided USB cable works well for my desk size. - Lights can be fun to change the look once in a while.  It keeps the kids amused, when they are in my office. - A few replacement switches ar…

No light bleed from underneath keycaps if you're on lower brightness levels. Letters are perfect, easy to see.  Feels solid, pretty heavy.  This is one of the only keyboard on Amazon with Brown switches, and I believe the only RGB one, at this price range. Blue is so common but the Browns are either non-existent or way more expensive (like 35 vs 55). At least when I was buying this.  I just previously got a different one that I had enough of and I'm happy to say this is a step up (albeit I can't speak to their RGB so I'm not comparing apples to apples).  Oh and it has a braided cord and USB cap/cover - nice touch if you're carrying yours around. The spare switches are also considerate.  Instructions are more of a cheat-sheet, and I don't…

reviews.title: Went from Drevo to this...
reviews.text: Best thing I ever did tbh. I was using the compact Drevo keyboard which had a few issues of its own. The compact design was done in a way that didn't allow easy cleaning AND the software for easy RBG light management didn't work 100% as it should have. Not to mention it was more expensive and had less features... And due to the harder cleaning the keys needed to be smashed/wiggled a bit to be coerced into working.  So this one is 20 bucks cheaper, has a 100% working software program, and you can even change the polling rates. The keys are properly spaced for proper cleaning and it comes with back-up switches for when your most used keys (usually ASDW sfor gamers) start to wear as mechanical keys often do. It's small enough and has all the proper keys for media and gaming without smashing them all too close together. A very attractive and well-thought out keyboard. As for the switches, I …

reviews.text: I chose the Red Switches because I absolutely despise super loud switches and ended up getting shipped a blue switch version. Off to a fantastic start, the spacebar which is used a lot in Valorant, also came with a annoying ping that I did not hear in the few videos I looked up on it. Also came with a scratch on the aluminum frame which was a bummer. All in all if the spacebar was fine, woulda been a easy 4/5 but you can't mess up a big key on a gaming keyboard, cmon man.

reviews.title: Nice keyboard... for 3 months
reviews.text: Lights are nice and the keyboard felt good... for about 3 months. I got this keyboard in December and use it regularly for gaming and productivity. I’m clean around my computer and I don’t eat around it. I play a lot of FPS games so I use wasd keys and space bar a lot. After about 3 months the wasd keys and space bar often get stuck or don’t register a press. I looked it up and my guess is that the plastic residue comes off and messes with the keys. That’s really disappointing. I’ve had cheap $10 keyboards that have lasted years with zero maintenance. I wanted to treat myself with a mechanical keyboard for my gaming pc set up. 3 months life is really not worth it at all. I would not recommend this product.

reviews.text: So i have a corsair k70 rapid fire with mx cherry speed. I love that keyboard, most likely the best keyboard i have ever owned for gaming. However, i am doing a lot more coding now a days and needed something that was less sensitive. the mx speed switches were a lil to sensitive for typing; i was often times pressing unwanted keys here and there and got a lil annoyed. so, i looked to amazon for a blue switch keyboard. however, i wasn't really willing to spend a fortune.  overall, i am quite impressed with the design, rgb lighting, build quality, price, and switches - they feel like actual mx cherry blues! they may be a lil louder tho. i haven't tried these for gaming yet, but i don't think they wont be as good for gaming as my k70 with mx cherry speed switches. the only thing that would really make these great would be if they last as long as my k70 - which are still very much functional…

reviews.title: Good keyboard but it takes time to adjust.
reviews.text: I had a prior version of this keyboard (the Microsoft Natural Ergonomic Keyboard 3000) for my office PC.  It did admirably, but after a year or so, my wrists were starting to hurt IN SPITE OF the ergonomics helping.  This one is better rated.  So far, it has helped, but it took at least a week of use just for my hands to BEGIN to get used to the differences.  I'd do a pro/con list, but I'm not sure there are any "cons" as compared to "issues to expect" if you buy this keyboard.  1.  Expect a steep learning curve to get used to the layout.  The "bend" in this keyboard is significant, and it will take time for your fingers to get used to hitting the right keys on a consistent basis.  Give it one or two weeks of regular use before deciding if you like it or not.  You can't know in a couple of days if it's helping you because you do need to re-learn your hand placemen…

reviews.title: Very comfortable keyboard for those suffering of any sort of wrist issues
reviews.text: I've been using ergonomic / natural keyboards for about ten years now and since the very first ones came out. This has proven to be the most comfortable one so far. I had one of these at my last job and I ended up buying one for my current job and for home.  I recommend buying the business version (this keyboard is also available in the home edition.) While a little more expensive, the business version comes with a small stand that can be removed to make the angle of the keyboard change. The home version does not come with this stand. Because of this, the angle for the home version cannot be changed and you are basically forced to use the keyboard in only two positions in opposite to four as it is the case with the business version.  People who hit the keys very strongly (as if using a typewriter), may find this keyboard not as strong. However, for someone who does hit keys very hard lik…

reviews.title: The case of the disappearing letters...
reviews.text: I really like this keyboard due to its comfort.  However, I am very disappointed that the key paint disappears too quickly.  I've got no "A", "S", "D", or "C" and only a partial "E", "R", and "V".  The keys still work.  The letters have gone incognito.  Even after buying a new keyboard (I bought the same one again as I like the comfort and feel) the letters started disappearing within a couple of months.  I'd sure like to see some proactive action on behalf of Microsoft to reach out and replace the keys with new ones that are painted to last a few years as opposed to a few weeks.

reviews.title: Great extras but not a good typing experience
reviews.text: I'm yet another Natural Elite fan saddened by the fact that Microsoft no longer makes it. If they started making it again and added some of the features this one has, I'd buy a lifetime supply.  I had this for about a week and really, really wanted to keep it. Having a dedicated calculator key was great, but even more useful were the page back and forward buttons and the toggle switch to change magnification. That toggle made my life much easier at work; I wish every keyboard had it.  I didn't use the riser for the front of the keyboard, though I would have used it more had I kept it just to see if it made typing more comfortable. The padded wrist rest was nice, and the keyboard itself was easy to clean. And although I don't care much about aesthetics, my colleagues all commented positively on the keyboard's appearance.  Unfortunately, the negatives outweighed all of that. The biggest pr…

reviews.title: Easy on my wrists and fingers!
reviews.text: Item arrived on time and is exactly what I ordered.  I got it for work since the keyboards they supply started causing me discomfort.  I'm very happy with it so far.  Had it for a while now.  All the keys push smoothing.  I've had issues with keys sticking with other ergonomic keyboards but not this one.  Very comfortable to use.  Thank you.

reviews.title: Never could use this
reviews.text: Missed the window to return due to emergency surgery and then a 30 day stint in rehab. I really can't use this - so different from a standard keyboard. I've tried off and on for a month now and have finally given up Much later than you would think and much, much more of a curve down the middle.

reviews.title: wonderful shape
reviews.text: This was a replacement for another ergonomic keyboard and I was thrilled to get it but many of the keys are loosing their white painted letters.  I’m not thrilled about that.

reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text: I love the function of this keyboard but it is the 2nd one I have purchased and this one lasted less than a year. I think the first one lasted less than two.  I don't use them a lot so I would have expected it to last much longer.  I won't be getting another one.

reviews.title: Leaning curve to use but no wrist pain
reviews.text: A great choice for an ergonomic keyboard. Adjustable height with removable piece beneath wrist rest if you don’t like your wrists too high. Separated keys take a bit to get used to, particularly the ‘b’ being on the left hand for me. It definitely takes time to get comfortable but with time it is difficult to go back to a traditional keyboard. I’ve been using for 6 months and am 100% happy with it.

reviews.title: It is a great keyboard
reviews.text: I'm pleased. I used have one of these ages ago. I've been using the Wave style but have found that the keys are still not in the right position, so I decided to get one of these. The down side is that it isn't wireless, but I have more than enough USB extensions to compensate for moving my keyboard stand around and up and down so that I can use it from just about any position and from several feet away from the screens. It is big, doesn't leave much room for the mouse on the keyboard stand, but I also acquired a new mouse that takes up less space and requires less movement to operate, so less of a problem than I thought. Lots of programmable buttons that I'll probably never use. Oh well! I recommend it highly for the comfortable hand position.

reviews.title: Great keyboard
reviews.text: Everybody who uses my computer hates it because the key position is a little different than what they are used too.  But I love it!  I've been using it for a long while, but spilled my coffee on the keyboard and needed a new one.  I won't use any other.

reviews.title: i love these types of key boards
reviews.text: I am still adjusting to the lay out compared to the keyboard I use at work.  I like it.  keys seem to work well.  It is a bit loud clicking the keys.  it is very comfortable.

reviews.title: Great keyboard for the price.
reviews.text: This keyboard is nice although a little bulky. I think lots of assumptions were made in the ergonomic design since my palms are just *slightly* more tilted than what the design accommodates, but it is nevertheless a great keyboard.  Some people here complained of the loudness of the keys, but I kind of enjoy it.... makes you feel like you are actually getting work done.

reviews.title: My Favorite keyboard
reviews.text: This is by far my favorite keyboard for both home and office. It has a lot of extra buttons and features that i don't use but it is nice to have when i do - though i LOVE the fact that it has a calculator button, i use this all the time. A few people say that the keyboard is loud as they comment on my typing speed.  The reason for the 4/5 instead of 5/5 star rating is it seems that i have to replace the keyboard every few years... The one i had at home started pressing keys randomly and eventually wouldn't stop - i had that keyboard for about 3 or 4 years. The soft material to rest your palms on has started to come apart at work - i also have had problems with the color fading drastically where the palms rest - i think i've had this one for about 2 years now. There are also a lot of spots for dirt, dust and other stuff to collect and can be a bit time consuming to thoroughly clean.

reviews.title: Every comfortable, especially if you're a bigger person. Ergonomics are great and personalized programing features are a great!
reviews.text: I hate to say I love it because I got it for work, but...it works very well and makes being in front of a computer working all day better because it works so well. Once I got the programing figured out I realized how much more this can do than my other keyboards and it made it even better.

reviews.title: Doesn't last more than a year or so
reviews.text: We've been using these keyboards for many years because of the ergonomic styling. We had to replace them every FEW years, but we lived with it.  Now they break down EVERY YEAR.  Keys stop working properly (have to hit them hard) and then they just suddenly stop working, period.  We have carefully taken them apart, cleaned them, put them back together (no easy task with 21 screws - YES, I did mean to type 21 - to remove from the bottom just to get inside).  When we started buying these they were about $28. Now the regular cost is closer to $40. Too much to have to make so many replacements.  If anyone finds a better one, please be sure to let me know.  Thanks.

reviews.title: Fantastic!
reviews.text: I've bought this keyboard three times - one for work, one for home (which the wife stole) and another for home. Fantastic!

reviews.title: AWESOME
reviews.text: I've always heard that an ergonomic keyboard was much better for you, so finlly I decided to bite the bullet and buy it.  At first I hated it.  I went from typing 60 words per minute down to 40, no joke. But, as time marchs on I love this thing.  It is now easier for me to use the ergonomic keyboard rather than the old kind.  I've also noticed that my shoulders don't hurt at the end of a long typing day either. Please remember this, if you decide to buy it, give yourself about 1-2 weeks to adjust.

reviews.title: Replacement died after 4 months
reviews.text: Very big and clunky.  Really never adjusted to the oversized stuff, even after all this time.  Works ok, better for large hands.  Update: December 2015  Replacement bought in the early summer died today,  Again the letters on the left side were disappearing.  All but a few were gone on the old keyboard, but at least it survived for few years.

reviews.text: Comfortable, better than a standard keyboard.

reviews.title: Negative Review Withdrawn
reviews.text: General use and a lot of Sudoku. To illuminate keyboard bought a WIFI operatized  reading lamp. Thereafter, when I tried to log in, computer stopped recognizing signals from Macally's keyboard after registering first two or four letters of the password . Ergo, no log in. Spent two hours in panic with network provider before I swapped out and went back to older, wider, WIRED keyboard. May have been WIFI interference from lamp and not any problem w/Maclly's keyboard that I first suspected and complained about.

reviews.title: “Wireless” Misleading Product Description
reviews.text: It’s a nicely designed keyboard, very aesthetically pleasing – however that is meaningless when you buy a wireless keyboard & it doesn’t function wirelessly. This keyboard only works on my MacBook Pro if it is plugged in. I have left it plugged in to charge for the recommended time, & it will not hold a charge. When I unplug it to use it wirelessly with the 2.4 G setting, the typing response starts to lag, and then the keyboard will lose its charge within five minutes. If I restart the process and plug it in it will work. I’ve also attempted to connect it to my MacBook Pro via Bluetooth and it will not recognize. Also, it does not have a USB port on the side, so if you are used to plugging in mouse transceivers, you are out of luck. Plugged it in, it worked immediately without even consulting the manual.  A godsend since I was having to reach nearly a yard to my laptop keyboard, which I could barely see. (I need a monitor and other externals.)  Thank you, Macally! If something goes wrong I'll report it but for now this was easy and led to a huge sigh of relief.

reviews.text: There are some minor details that make this keyboard great, the rounded bevel at the bottom of the keyboard is great, the power, shift lock, and function lock lights at the top right. The feel of the keys is great and the raised home keys (f/j) are great for finding placement really easy.  The ONLY issue if I had to find a negative, is I wish the cmd key was a little bigger and the fn key could be smaller to give it the room I'd like.  I am using it on a macbook air and I am coming from a bluetooth apple keyboard which kept disconnecting.  Definitely recommend this for those that are ok with wired keyboards. (My personal preference)

reviews.title: Customer Service
reviews.text: Since it is so easy to buy almost anything on Amazon, I want to discuss customer service. Not Amazon customer service which I have always found to be excellent. No, I want to write about my experience with Macally. I bought this keyboard in November 2020. It worked fairly well well except for the Caps lock light which I didn't care about at the time.  In September of 2021 the keyboard got really finicky, dropping the first letter of a sentence when I was typing and it began to start getting really weird. Finally it literally stopped working -- I mean my Mac Pro wouldn't even recognize it in the system preferences.  I checked it out with another computer and realized that it must be broken. WHAT TO DO. At first I thought of calling Amazon but I realized they usually only allow returns for 30 days. I decided to look up Macally's customer service phone number because I noticed that the keyb…

reviews.title: Key labels rub off & shift key adds symbol intermittently
reviews.text: I love that this keyboard is so much quieter than others and the key style allows for fewer crumbs and such to become lodged in the keyboard if you eat at your desk while you’re working. My complaint though, is that after only a month of use, you can see in my photo that the S, D, & C letters are already becoming worn. I don’t have to look at the keyboard to type, but it’s frustrating that the key labels are so quickly rubbed off. I use this keyboard with my office laptop, so it gets 40hrs a week of work, but I hadn’t imagined I’d be seeing the key labels rub off so quickly. Very disappointed about that.  Update: in addition to the key labels wearing off, at fewer than two full months of use, I am now experiencing an issue where the shift key inserts the pipe symbol “|” intermittently when I’m using it. Very maddening. I no longer recommend this keyboard.

reviews.title: Small Size and Quiet

It immediately began working the moment I plugged in the nano USB receiver into my Chromebox. Worked flawlessly and quietly. As a writer, I am on the keyboard 6-10 hours a day and I have worn out two keyboards by wearing off the lettering, but to be truthful, I put the small keyboard away after the day's end, not for any problems with it, just that I realized that I needed to weight and feel of the heavier, larger keyboard. reviews.title: Great Keyboard - Bad Reliability Plus Non-Existent Support
reviews.text: Ordered this roughly a year ago. Started having problems with the mouse within a few months, with the mouse not holding a charge. Got the product replaced under warranty. Replacement mouse never would connect via the USB dongle consistently. 10 months in or so, my keyboard started acting up and, despite being plugged in via USB-C on my desk, continually shows out of power / red light. When I move it to Bluetooth it strangely works, so it can't be out of power. Reached out to Azio support and got crickets. I was worried that I might not like using it, but it's simplified use of the computer having the keyboard and mouse in one small unit, and only takes up one USB slot for the receiver. What would I change? I'd have liked scrolling to have been built into the side of the touchpad. Instead, I have to use the arrow keys to scroll up and down. I'd also have liked the touchpad to be a little less sensitive. The arrow on the desktop moves just a bit as you're removing your finger from the pad, which is a little annoying. reviews.title: Mini Keyboard with Full Size Quality
reviews.text: I have always used full size keyboards before and find this one is easier to type on plus takes up less space. This board does not have a number keyboard on the right and the number keys at the top are used for numerical entries. It is so small and yet so easy to type on you'll be very happy with it. It is 10 and 3/4 inches wide and 5 1/2 inches tall which makes it the smallest keyboard ever and works great with tablets for on the go working. I have mine hooked into a desktop computer and it saves so much space on my desk! You cannot go wrong with this one.

reviews.title: key spacing a little too close together for my taste
reviews.text: I got this for the illumination and nice compact layout (cursor keys under the right SHIFT key.)  Has typical cheap-keyboard issues such as limited N-key-rollover (can't type right-shift "DE" together, without lifting the "D" key.) The keyboard is very "quiet," if you like that sort of thing. I prefer a little more tactile feedback. The keys are only spaced at 18mm pitch. Standard keyboard spacing is 19mm pitch (or 19.05mm if you are _very_ picky.) Finally, the control-key layout is Windows-style with no option to switch to Mac-style. I ended up donating this to a thrift store. Someone will be thrilled. Replaced it with the more-expensiv (but worth it) model Perixx PERIBOARD-428 RGB, which has none of these issues (except the Windows-centric control-keys.

reviews.title: Nice little keyboard, but...
reviews.text: I like this keyboard, and it does everything I need, but the printing on the keys is starting to rub off just a couple months after I got it.  It's a good thing I can mostly type without looking, because pretty soon the letter keys are all going to be blank!

reviews.title: No volume control
reviews.text: Maybe I'm ancient but I didn't know volume control on a keyboard was optional. So be aware that this one does not have volume control buttons. I wish I could return it but it's too late.

reviews.title: A physical keyboard for mobile devices.
reviews.text: No batteries to charge, or chargers to loose.  Plug the keyboard into a USB hub, which is connected to a mobile device, and your phone or tablet is halfway to all the ability of a full sized laptop.  It makes my smart phone twice as useful, and the keyboard fits in my cargo pockets and my large jacket pockets.

reviews.title: Great size
reviews.text: Like the smaller size keyboard compared to full size. I'm not a touch typist. I hunt and peck and with this size m\keyboard my hand doesn't have to move so far around the keyboard. The down side is the lack of a number pad. Using the numbers across the top is cumbersome if you have previously used a keyboard with a number pad. Also, and this is important, there is only 1 control key and it is on the left side, so if you are a one handed typist like me you often must use your left hand for the 'control +' function. I wish it was possible to program a few function keys. Also there are no instructions either in the package or on line

reviews.title: Well made comfortable for small hands

reviews.title: Plenty large for big fingers
reviews.text: Got an L-shaped desk, with 2 pullout PC keyboard/mouse trays, but one tray is not very wide.  Was glad to find this keyboard, which fits with mouse/mouse pad perfectly in tray with a couple of inches to spare!). Keyboard has excellent action; no sticking at all. The backlight feature is awesome, especially in the evening/low light.  I'm very picky and critical, but now I know I know WHY! It's because I remember excellent products like this and think, why can't all products be this good?

reviews.title: Good back-lit keyboard
reviews.text: It's a good back-lit keyboard.  Quiet, small sized which is great for using the mouse right next to it, and uses USB so no need for charging and lagging issues with Bluetooth.  Uses Fn + F8 key to get 4 lighting effects:  High, Med, Low, and off.  There are 3 LED lights for caps lock, scroll lock, but not sure what the last one is for.  It comes with a small manual but only has warnings and such which don't really mean anything to the average consumer.  Disappointing for a German designed product.  My only wish is that it had a Ctrl key on the right side.  I didn't notice anything wrong with the keys like some were saying.
