reviews.title: Easy to Read, Odd Layout Keyboard
reviews.text: Love the large font and striking blue illumination of this keyboard.  Great for tire old eyes or typing in a poorly lit room.  I am struggling with the keyboard layout as there is a column of keys to the right of the Enter.  Instead of Home, Page Up, Page Down, and End being shift keys on the numeric keypad or being above the typical QWERTY layout, they are instead in a column on the right so I constantly hit Page Down instead of Enter.  Also, the Home key is to the right of the backspace key, so my cursor often goes back to the beginning of a line instead of back one character because I hit one key too far to the right.  This really has slowed my typing as this arrangement is unusual.  Even laptops with small space for keyboards have the more traditional layout.

reviews.title: Easy to see the keys in low light areas

reviews.title: Keys are hard to press
reviews.text: I ordered this keyboard due to wanting a smaller one that the one I am currently using.  I have tiny hands so the smaller keyboards I can type faster on.  They keys are close together just like that of a laptop which is one of the reasons I wanted it.  However, with that being said I used it for maybe two days and right back in the box it went.  The keys are very hard to press and I even checked the "Sticky Key" setting, nope not the issue.  I am not sure why the keyboard is like this or maybe this is a bad one, needless to say I am back to using my old one again.  I do like the lighted feature I am using a red one now and the blue seemed to be a bit brighter than my red one.  A way to turn down the lighting would be a nice feature.  Overall I can't give it more than two stars due to the fact that I can't even use it because you have to be a pro wrestler to push the keys down.

reviews.title: A kicky Keyboard brightens things up.  Nice change of pace!
reviews.text: [[VIDEOID:6d7441bd4559a7ba77f6cf4452cd24dd]] Every keyboard in my house is... pretty much the same.  But now.... there's a fresh breeze.  The only desktop type unit I have is my server hiding in part of the "mancave".  I picked up this keyboard to brighten up that dungeon.  The KNOWSQT rounded keys remind me of the old style manual typewriters I grew up on- round keys and a bit more travel.  It's not as much travel as it was then, and the effort level is the same as today's keyboards.  It's a "wired" keyboard, plugs into any USB A type port, and is plug and play.  I like the big red ESC key, the Green Num Lock/Caps Lock lights, and the white expanse of keys.  It's not a listed feature, but I feel a bit more... creative at it than usual.  A feature I'm just loving- is that, when you press the FN button and F11 (which has a little lock icon on it), the keyboard won't accept any typed input…

reviews.title: I just love this keyboard.

reviews.title: Nice replacement keyboard with a twist
reviews.text: I spilled an entire cup of hot coffee in the keyboard that came with my desktop and even after cleaning and drying there were some keys that just wouldn't work, so I thought I'd try this groovy retro keyboard. It plugged right in a USB port with no fiddling required. The first thing I noticed was the color. I dig it. The pastel greens and blues really set this keyboard apart from my old drab black one. I took a few minutes to  get used to the feel of the keys. They require a tad more push than a standard keyboard, but I like the tactile feel. I also like the feel of the round keys. It even comes with a cool little crumb sweeper brush, because toast, you know. I'm really quite pleased with this keyboard. Five stars.

reviews.title: I love this cool little keyboard!
reviews.text: This is a great little keyboard!  But not as little as the tiny thing that came with my new iMac...that thing is just too small to get into a good groove when typing.  It is standard USB-A, so if you have USB-C connections on your computer, you will need an adapter...they are easy to find and inexpensive.  The pop-up feet on the bottom, help with the ergonomics, but I wouldn't say it's any more ergonomic than the average keyboard.  I don't have any trouble typing on it, after a few minutes of getting used to the slightly deeper presses you need to make.  I don't feel any fatigue, though.  I enjoy the more tactile feel of this keyboard, as opposed to most laptop keyboards.  This keyboard has such a cool, retro look, and it totally beats both the tiny iMac keyboard and the boring extra black keyboard I was using when I needed to type a lot.

reviews.title: Beware of the Shape of the RETURN Key -- ISO vs ANSI
reviews.text: I really like this keyboard, generally. Easy to see, quiet, nice touch, nice throw length for each keypress.  But, specifically, I simply cannot use it because of the shape of the return key.  For years I have typed using a horizontally-shaped return key the ANSI standard.  This keyboard is an ISO standard, and has a vertical return key, with the backslash key next to it, right where my pinky has been hitting the return key for...well, forever.  I literally popped the backslash key off the keyboard because I was hitting it so often. I may glue a plastic extension onto the return key to make it wider and just lose the backslash key. Or buy an ANSI keyboard.  Bottom line: when choosing a keyboard, be aware of the Return key's shape. Turns out I want an ANSI, not an ISO.

reviews.title: Keyboard works fine, trackball is tricky to use
reviews.text: No complaints about the keyboard, works fine. I have it mounted to an LCD on an arm where it's used as a server monitor on a KVM. The problem with this unit is the trackball (about 5/8" diameter, small) is VERY light with no resistance, and it's hard to use it accurately. With the positioning of it, it is obviously designed for one-handed operation, except it is nearly impossible to lift your thumb from the trackball (say to press a button) without the cursor moving. If the ball was weighted at all it would help considerably. If this item got anything more than very occasional use, I would have to replace it with the trackpad version that I am sure would be MUCH more usable. I ended up adding a regular mouse at this point as the trackball is virtually unusable.

reviews.title: great 1990's throwback keyboard for system builders
reviews.text: It's 2016, you say. And here you are, on Amazon, looking at keyboards. Why in the world would I buy a PS/2 keyboard? PS/2 was introduced nearly 30 years ago (1987!), and the currently reality is that not a single laptop in the market supports this input, and even desktops are starting to phase them out. Well, as sexy and shiny USB is, the geek in all of us seem to still prefer PS/2 when it comes to debugging system builds.  Frantically hitting DEL, F8, F9, or whatever cryptic combination of keys to get into the BIOS is a well known thing. Turns out, when motherboards are on the fritz, the USB controllers sometimes stop responding, leaving PS/2 as the only way to get access to the BIOS. That alone makes this keyboard worth it's weight in gold, because as far as I can tell, it's the ONLY new PS/2 keyboard available on the market. reviews.text: Using it to restore the full-sized wired keyboard functionality (well mostly) that I have on my older iMac. I do a lot of numeric entry (spreadsheet-Excel type stuff), so missed the keypad on my wired keyboard when I ordered the wireless version with my newer iMac. This separate Belkin Bluetooth Wireless Keypad gives me most of that without the wires. It has exactly the same styling as the Apple keyboard so they can sit side by side and look great. Bonus, if you are left handed, the keypad can be on the left or anywhere (within 30 foot Bluetooth range), really. Works well with two AA rechargeable LiIon batteries, as well as disposables, just like the wireless Apple keyboard, Magic Trackpad, etc. Wired keyboard has 3 more function keys than this combo, plus not all included keys work exactly the same for all applications. e.g. Control + does not insert cells in Excel (use Control I instea…

reviews.title: It's pretty. Very pretty.  But that's it.
reviews.text: The good: Sleek design, quality weight and construction.  Unfortunately that is where it ends.  The bad:  Save yourself some frustration.  There is a power button on the right side that you have to turn on.  You know the battery slot?  It's on the opposite end.  Press it and the light comes in and you can easily pair it.  This is missing from the pairing instructions and I had to dig online for almost an hour to find this information.  Delete, page up, page down, and clear buttons DELETE ABSOLUTELY NOTHING.  That renders the product fairly useless in my opinion  If you bought this thinking you were going to use it as a calculator, forget it.  The only thing you can do is to enter numbers and the + or - sign. If you enter = and then enter, it will not add or do any other mathematical function.  I will most likely be returning it.

reviews.title: Minimalism taken too far
reviews.text: Our late 2015 iMac arrived with a compact wireless Bluetooth keyboard and a wireless touch mouse. At times I've wished it had also included a numeric keypad, so was looking forward to adding this one.  This keypad is listed as matching the iMac keyboard, but that's no longer true. It DOES match my old wireless Mac keyboard that ran on AA batteries, but does NOT match the rechargeable keyboard shipped with our late 2015 iMac. It's about twice as high.  But that's minor. What is NOT minor is the almost complete lack of instructions. I was able to follow the one page quick install guide, though it took two tries of installing batteries using a quarter to open and close the battery cap before I was able to get the keypad to switch on (thankfully indicated with a tiny green LED at the top right.) It then showed up on the iMac Bluetooth preference screen. I paired it, and was then asked by my …

reviews.title: Excellent keypad.  No issues at all.  Only observation is that it is big...takes up a lot of room.
reviews.text: This is great.  I have a MacBook and iMac and am using the latest OS Sierra and have no issues at all with this keypad.  It connected flawlessly.  Works great.  Some issues ...  it is big.  Much bigger than my wireless keyboard and trackpad.  I have to juggle things a bit to fit it on the desk.  Then again I don't use it unless I am planning on doing a lot of number entering.  While the page up and page down buttons are nice and work well as do the home and end buttons, it would have been nice to have up/down, left/right arrows as well.  I have purchased a few other brands of wireless keypads and have not been satisfied.  This one, other than the big size, which does come in handy while entering numbers, is spot on.  No issues in connecting, maintaining the connection, etc.  Just have to remember to turn it off to conserve the batteries.

I loved the original mouse that came with my Apple iMAC so I decided to simply replicate it.  The good news is that I ordered this mouse and, yes it is just like the one I have on my desk top computer, except it doesn't use batteries since it is fully rechargeable using a USB cable connected to your computer. The bad news is that I didn't read the product description closely enough and did not realize this mouse WILL NOT WORK with the older IOS software on my 11 year-old MacBook.  Read the description carefully before ordering.  Fortunately, it crossed my mind to use this new mouse on my desk top computer that has newer IOS software - and use my older mouse on my MacBook Pro. I am happy.

description: M325 Wireless Mouse features micro-precise scrolling and a tilt wheel to provide speed and accuracy

reviews.title: Basic, colorful, reasonably priced mouse for someone who needs nothing more than this
reviews.text: Love the color and design of this mouse. It comes with one battery already inserted and it is as easy as plugging the tiny wireless receiver into a USB port, having the system automatically set it up, then turning it on. The mouse is responsive, has a center wheel, and the typical left and right buttons. This is a reasonably-priced (cheap) basic mouse because I do not need all the bells and whistle and I do not do gaming.  Be aware that the "c" in the M325c means that the receiver is NOT a unifying receiver. This means only the mouse will work with this receiver and I cannot pair a keyboard with it without plugging in another wireless receiver into another USB port. If it had the star logo on the receiver, I would be able to pair a keyboard with that one receiver.  I put a link to an article about this difference in the comments section of my review for those who are interested.

reviews.title: Great for Small Hand and General Browsing; Not Good for Detailed Work
reviews.text: This mouse is adorable and perfect for a small hand. Please note this is my 4th Logitech mouse so I'm very familiar with this brand. Compared to the other 3 mice that I have, there's A LOT of play with this mouse. This decreases the accuracy of cursor/arrow, i.e. getting it to point where you want it to point.  There isn't a way to improve accuracy.  It's great for general browsing, but is frustrating to use with Excel spreadsheets and when creating presentations in Power Point.

reviews.title: Worked out how I had hoped
reviews.text: I bought this mouse because I was having problems with pain and numbness in my hand.  I use the mouse for both gaming and work, so it needs to be fast, responsive, and comfortable. It took me a few days to get used to, but now that I have, I will never go back to a regular mouse. The pain and numbness in my hand went away. It is fast and responsive for gaming, and totally adjustable. I was able to assign keys to mouse buttons, and they are all within easy reach. I have larger hands, glove size large, and this fits my hand perfectly. I can reach all the buttons easily without moving my hand around.  It is a larger, heavier mouse. If you have small hands, it may not be very comfortable and easy to use for you.

reviews.title: Disappointed... created pressure on wrist
reviews.text: Was looking forward to this mouse.  Construction and scrolling feel very very premium.  Clicking buttons have way too much travel to activate, but, most importantly, with or without the wrist extension, it sits too high to be comfortable.  Pairing can be done with up to three devices: Two via bluetooth and the third one via its USB-A dongle. Connecting to different devices was effortless.  Compared to other ergonomic mice, this one is more vertical and taller.  As a result, the user's hand is more in a vertical position, causing pressure on the outer side of the wrist.  This happens with or without the wrist extension.  With the wrist extension, moving the mouse involves moving the entire forearm.  This would be great if I had to immobilize my wrist for whatever reason.  But not great to draw with the mouse or for finer gestures.  The charging port on the mouse is USB-C, but the radio do…

reviews.title: Should measure finger length not palm width for sizing
reviews.text: You need extra long fingers to reach the l/r buttons.  Stretching to reach the l/r buttons puts the palm rest in the wrong place, so that unless you keep the wrist bent inwards all the time, at almost a 90 degree angle to the arm, the wrist will fall off the rest. It is much too easy to hit the back/forwards buttons, just trying to get a grip on the very smooth surface mouse.  A dedicated groove for the thumb to rest in and grip the mouse would help keep it off the back/forwards buttons. The seller describes smaller mice but does not actually offer them for sale, so I have to buy a smaller mouse from another seller. Pretty lights but not an ergonomic fit to hands.

reviews.title: a little too vertical…?
reviews.text: I find that I nearly have to tilt my arm too far over to use this the way it’s shown in the product image, so now rather than soreness from tilting flat I get soreness in the elbow from over tilting the opposite way. I find it most comfortable if I rest my pointer finger on top…. But then my wrist hovers a bit. Batter is great and easy to recharge with a usb c. There is a little holder for the dongle if you travel from work to home (or someplace else) with your mouse. I prefer to pack mine along and use it in place of a laptop track pad. Mouse sleeps when not in use and easily lasts weeks on a charge. I don’t have any glitchy interruptions in mouse movement until the battery gets a little low.

The mouse is just too big for my small hand. To give an idea of my hand size, I wear a size small women’s glove.  My hand doesn’t fit naturally on the mouse. It is just ok.  The quality is not nearly as solid as the old models were.  The mouse itself works fine but the scroll wheel is very clicky and not smooth at all.  The buttons are much more flimsy. Pros:  Rechargeable (this is an improvement for sure) Comfortable Works on lots of surfaces Good battery life  Cons: Picks up weird movements sometimes The scroll wheel button isn't a button.  The scroll wheel is my biggest issue with this "new and improved" version, and it's because the scroll wheel button isn't a button, it's a toggle to switch between clicks while scrolling and smooth scrolling.  As a gamer the scroll wheel is an important button, and having it be behind the scroll wheel is counter intuitive, and the fact that this clicky/not clicky feature exists in it's place is absolutely silly.

reviews.title: It's an upgrade from my beloved M510's.. But not by much
reviews.text: I just want to give a shout out to the Logitech M510.. That mouse is solid as a rock, I've been rocking those mice for several years now but have been wanting to upgrade for some time since mice have come a long way.. Honestly, the M510 is still perfectly fine even in 2020.  Let me start with the feel, I don't have particularly large hands. They're pretty average I'd say.. With that being said, this is a pretty small mouse and definitely does take some getting used to. I've owned it for a little over a month now and I'm honestly still not 100% comfortable with it, but I'm starting to get there.. If you have large hands I would completely skip this mouse, you will not be comfortable at all.  The buttons are a bit sensitive which also takes getting used to, I have found myself miss-clicking many times because of how much more sensitive and how little response it takes for it to register a …

Mac Mini, Custom Asus desktop, Surface pro 3, all of these different devices... and this is the second Mx Anywhere 2 that i have tested, same result.  Great mouse, can connect multiple devices, can now recharge the battery. It's unfortunate this will never compare to the true reliability and performance of the Original MX Anywhere mouse. Get back to the roots Logitech!!!!!!!

reviews.title: Defective from the factory
reviews.text: Logitech used to be the by far best peripheral equipment for computers. I loved their stuff! When you bought a Logitech keyboard or mouse you knew it would perform flawlessly and last for a long time. Sadly this is no longer true. Logitech's quality has deteriorated hugely in the past couple of years. I bought two of these high priced mice because they are perfect size for a traveler like me and both mice after about six months or so developed button issues and scroll wheel issues. Buttons would no longer function and the scroll wheel became unbalanced so that on hyper scroll it would at the end of the scroll try to roll so the unbalanced part of the wheel would be on the bottom scrolling your page up and down in front of you. After a loooong warranty process that took me two weeks of daily emails with Logitech "customer service" (not really a service but more a pain in the neck)…

reviews.title: Two Anywhere MX Mice Have Dreaded Double-Click problem
reviews.text: This is now affected by the dreaded double-click problem.  If you google Logitech mice, there are remedies to take it apart to fix it. I've reloaded the drivers, changed the double-click speed, nothing helps.  I'm not going to fiddle with taking a mouse apart and soldering a micro-switch.  I have two Anywhere MX that are doing this.  They worked great, that's why I picked up another one for work.  I bought this one in May and the other last October.  I kept thinking that I was doing something wrong but I don't think so.  Beware. :(

reviews.title: Great When New, But Fail Over Time
reviews.text: To be honest, I'm really tired of these mice failing.  They work great at first, then eventually quit scrolling or, worse, get stuck in scroll mode and drive the cursor to the bottom of the page for no reason. Two have failed on me. The first was purchased in 2011 for $36, the second in 2014 for $30. Both failed to scroll reliably and made using them impossible. Other, cheaper, wireless mice work better, or at least longer.  This mouse has nice features like left/right scrolling by tilting the scroll wheel and they work on many different surfaces, but those features fall by the wayside if the thing doesn't work at all after some time.  I've tried blowing it out with compressed air to clear debris, but it didn't fix it. Haven't come to taking it apart and cleaning it, as some proffer, because it's simply not worth the time.  For how much these mice cost -- $66 for the two -- they should b…

Also, to note: the mouse will operate perfectly on just one battery at a time if you can only find one spare around the house. reviews.title: Ergonomic but moves pressure point to side of wrist.
reviews.text: This being the first time I have used an ergonomic mouse I had certain expectations regarding how it would solve the problem I usually have with mice.  While it removes the pressure points from the center of the wrist the tilt move that point to the bone on the side of your wrist. This is easily cured by a cushioned mouse pad. So why then use it if you still need a soft spot for your wrist? Ease of use! The mouse has a variable sensitivity rate that is nice and high for us power users (move the mouse a fraction and you can span the entire screen), or dial back the sensitivity for doing very fine and slow cursor movements. The two buttons on the side are excellent as the back and forward buttons. I have become an active user of the back button. Saves having to move the mouse to the screen icon to go back. The Bluetooth connection works about 90% of the time. When you walk away for a bit, …

reviews.title: Great Mouse!
reviews.text: This is a great mouse for hand position and comfort. It is fantastic on battery life! I charge it once every 2-3 weeks which far exceeds many other mice I have that cost me a whole lot more.  However, there is one con to this mouse. The location of switching connection type is right under your thumb (see picture). This can cause normal movement to bump the button changing your connection and causing you to temporarily lose your mouse connection. A quick fix, sure, just hit the button a few more times to return. But annoying to be working along and suddenly lose your mouse.

reviews.title: Love Ergonomic Grip.  Hate Functionality.
reviews.text: I love the vertical ergonomic grip, but wish it was it was slightly bigger or came in different sizes.  However, it is nearly impossible for me to accurately select text to cut and paste.  I don't know if this problem is my coordination, uncertainty about how far I need to push the button down to create a click or lag between clicking and the click being received by the computer.  Select a whole page worth of text is nearly impossible for me.  Not sure if optical vs laser is part of my problem.  Using in Bluetooth mode.  Am constantly hitting the button for switching communication mode which is stupidly placed just below my thumb.  Mouse is slow to wake up and connect, so I cycle through the communication modes instead.  Really wanted to like this mouse, but now looking for another one.

reviews.title: Works great
reviews.text: I love how this mouse works although I can't seem to get the mouse to set up with Bluetooth. I use it on wireless and also, I have no idea what voice buttons are for so I'll have to research that, but overall it shuts off automatically after 6 minutes of non-usage. It's lasted over 4 days without a charge, that's great.

reviews.text: So far so good... Pairs fast and movement is good. Getting use to the gesturing. VERY small, imaged bigger. Very solid build.  I'd buy it again...  3 months later - LOVE this thing! reviews.title: I normally love Logitech products but this one missed the mark
reviews.text: I normally love Logitech products but this one missed the mark. It has a great design and is easy to use. But the battery life is terrible. It will last maybe two days and then die. It doesn't take too long to charge but you pretty much have to remember to charge this each day, which can be annoying if you are constantly on the go. I would rather check out the Logitech MX anywhere mouse instead. It's not Bluetooth, but at least I don't have to worry about charging it.

reviews.title: Has a Mind of It's Own
reviews.text: I have been using this mouse for about three months and just ordered Logitech's MX's Master from Amazon to replace it.  I thought it was kind of elegant looking and had fairly good reviews and was cheaper than the Apple Magic Mouse 2 but similar enough to justify the purchases but I have not been happy with it for the following reasons.  It is very small and so not particularly comfortable and feels awkward to use.  "The straw that broke the camel's back" was the inadvertent and unexpected activation of the zoom function when scrolling and the occasional unexplained loss of the scroll function.  These two problems, which were annoying and time consuming to compensate for when working, was too much.  So, I will no longer use the Mouse on my home computer.  It probably will be OK to use with my laptop when on a trip.  I would not recommend it for regular use and certainly not for w…

reviews.title: It's OK, but not that great
reviews.text: It's OK, but not that great.  The good news is, it has a small travel footprint and convenient blue tooth interface. The not so good news is that it is very awkward and noisy during use.  It may be a better choice for someone with tiny hands, but I have much difficulty with accurately clicking and scrolling. The Apple Magic Mouse is the gold standard that I compare all portable blue tooth mice to. And the Apple mouse has user replaceable batteries which is important when all rechargeable batteries eventually fail to hold a charge, and you are stuck with just a fancy paperweight.

reviews.title: Very small and cheap feeling
reviews.text: I was hoping this would sort of have the feel and functionality of the Apple Magic Mouse but it's much smaller and cheap feeling than I expected. We ended up replacing it after a couple months. It's so light a small gust of wind could blow it away.

reviews.title: Battery Drawbacks OS X
reviews.text: I like this mouse, but the battery runs out with little warning.  You cannot use it while charging because the port is on the bottom. Bad design choice.  The Logitech software will give you a low battery warning, but by the time you get it the mouse is about to die.  Even on the Bluetooth menu, you do not see battery percentage. A couple of minutes of charging will give you an hour of battery, so the battery drawbacks are not dire.  Other than that, it is very good.  Scrolling is not quite as smooth as with magic mouse, but close.  The size is a huge advantage, great for traveling.  Clicking does not require nearly as much force as on Apple's Magic Mouse.  NOTE: Mac users must install the Logitech drivers, or the mouse will be difficult to use for scrolling. The Logitech preference panel is LAME -- a panel with a single button that launches a standalone app called Logitech Options.  Over…

It is small, so if you are looking for a mouse for heavy usage this one might be too small and cause some discomfort/cramping. For light use and portability this is a good fit.

reviews.title: Not a terrible mouse
reviews.text: If you need an ultra portable mouse that fits nicely in your pocket, this mouse is good.  Problem is the touch pad implementation.  My biggest issue is that you cant hold LEFT and RIGHT mouse buttons at the same time.  I dont like the scroll, instead of a normal scroll wheel, you can just flick with your finger, on this mouse you have to remove your hand and use it as a touchpad scroller.  The primary reason I bought this mouse, was because a cheaper mouse wasnt working well with the Logitech K810 keyboard, but after a windows update, that was fixed, so I keep this mouse around for the rare case of having to have a mouse in my pocket.

reviews.title: Definitely not for me, but maybe for my sons
reviews.text: First for pros: This is tiny, maybe about 3/4 inch thick at it's widest. Sleek, attractive and would probably delight any techie who is looking for some kind of new hip gadget. For the cons: It's too small. There are no indentations to grip the mouse and it is difficult to click on any area that you are trying to. Navigation/movement of the mouse is ok, it's the clicking that is difficult to do (and it becomes quite annoying to say the least). Within using this for a full day I, unfortunately, reverted back to my old wireless HP mouse. Maybe I am just old school and set in my ways (I am in my 50's), so I will be 'loaning' this to my techie son to give it a go. Maybe he will appreciate this better and will be able to navigate easier than I could. If that is the case, I will revisit my review and update accordingly.

reviews.text: This Logitech Pop Mouse is stylish in rose, contemporary and lightweight. For reference, I wear a women’s size L or XL in Isotoner gloves, size M in disposable vinyl gloves and size L in nitrile gloves. The size and style of the Pop Mouse seem better suited to a teen or others with small hands.  This mouse is quiet, fast and responsive. It can be customized using the Logitech software compatible with Windows 10 and Mac OS 10.15, 11 and 12. The software does not work with iOS, so the emoji shortcut feature won’t work with iPad. It was impressive, however, how quickly the mouse Bluetooth paired with my iPad mini…

reviews.title: Quiet and super fast Bluetooth setup - no Emoji function with iPadOS

It was seriously so easy to just pair and go, and I love how it can be paired with three different things (just push a little button on the bottom of the mouse to switch between computers/iPads). It feels okay in my hand - not the highest quality I’ve seen (plastic is very basic and it is pretty lightweight as well), but it doesn’t feel cheap. The color is so fun, which is the main reason I got it. Also it is very quiet and doesn’t have any loud clicking. The one thing to mention is that the circle button under the scrolling wheel doesn’t have any functionality with an iPad. Nothing was happening when I kept clicking it to try and use the emoji shortcut, so after heading over to Logitech’s website i saw “*Emojis and software are currently supported on Windows® and macOS only.” So maybe iPadOS will eventually sup…

There is still feedback on the wheel when it is spun, but not a complete "click". The buttons do give a click feel, but the distance to click is just a little less than my old mouse.  The biggest thing to me is that the wheel button is a bit hard to click, and takes more strength than on my old Microsoft mouse or my old Jellycomb mouse, and that is an essential button for me to orbit and pan in the software I use. I've mostly gotten used to it though.  I've tested the multi-device function, and it works well as expected. But I don't use that function often since I use it mostly on one device.

reviews.title: Fun, functional mouse! Multiple devices connection, no noise click
reviews.text: Love this!  I got it for the sole fact that it was pink and it was Logitech (a brand I trust) but I'm very glad I did because it works so well and is multifunctional.  I'm currently using this at home with my work laptop but I'm going to start taking it back and forth to work too because I love it so much.  It's so comfortable to use and it makes absolutely no noise when you click but you can feel that you did.  It glides easily across different surfaces.  It feels like quality in your hand.  You can connect it to 3 different devices effortlessly via Bluetooth so you don't have to waste a USB slot.  It comes with batteries already installed that should last a very long time.  I haven't used the emoji button yet because I'm not much of an emoji person, but that's a fun little addition.  I am very happy and will recommend this to my coworkers.

reviews.title: Is it silly to like a cute mouse?
reviews.text: I got this mouse for two reasons: it's a Logitech which is my favorite brand of mouse, and it's pink. I like that it's bluetooth as well as wireless, and it's easy to connect. Works right out of the box. Fits my hand well, smooth as glass operation, all the things I expect from a Logitech. I have only one small quibble, and unfortunately it turned out to be an issue. The cover is held in place by magnets. Not bad usually, but I dropped the mouse hours after acquiring it--I know, I know, clumsy of me--and the cover popped off. No one's fault but my own. But the left-hand button now requires me to push harder than I did before, which is a distraction when I'm using it. I can't swear the lid popping off caused the problem, but I would prefer that the lid was attached more securely, as it provides added protection to what's under it. Anyway, just a thought. Still love the mouse...

reviews.title: Ah, lovely.
reviews.text: Like I imagine many people have done here, I wanted a very quiet clicking mouse.  But I also wanted a mouse that isn't portable or compact--just a regular mouse like the one that came with your office PC.  (In the picture, the Rapoo is on the left, the other two are mice we've likely all seen/used before.)  And on that note, wired.  Not wireless.  Wireless just means the toddler runs away with it.  No, thank you.  And that's exactly what you're getting here.  Classic mouse shape, classic mouse feel.  Except one big difference, very little click click click click.  The sound is similar to if you press a key on your keyboard as softly as possible until it finally depresses.  That light thud noise of the membrane collapsing.  It's extremely quiet, but does give a nice tactile click to your finger.  And if you're like me, just wanting to play a little solitaire or what have you while the wif…

reviews.title: Jerky, and barely counts as quiet
reviews.text: The cursor spasms wildly if you move it the slightest bit off the table or mousepad, rendering this completely unusable. The cursor movement in general is jerky and not smooth. It's super lightweight, which only contributes to the problem of the spasming. It is less noisy than standard mice but it's not "silent" or even quiet compared to other silent mice I've used. In a generally noisy environment, such as a coffee shop, or next to a fan, it can pass as silent, but for use in a quiet home or library it'd be a nuisance.

reviews.title: Clicking so quiet now!
reviews.text: Substantial improvement over every other mouse as far as 'click noise.' Now I can click wildly and no one will notice. The wheel click is loud but I don't really need to use it. The wheel scroll is quiet enough that I should be able to use it sparingly. If you scroll really fast it gets louder, so if that's something you'll be using a lot and you need silence then look elsewhere.

reviews.title: Bought to have a quiet mouse.  Middle-click is REALLY LOUD.  Product fails for advertised purpose!
reviews.text: They did an awesome job on the left and right buttons, as well as the scroll wheel while using to scroll up, or down.  Clicking the scroll wheel?  It will wake a baby.  Zero stars if I could; this was advertised as "FOR QUIET ENVIRONMENTS."  Telling me I can't use one of the five functions of this mouse (in terms of buttons) in said quiet environment?  Someone's losing, and it's not me; I'm out eight bucks and it's no big deal, but this company is lying about their product and that might invite a legal solution.  Not from me, at this time; but, one should not lie, it's not good for the soul.  It opens one up for attacks, which might come far in the future.  Or at least, as far as the statute of limitations allows.

description: Product Description

Offers Ultimate Portability. The stylish, minimalist design of the Wedge Touch Mouse will allow you to be productive anytime, anywhere. It is optimized for Windows 8 navigation, works with most tablets and laptops, has wireless Bluetooth connectivity, and Blue Track technology for using on virtually any surface.
From the Manufacturer
Microsoft Wedge Touch Mouse
Compact for ultimate portability
Offers Ultimate Portability

The stylish, minimalist design of the Wedge Touch Mouse will allow you to be productive anytime, anywhere in Windows 7 and Windows 8. Wedge Touch Mouse works great with Windows 8 and the new horizontal scrolling experience on the Start Screen and in documents.

Wedge Touch Mouse features a touch sensitive surface that responds to one finger touches differently depending on where they contact the surface. Stroke with one finger vertically or horizontally to scroll. Press your left finger for "Left click". Press your right finger, while slightly lifting your left finger, for "Right click".
Wedge Touch Mouse is the perfect companion for your laptop or Windows 8 tablet when you're on the go.
Bluetooth technology means no clutter

Not only is Wedge Touch Mouse compact, it doesn't come with cables or USB transceivers. Just turn it on and connect it to your Bluetooth-enabled laptop or tablet. Additionally, BlueTrack technology means it tracks on virtually any surface, whether you're at a conference or a coffee shop.
Conserves battery power

Wedge Touch Mouse even knows how to conserve energy. When your PC or tablet is shut down or hibernating, the mouse goes into "Backpack Mode." You can throw it into your bag and not worry if you turned it off because it senses that it no longer needs to be on.

reviews.title: What I was looking for!
reviews.text: To give you a bit of background, I'm using this mouse, and it's matching keyboard [[ASIN:B008OEHPKM Microsoft Wedge Mobile Keyboard (U6R-00001)]] with a Windows 8 desktop computer that I built. I've been in IT for 14 years, and am VERY picky about my mice and keyboards, and I was hesitant to buy these items site unseen. Lucky for me, I ended up making a good choice.  First off, I HATE clutter, so the size was important to me. I realize that this mouse was built for mobile users, and a lot of expert reviews will tell you this mouse is not for every day use, but for me the smaller the better. Both the mouse and keyboard fit comfortably on my keyboard tray, and I have room to spare. Keep in mind, this mouse is TINY. My fiancé's flash drive is actually longer than the mouse is tall. If you can get around the small size, this mouse is quite functional, especially when paired with the Windows …

reviews.title: In addition to Windows, it works in varying degrees on Android and Chromebook
reviews.text: This is a handy little bluetooth mouse. If you are pressed for space, this is indeed a space saver. For example, if you have a laptop with a touchpad, you need some elbow space to use the touchpad or use an external traditional USB mouse. With this tiny one and touch scrolling, you can just move your finger up and down and left and right the mouse surface.  Despite the small size, it was surprisingly usable, even during some long sessions with a desktop computer. Obviously it can't replace a desktop mouse for power users, especially if you are used to mice, but it is good enough to get things done without getting in the way if that's the only mouse you have with you. It worked on various surfaces.  This is a really small mouse. It is roughly 5.5cm long, 6cm wide and its height ranges from around 1cm to 3cm at its highest. With the battery installed the mouse weighs 2.2 ounces. There are …

reviews.title: Works great with my Apple MacBook! Love that it's small and fits next to the trackpad.
reviews.text: I use this with my MacBook and it works great. My husband actually got it through his work and hated it, but his hands are much larger than mine, He got another mouse and gave me this one. It was a little strange getting used to the shape for a minute, but not too bad because I am used to Apple products and this operates very similarly to the Apple mouse that come with most Apple computers. The only issue I have had is that it does look connectivity on occasion and I have to pop the battery in and out. I am going to see if getting better batteries (made for electronics) helps this problem because this mouse eats regular AA batteries. This small mouse fits nicely on the surface of my MacBook right next to the trackpad. Your average Mouse is too large. This mouse travels nicely in my laptop bag. If this mouse ever breaks, or I lose it, I will definitely buy another if they are still making…

reviews.title: Super cute, very small

reviews.title: Great Mouse Alternative
reviews.text: Unique mouse.  Works with computers and tablets that have Bluetooth. Small size makes it easy to take with you.

reviews.title: Looks cool, tough to use
reviews.text: Found this mouse really uncomfortable to use - seems like they let the designers create the whole thing without any usability testing.  It's well created - it feels 'premium'.  But there is no wrist rest, and the touch scrolling didn't work well - overall it just looked a lot better than it worked!

reviews.title: Oustanding for Windows 10, tablet style computers
reviews.text: Like it or not, the Windows Start menu is no more. Thus, the right mouse button is now king in Windows 8 and 10, where adding/sorting the main screen is absolutely essential.  Unfortunately - and for tablet style computers akin to my ASUS Transformer - the trackpad is mediocre, at best. Right clicking becomes a chore, where accidental clicks/swipes create navigation chaos.  The Microsoft Wedge Touch Mouse is the panacea. Small enough to travel anywhere, ridiculously responsive, easy on/off, and a swipe function that works like a dream. The wedge shape likewise puts a traditional mouse to shame. It takes the pressure of wrists, as the fingers now run the show (based on angle). It feels really well made for something only $25 (at time of purchase).  Finally - and perhaps most importantly - this mouse paired instantly with Windows 10.

reviews.title: Small and handy.
reviews.text: Works great.  Using it here.  No problems with it, yet.  The on/off button is a bit getting used to.

reviews.title: microsoft wedge mouse
reviews.text: Its amazing but I assumed it was stationary and the top was a touch pad that would used like the pad on my laptop. its just like an optical mouse and you used it by moving it around and clicking left and right. uses a AA battery and works well.

reviews.title: I LOVE this mouse
reviews.text: I am in love with this mouse. I was looking for a travel mouse so that I wouldn't have to drag my Apple Magic Mouse around. This is one sturdy, good-looking tiny mouse. It's about half the size of my iPhone and it works with my iMac and my Kindle Fire HDX! Simply adorable. It will definitely get giggles from strangers who ask "What is that?!"

Having said that, I do like that it is Bluetooth so I don't lose the USB dongle like I have with my other mice.  I don't have a lot of USB ports on my ultrabook so I end up taking the USB dongles out for my other mice, and end up losing them.  While I like this product, I do recommend the Microsoft Arc touch mouse more, it's larger when bending it to use, but I have already lost the usb dongle of that mouse.  Sigh.

products.title: Posturite Penguin Ambidextrous Wired Ergonomic Mouse USB, Alleviates RSI, Easy-Glide, Vertical Design, PC Computer & Apple Mac Compatible (Black/Silver, Size: Large)
features: ADVANCED ERGONOMIC DESIGN: the Penguin Wired Mouse features a vertical design that sets new standards of protection against a range of upper limb conditions caused by extensive computer/laptop use, such as repetitive strain injury (RSI) and carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS)
PRECISION PERFORMANCE: adjustable 400, 600, 800 or 1200 DPI resolution optical tracking technology encourages fast and precise operating movements on a wide range of surfaces

EASY-GLIDE: symmetrical base allows the user to rest either hand comfortably alongside the vertical design, encouraging the use of the bigger muscles in the fore and upper arm to maneuver the ergo mouse. Fine cursor control is achievable with small hand and/or finger movements

AMBIDEXTROUS DESIGN: allows for easy transition between right and left-handed use, avoiding exaggerated movements of the wrist joint, which can increase pressure on the soft tissues in the carpal tunnel. When using a PC, regular switching of hands throughout the day helps prevent static muscle strain (SMS) in the arm and shoulder - a major source of discomfort in mouse work
description: The Penguin marks a major breakthrough in the battle to beat health problems created when computer users spend too much time handling a conventional mouse.

reviews.title: No Better Than a Vertical Mouse
reviews.text: In the pursuit of the ultimate couch mouse (body reclined, hand on pillow) this mouse fails. It is absolutely no different in hand rotation than a vertical mouse, which you can buy MUCH cheaper. I also did not like the width of the stick. It is way too wide. Like gripping a baseball bat. It is also heavier than any other mouse I've used. Also the base your hand rests on is very wide. So you are trying to move this heavy, wide, object across a pillow and it just creates drag, like sliding a filled coffee cup around. And all for like 70 bucks - no way! This should cost about 25 dollars. Anker's vertical mouse is at the same angle (I literally held my hand in place while the mice were switched - exact same angle), but is light as a feather, smaller with a smaller base, and your hand lays on top of it instead of gripping it. And nothing seems to beat the 3M stick mouse, which places your han…

reviews.title: Great Mouse!
reviews.text: I've been using a computer/mouse for over 30 years and have found this to be the most comfortable mouse for my hand.  It also is versatile to use with the left or right hand, the small switch on the front allows you to reverse the direction of the mouse to accommodate left or right handedness.

reviews.title: Sizing Issues.
reviews.text: I had to return this device simply because of the awful fit. After printing the hand size chart and measuring my hand against it, I ordered the appropriate size. My hand by far exceeded the diagram size for the large, however when the mouse arrived, I found it very difficult to reach the buttons.  My hand is not disproportionate. If you're a female and do not have extremely long fingers, consider buying a size smaller than the chart recommends.  The mouse was not at all difficult to adapt to using, even though I had never used anything but a standard mouse, however the stretch to reach the buttons was very uncomfortable.

reviews.title: Love this product!
reviews.text: I researched a number of vertical mice and decided to try the Penguin primarily due to the ambidextrous capability. I am right handed, but am able to use a left handed mouse. It's nice to switch back and forth every 6 months or so to rest the working arm. It fit perfectly out of the box and I adapted within the first day. Very comfortable, easy to use, sleek design, easy to set up, and affordable. I highly recommend the Penguin!! It exceeded my expectations in every way. It feels so natural in your hand. No awkward turning of the arm or wrist and no strain whatsoever, even after hours of use. Kudos to the designer!!

reviews.title: It's your hand as much as it is the mouse
reviews.text: OK.  I have a wrist and arm problem which is actually a neck problem.  I'm having surgery soon but its effects will be limited.  So, I've tried all the ergonomic mice including the much-vaulted Evoluent Vertical Mouse D.  It's a great mouse that is built like a tank, but it does not work for me.  And that's the point. A mouse that one person loves may not be loved by all.  It's a personal fit thing so quality is not the only factor.  This Penguin mouse is by far the best for me.  Some people say it doesn't feel like a quality mouse but I don't get that read from it.  It seems well built to me. So: Pros: "Joystick" shape is best for me since it does not require "sideways" pushing to click. Buttons are firm enough that I can feel the switches click. I've lost some feeling in my fingers. Ambidextrous switching via a button low in front.  Cons: DPI switch is on the bottom.  Fast switching is…

reviews.title: Its just... not good
reviews.text: The ergonomics are alright in terms of overall shape, but the buttons are very mushy and imprecise and take a fair amount of pressure to activate. The scroll wheel is the exact opposite and way to sensitive. Overall it feels like a cheap device.

reviews.title: Looks good, feels good to use, stopped working at all within two months:  dissappointed!
reviews.text: Loved it while it worked!  Then it stopped.  We changed the batteries, we charged and recharged.  Nothing helps.  Doesn't work.  For such a high price tag, I expected much better.

reviews.title: Love this mouse so much I own two
reviews.text: Cute but practical. Easy bow tie switch for left hand right hand switching. The only drawback is that the charging is a special connector instead of USB. But otherwise really like that it comes with a USB bluetooth dongle, sort of easy to lose but also keeps connection better than direct Bluetooth to the laptop.

reviews.title: the functionality of this mouse is so poor. It would take me three times as long ...
reviews.text: I have been suffering from wrist pain at work and bought this mouse to help. The vertical position did WONDERS! I was so excited. However, the functionality of this mouse is so poor. It would take me three times as long do anything on my computer because the lag time of the mouse was so bad. I have tried cleaning the bottom and the laser. I have tried turning it on and off. I have tried charging it over night and plugging the usb into a different spot. Nothing makes this go away. If I could get this fixed I would be a user for life as the comfort level of using it is so great.

reviews.title: Would not recommend to a friend.
reviews.text: I had just two weeks ago before Christmas bought and tried the Posturite Wireless Penguin Mouse though it positioned your hand in the correct position full vertical it was very cumbersome to maneuver the pointer, awkward as since your palm rest on the mouse it leaves you using your whole fore arm to maneuver the mouse not near as accurate and precise as the Anker so I had no choice but to return it.  Pros; Easy on the hand full vertical position.  Cons; impossible to maneuver the pointer with pinpoint accuracy

It keeps your hand in an unnatural straight vertical upright which is almost as bad as a traditional horizontal mouse for wrist strain. Plus it  moves in a weird, bulky manner without smooth motion. The wheel is in a stupid position that is cumbersome to use. NOT recommended.

reviews.title: Very comfortable to use

reviews.title: definitely recommend even if you aren't in pain like I was

reviews.title: Wireless Mouse, Matte Red by Verbatim
reviews.text: Needs 1 AA battery. Great for laptop, Chromebook and desktop users. 2.4 GHz wireless. 1200 DPI optical sensor. I'll let you know if it doesn't last a year but it looks and feels sturdy and well made.

reviews.title: good for Travel
reviews.text: I travel frequently and go through nice almost as frequently. This is an adequate mouse for travel. It is pretty much plug and play. while not the most comfortable, it is not uncomfortable. It is easy to operate. the scroll is not as smooth as some and there is not designated power button. It has an auto button which apparently moves the necessity.  It performs basic functions adequately. It is not the fanciest or the fastest but it travels well.

reviews.title: Gets the job done
reviews.text: I use this mouse with a Dell laptop. I close the laptop when I'm done with it, and the mouse goes to sleep when I close the computer. It wakes up when I open the computer, so I haven't had much trouble waking the mouse. This may be a problem in other situations.  It takes a AA battery, and occupies one of two USB ports on the laptop. There's a slot inside where you can put the USB connection when you're not using it. There's no power switch, so take out the battery if you don't want it to be drained.  I'm not crazy about the shape of this thing. The boxy shape doesn't fit naturally into my hand and it feels weird. I prefer a more traditional shape, but it's not like it's stopping me or anything. It's not hard to click or scroll and it doesn't make my hand tired. Overall, this gets the job done and doesn't look bad doing it. Four stars.

reviews.title: Works great for my pc, love Matte Red.
reviews.text: Love the matte red color, and it won’t get lost.  My son installed this for my Pc for me. I have small hands, long slim fingers, and this Verbatim feels comfortable to use. It does replace my older mouse which is just about the same size, but has always had a loose feeling to it, and Cost allot more then this one.  This mouse  moves on my desk with nothing under it, and is quite responsive. Can’t ask for more then that. 5 stars

reviews.title: Not at all Rugged
reviews.text: I was all prepared to say that this mouse was a ‘Great Value’ and to give it 4 Stars.  And then… it dropped off the couch.  Now my goto mouse has been dropped dozens of times and amazingly not suffered (it’s Logitec), but this mouse self-destructed.  The right button is now permanently pressed down and nothing I’ve done has freed it.  So essentially, it’s toast.  SUMMARY NOTES ================= —Everyone has different mouse requirements and mine and the other non-gamers in the house really only need a basic model.  —I had no problem using it with either PC or Mac.  Basically just popped in the dongle and it started working.  —This mouse has good motion detection.  —The wheel is stiff.  —As related above, it didn’t last long.  So if you never make mistakes and drop it, it might be a good value.  I’m going to stick with my slightly more expensive mouse.

reviews.title: The mouse I didn’t know I needed
reviews.text: This mouse is basically the same as the M720. Prior to this Logitech mouse I was using the Microsoft Surface mouse. When I bought the Microsoft mouse I was going for something super slim in profile and under $30. A few months later I bought this because I saw it on sale for under $30. I love the ergonomics on the mouse- something I didn’t realize I was missing out on with the Microsoft mouse. More impressive though was how easy this mouse makes it for me to shift between my work laptop, personal laptop, and desktop at home. Oh, and they're all different OSes too; Windows, Mac, and ChromeOS. The M720 has a great feature called Flow which lets you switch seamlessly between computers, regardless of OS. You just need to move the mouse to the edge of the screen like you would for a second monitor and the mouse pops over to your other computer, if they’re both on and set up. Great feature that…

reviews.title: Not a bad mouse, but doesn't work that well with multiple systems
reviews.text: The point of this mouse, along with a logitech keyboard is to allow you to operate 2 computers from one mouse and keyboard. I could not get both hooked up to both devices via bluetooth, so I have an RF dongle on one so it can run wirelessly and bluetooth on the other. The bluetooth just stops working, it shows paired but can't connect a few times a week. I use this mouse 8-10 hours a day 7 days a week, it drops connection requiring a system reboot 3-4 days per week. Never an issue on the RF so if you can set it up on that I think you will be ok.  Just below where your thumb goes there is another button that you will likely hit often if you have a big thumb which stops you from what you are doing until you select your screen again.  I haven't found anything else other than a Microsoft project to do this so if you need to operate 2 devices with one mouse you are likely stuck.

Although I love the feel and ergonomics of the design (I have medium sized lady hands), the hyper scroll takes zooming extents in AutoCad to crazy new and often times accidental levels. In fact the scroll wheel is so loose, that if you move the mouse around using only the buttons, the scroll wheel rocks back and forth by itself, zooming in or out without provocation in AutoCad. I haven't used it in any modeling programs, but I suspect this hyper scroll feature might cause some motion sickness in Rhino, or SketchUp. Architecture and engineer folk beware!

IT IS NOT WORTH the money.. total rip off.. and they keep deleting the 12% 1 star comments.. BEWARE!

reviews.title: Great Product! Hospital worthy!

reviews.title: Good solution for Carpal Tunnel
reviews.text: It takes a while to get used to this mouse, but it really helped what was starting to be very painful carpal tunnel.  I used to get numbness and tingling, then pain all the way up to my shoulder.  the pain in my forearm was sometimes really unbearable.  I switched to this mouse at work and haven't had the problem since.  It's not my preferred mouse for detail work, but I'm used to it now and it's okay.  I wish the buttons were more quiet.  they make very loud click noises when pressed and I prefer silent click

reviews.title: Five Stars

reviews.title: Fits weird

reviews.title: Works amazing! Take out the weight they add in the bottom!
reviews.text: I never have ANY wrist pain! I'm on my computer 14+ hours a day for school and work, and I was getting the worst pains ever! I found this and haven't had any pain since! Takes a little getting used to and you should immediately removed the weight they put in the bottom (which is super easy to take out), and voilà, not too heavy and release of all pain!

reviews.title: Mouse is working great with my MacBook Pro
reviews.text: Mouse is working great with my MacBook Pro. It's a little light/cheap feeling, but that's not a big deal to me.

reviews.title: Bad construction.
reviews.text: The sticker that is stuck to the base of the mouse started peeling. Everytime I moved the mouse, the peeling sticker was rubbing against the mouse bad making for a horrible experience.  I like the weights to control the weight of the mouse.

reviews.title: Five Stars
reviews.text: I absolutely love these mice.  I've got several now for each of my workstations at home and work.

reviews.title: Close, but no Anker.
reviews.text: My company bought this mouse for me, but I still wanted to review it here. Here's what's up: I have a large women's hand at 8" around the knuckles. I usually wear a Medium men's glove or Large/XL women's, so compare from there.  I have a wired Anker vertical mouse at home. I wanted a wireless Anker mouse for work, would have gone with the wired version... but the website the company uses does not offer Anker. This is the most similar design offered, so that's what I ordered and here it is.  The box came with the USB chip and the mouse and a set of batteries. No instructions required. Put batteries in mouse, switch to "on" (on the underside), plug in the USB and do mousey things. Turn it off when you go home from work for the night, and the batteries will last much longer. I haven't done a glass test - honestly I have no idea why people are so bothered by whether a mouse will …

reviews.title: Just OK
reviews.text: Lasted only 5 months.  Ugh!  Then again, all of the mini's I've purchased seem to work for only a few months, then they die.

reviews.title: Better after you add some grip
reviews.text: I purchased this from another retailer, but I wanted to write a review.  I do like this mouse.  It's very comfortable and feels natural after a very short adjustment period.  One thing I did do was add a bit of grip to the mouse.  Out of the box, it is very slick and shiny.  For me, it felt a bit slippery.  I added a few strips of athletic tape for where my thumb goes and also on the mouse buttons.  It feels a lot better now.  I think I'll get some grip tape eventually, but this was a quick and easy fix.  Good purchase though.

reviews.title: Reliable, comfortable, solid (feel and construction).
reviews.text: Have been using this for over 3 weeks now and I really like it. At first it's ergonomics were a little weird, angled wrong I thought. But after an 8 hour day i noticed that I have less strain. All the functions work very very well.

reviews.title: It's relatively comfortable and the scroll wheel functions well
reviews.text: For the price it's alright. It's relatively comfortable and the scroll wheel functions well.  But the thing about vertical mouses/mice is that the force from your finger used to click doesn't go into the table, it goes into your thumb. You would think because it requires so little force to push the button this shouldn't be a problem, but it is noticeably difficult to maintain the mouse in its current position.  Do not buy this mouse if you play video games or frequently use photoshop. Really anything that requires high mouse accuracy.  I'd suggest spending a couple more dollars on a nicer one. I have gotten sort of used to it, but I switch back to my lateral mouse often.  If the buttons were easier to press this would be a 5 star mouse (depending on how long it lasts).

reviews.title: Works great and battery really lasts.

It is very accurate and holds up well when I toss it in my travel bag.  This works much better than any of the wireless mice I have used before and much better than I expected at this price.

reviews.title: It's a mouse, it works.
reviews.text: When purchasing a bluetooth mouse, or any bluetooth device, an important factor is how well it connects and how well it STAYS connected.  After all this time, the industry still can’t make up its mind about how bluetooth works: - Microsoft with their mouse and Sony with their controller that pair without the need of a code (which Android’s bluetooth stack doesn’t support). - Mice and keyboards that will not reconnect after it wakes from sleep mode. - To this day, bluetooth devices still can’t wake a computer from suspend state. So when I get a simple bluetooth mouse for a good price, and it actually works as expected, I was happy.  For my review, I’m comparing the Bornd mouse to the [[ASIN:B006428K7I Motorola 89519N Bluetooth Mouse]] which I got in a set that included the [[ASIN:B004L9MBH6 Motorola Wireless Keyboard for Motorola ATRIX and XOOM (Motorola Retail Packaging)]].  With the Mot…

reviews.title: almost perfect-recommended
reviews.text: The packaging was damaged and that deterred me. But when I used the mouse I found that it worked really easily with my iMac and Apple devices. Unfortunately, when I connected it (very easily) to my Kindle, it lagged. It went from super fast (as fast as my Magic Mouse) to slow as hell.  It's not a gorgeous mouse. It's very basic. It has a nice scroll wheel. It can be used with iDevices and computers. And the price is VERY right. I was looking for a travel mouse and this was truly almost perfect.  Despite the damage to the packaging, I don't think that mine was defective since it worked perfectly with my Apple devices, just not my Kindle devices.

reviews.title: Good Blue Tooth Mouse
reviews.text: Well built mouse.  Made for small hands so not sure how a larger hands person would do with it - but it is just right for use with a notepad.  One problem though - it eats batteries.  It runs off of a single double A battery and has power saving features but seems to deplete batteries every other week.  Would give it five stars if it wasn't for the battery situation.

reviews.title: So far so good
reviews.text: It seems well made. I've read the good and the bad and at least out of the box it works. I got this for my 8 year old to use with his tablet. If it last a year great. It works and it is a cool shade of blue which is his favorite color. This along with the Tagus keyboard I got him makes his tablet do about everything. I gave him a pair of my Bluetooth headphones so now he does it almost silently. Win win...

It is a nice compliment to the available on-screen gesture controls of the computer, especially for a die-hard convert from Windows XP and Windows 7 operating systems.

reviews.title: Decent mouse with a huge flaw
reviews.text: I'm on a quest to find the perfect wireless notebook mouse.  As of yet, I have not found one that is a good every-day mouse and yet portable.  The biggest flaw to this mouse is it's receiver.  The snap on feature works fine, but ads bulk to the bottom of the mouse.  The biggest problem is that it breaks easily.  I've broken 2 of the receivers, now, both times they were attached to the computer and broke when lightly bumped.  Not dropped or slammed against a doorway, but when moving it on my desk and it catches on something and bends or cracks where the USB port meets the receiver.  Pros:  Easy to install  All features work  Mouse itself is durable  Long battery life  Good mouse range  Cons:  Weak receiver construction  Feel in hand (subjective, I know)  Receiver not integrated well into base

reviews.title: Wrist Pain No more

It's definitely odd at first but it is easy to adapt to  and has 100% reduced pain in my arm.

reviews.title: Pretty good

It does have a tendency to skip around if the battery starts to get low of if it's not really close to my laptop. It does work, it fits nicely in my hand and it feels sturdy. reviews.title: Solid mouse, but don't get your hopes up over the extra features
reviews.text: I had no difficulty with the basic set up for my new mouse. Basic plug and play kind of thing. That said, there is sadly no clear way to program some of the extras on the mouse. The website isn't terribly helpful and has no downloads for drivers or just-in-case-you-couldn't-figure-it-out instructions on how to program the extra buttons. A bit disappointing, since I'd welcome making use of them, but otherwise I can't find any problems with the job it's doing.

reviews.title: ** Use tips ** Nice mouse....
reviews.text: Nice mouse.... slightly large, and I have large hands.  If you have small hands, I would purchase a size down.  It is simple to set up, works well (so far), and I like the wireless feature.  Tips:  My other mouse had a place to store the USB unit.  This one also has a storage slot, which makes it convenient.  Otherwise, you can leave the USB connector in the laptop (If it fits in your case with the device inserted...)  Be sure to turn off the device when not in use to conserve your batteries. (Sliding switch on bottom)  This mouse is Windows compatible.  I run Windows 7.... works fine.  If you have a trackpad that drives you crazy, these devices are great!  Enjoy!

reviews.text: It works ok, but if you like to hear the click of a mouse, steer clear of this one.  It’s hard to tell if it has actually “clicked” where you want it to do it has a little bit of a learning curve.

reviews.title: Neat low profile mouse, works well! USB thing is a little too snug though...
reviews.text: I'm using this with the Acer Vero laptop and it works perfectly. The track wheel works pretty well but it's kind of like driving an old truck with very loose-feeling steering. It works, it just spins fairly freely so it feels strange at first. I like it though! The optical on this works well, I'm using my laptop's sleeve as a mouse pad and it works great!  Taking away one star because the usb dongle on this has WAY too tight of a fit! I can't even get it into one of the laptop's usb ports and it's a matching branded Acer Vero laptop, same color and everything! But I put it in a port on the left side and had to nudge it in a bit harder than anything else and it went in. I tested it in various other usb ports around my house and in ALL of them it's a very snug fit and in some, it's hard to push it in. The dongle itself isn't bent or anything so the only thing I can think of is poor design.…

reviews.title: Cute Looking!
reviews.text: This is a cute mouse. It's small and feels streamlined. I appreciate that it's made from recycled material. It immediately linked to my Chromebook. The only thing I don't love is that it doesn't make the satisfying clicking sound or feel when you click on things. That's going to take some getting used to, for sure! Other than that, it is working just fine.
